title: Oakdale Road and Eddystone Avenue - Traffic Control Signals
brief: City Council will vote on installing traffic lights at Oakdale Road and Eddystone Avenue, replacing the existing all-way stop.

title: 245-251 Marlee Avenue, 1-7 Romar Crescent and 16 Stayner Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
brief: Two buildings (37 and 35 storeys, 886 homes) are proposed at 245-251 Marlee Avenue and nearby addresses. The applicant appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal, and North York Community Council is asked to have the City Solicitor oppose the appeal.

title: 1099 Broadview Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City Council will vote on zoning changes to allow two 14- and 16-storey towers at 1099 Broadview Avenue, with 313 homes, shops and a rear courtyard.

title: 32 - 50 Forest Manor Road, North York - Assumption of Services, Registered Plan 66M-2515
brief: A technical item: City Council is asked to formally take over the roads and underground services in the Forest Manor Road subdivision from the developer. The city would then maintain them.

title: 5318 - 5324 Yonge Street and 11 Churchill Avenue - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Staff recommend approving the demolition of 17 rental homes at 11 Churchill Avenue, to be replaced in the new development with a tenant assistance plan. City Council is asked to approve. The item also references $20,000.00.

title: 1 Front Street West - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property in the Union Station Heritage Conservation District Under Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Amend a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties
brief: City Council will vote on changes to the heritage Dominion Public Building at 1 Front Street West, lowering 14 north-side openings for new shops, with an updated heritage protection deal.

title: 543 Yonge Street - Demolition of a Building within the Historic Yonge Street Heritage Conservation District and Approval of a Replacement Building
topics: heritage conservation districts, heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties
brief: City Council will vote on tearing down a four-storey building at 543 Yonge Street, in the heritage Yonge Street area, and replacing it with a 68-storey building with stores and homes.

title: 1266 Queen Street West - Demolition and New Construction on a Designated Heritage Property under Part V, Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Approval
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties
brief: City Council will vote on tearing down a non-heritage building at 1266 Queen Street West, in the Parkdale heritage area, and replacing it with a 27-storey building with homes and shops.

title: 530-550 Yonge Street, 6-8 Breadalbane Street and 145 St. Luke Lane - Alterations, Demolition and New Construction of Buildings on a Designated Heritage Property under Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: construction, demolitions, heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties
brief: City Council will vote on changes to the heritage buildings at 530-550 Yonge Street, keeping key facades within a 67-storey building, with a heritage easement agreement to protect them.

title: 1125 Sheppard Avenue East (Block 2) - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Refusal
brief: Staff recommend refusing a 52- and 48-storey, 1,238-home development at 1125 Sheppard Avenue East (Block 2). Council is asked to refuse it, keeping the site's current rules.

title: 170 Merton Street - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties
brief: City Council will vote on changes to the 1969 former Visiting Homemakers Association building at 170 Merton Street, keeping part of it within a 45-storey redevelopment, with a heritage easement agreement.

title: 1291-1311 Gerrard Street East and 243-247 Greenwood Avenue - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City Council will vote on tearing down 29 rental homes at 1291-1311 Gerrard Street East and 243-247 Greenwood Avenue, on condition the owner builds 29 replacement rental units and helps current tenants. If the owner fails to finish the new building on time, a $20,000.00 charge per unit would be added to the property tax bill.

title: On-Street Electric Vehicle Charging Stations - Parking Amendments (Non-Delegated Locations)
brief: City Council will vote on creating two on-street electric car charging areas, with four charging stations, on Lansdowne Avenue and Pape Avenue, plus technical fixes to existing EV charging rules on Carlton Street, Dovercourt Road and Queen Street East.

title: 16 Wilby Crescent - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: development, multi-unit dwellings, rezoning, zoning bylaws
land development, multi residential apartment buildings
brief: City Council will vote on a 39-storey, 436-home residential tower at 16 Wilby Crescent.

title: Weston Road and Kenhar Drive - Traffic Control Signal
brief: City Council will vote on installing a traffic signal at Weston Road and Kenhar Drive, including a protected crossing at a key TTC bus stop.

title: 80 Mill Street - Installation of an Accessible Loading Zone
brief: The item proposes the 15-minute parking zone outside 80 Mill Street turned into an accessible loading zone, so Wheel-Trans riders and accessibility permit holders can board safely.

title: Harbour Street (200 Queens Quay West) - Construction Staging Area
brief: City Council will vote on closing the Waterfront Trail and a curb lane on Harbour Street, December 2025 to July 2030, for a 59-storey condo building at 200 Queens Quay West.

title: 980 Dufferin Street and 1141 Bloor Street West - TTC Tunnel Construction (Stage1) -Construction Staging Area Time Extension
brief: City Council will vote on extending road closures around Bloor Street West and Dufferin Street, February 2026 to February 2027, for the tunnel linking Dufferin station to a new 33-storey building.

title: 3755 Bloor Street West - Construction Staging Area Time Extension
brief: City Council will decide whether to extend the construction staging area on Kipling Avenue for the new Etobicoke Civic Centre, after forestry and hydro delays stalled the approved schedule.

title: Metrolinx’s Scarborough Subway Extension - Fourth Quarter 2025 Semi-Annual Update
brief: This is a routine item: council hears a progress update on building the Scarborough Subway Extension, with the next update due by fall 2026. Nothing is decided.

title: Multi-Tenant Houses Regulatory Framework: Implementation Update
topics: affordable housing, implementation, multi-residential properties, multi-unit dwellings, policy development
housing projects, multi residential apartment buildings
brief: Council votes on updating the multi-tenant (rooming) house rules, changing definitions in the licensing by-law. These are among the most affordable homes in the city.

title: 1673-1675 Bathurst Street - Rental Housing Conversion Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City Council will vote on turning an eight-unit rental building at 1673-1675 Bathurst Street into condos. All units rent above the city's mid-range rents, and conditions would protect current tenants.

title: 6175 to 6183 Kingston Road, 1, 2, 4, 7, 10 and 11 Franklin Avenue (Lots 8 and 9) - Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Two lots at 6175-6183 Kingston Road would be exempted from lot-splitting rules to become four lots for two semi-detached homes. Each home would get its own title; no design changes are proposed.

title: 149 College Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City Council will vote on zoning changes to allow a 60-storey building at 149 College Street, with 620 student residence units, 225 homes and institutional space, integrating the heritage building on the site.

title: 38-50 Park Road - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Refusal
brief: City staff want City Council to refuse a 31-storey, 289-home building at 38-50 Park Road, saying it does not fit the low-rise Rosedale Valley area, and to have city lawyers defend the refusal if the builder appeals.

title: 59-81 Lawton Boulevard - Zoning By-law Amendment - Appeal Report
topics: apartment neighbourhoods, planning & development (sc), zoning bylaws
brief: City Council will vote on directing the city lawyer to oppose, at a provincial tribunal, a developer's appeal for 38- and 43-storey, 706-home buildings at 59-81 Lawton Boulevard, while talks continue.

title: 630-646 Spadina Avenue and 67 Harbord Street - Official Plan Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City Council will vote on changing the growth plan to redesignate part of 630 Spadina Avenue from Neighbourhoods to Mixed Use Areas. The application proposes no new building; existing buildings would stay.

title: 6175 to 6183 Kingston Road, 1, 2, 4, 7, 10 and 11 Franklin Avenue (Blocks 11 and 12) - Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report
brief: Blocks 11 and 12 at 6175-6183 Kingston Road would be exempted from lot-splitting rules so 32 lots can be created for 16 semi-detached and townhouse homes. Each home would get its own title; no design changes are proposed.
stake: Ward 25 is named in the record.

title: Elm Street Streetscape Vision - Final Report
brief: City Council will vote on adopting a pedestrian-friendly design plan for Elm Street between Yonge and Bay Streets, to guide how building applications on the street are judged.

title: 170 and 180 Merton Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: demolitions, heritage designation, planning & development (sc), zoning bylaws
brief: City Council will vote on zoning changes to allow a 45-storey building with 531 homes and shops at 170 and 180 Merton Street, with shops instead of replacement offices.

title: 138 Dowling Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City Council will vote on zoning changes to allow a 16-storey, 145-home apartment building at 138 Dowling Avenue.

title: 354-358 Pape Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: building permits, planning & development (sc), zoning bylaws
brief: City Council will vote on zoning changes to allow a 10-storey building with 41 homes, ground-floor stores and second-floor offices at 354-358 Pape Avenue.

title: 543-555 Yonge Street -Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City Council will vote on zoning changes to allow a 68-storey building with 679 homes at 543-555 Yonge Street, built over and behind the kept building at 555 Yonge Street.

title: 530-550 Yonge Street, 145 St. Luke Lane and 6-8 Breadalbane Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: planning & development (sc), residential properties, zoning bylaws
brief: City Council will vote on zoning changes to allow a 67-storey building with 822 homes at 530-550 Yonge Street, with a public open space facing Dr. Lillian McGregor Park. One rental home would be torn down, with help for the tenant.

title: Accessible Parking Space - Davenport Road (Non-Delegated)
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, accessibility, parking spaces
brief: City Council will vote on creating a new accessible parking space on south Davenport Road near Dufferin Street, and removing a nearby one to fix signs that do not match the rules.

title: 1-13 St. Clair Avenue West - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Refusal
brief: City staff want City Council to refuse a 49-storey, 340-home tower at 1-13 St. Clair Avenue West, saying the plan does not show how it fits beside the heritage office building, and to defend the refusal if appealed.

title: 1291-1311 Gerrard Street East and 243-247 Greenwood Avenue - Zoning By-law Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City Council will vote on zoning changes to allow a 12-storey building with 278 homes and shops at 1291-1311 Gerrard Street East and 243-247 Greenwood Avenue, including 29 replacement and 6 new affordable rentals.

title: 1012, 1014, 1016 and 1018 Gerrard Street East - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City Council will vote on zoning changes to allow a 14-storey building with 112 homes and shops at 1012-1018 Gerrard Street East, with underground parking.

title: Assumption of Services, Registered Plan 66M-2549, 743 Warden Avenue, Zahavish Downtown Developments Ltd
brief: The city would take over the roads and underground pipes built for the subdivision at 743 Warden Avenue under a 2017 deal with the builder. The city's guarantee would be released; council is asked to approve.

title: 1 Front Street West  - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City Council will vote on changes to the approved project at 1 Front Street West: more homes and fewer offices in the west tower, with changes to the heritage Dominion Public Building. The report also lists an amount of $300,000.

title: 149 College Street - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties
brief: City Council will vote on changes to the heritage Stewart Building at 149 College Street, integrating its kept facades into a 60-storey tower, plus a deal to protect the building.

title: 1673 and 1675 Bathurst Street - Plan of Condominium Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City Council will vote on the draft condo plan for 1673 and 1675 Bathurst Street, allowing the eight-unit apartment building to become condos, with conditions.

title: 6 Dawes Road - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City Council will vote on zoning changes to allow a taller 39-storey rental building at 6 Dawes Road, up from 17 storeys, with 452 rental homes including three affordable units.

title: 333 College Street and 303 Augusta Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: land use, planning & development (sc), zoning bylaws
brief: City Council will vote on zoning changes to allow a 20-storey building with 638 student residence units at 333 College Street and the rear of 303 Augusta Avenue, with ground-floor non-residential space.

title: 2451-2495 Danforth Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: building permits, planning & development (sc), zoning bylaws
brief: City Council will vote on zoning changes to allow two 13- and 29-storey buildings with 620 homes at 2451-2495 Danforth Avenue, with a grocery store, shops and public open space.

title: Use of Nathan Phillips Square for Team Canada FanFest - February 6-8, 2026
brief: City Council will vote on letting the Canadian Olympic Committee serve beer and wine at Nathan Phillips Square for the Team Canada FanFest, February 6 to 8, 2026, pending provincial and health approvals.

title: Bloor West Village Avenue Study - Urban Design Guidelines - Final Report
topics: heritage properties, planning & development (sc), urban design
brief: City Council will vote on adopting Bloor West Village design guidelines to guide building applications along Bloor Street West, and on marking certain properties as having heritage value.

title: King Street East - Passenger Loading Zone
brief: City Council will vote on replacing the taxi stand on King Street East, east of Ontario Street, with a passenger loading zone, better suited to shuttle buses for nearby venues.

title: Bloor Annex Business Improvement Area Minor Boundary Expansion
brief: Council would grow the Bloor Annex business area slightly to include Seaton Park, just north of Bloor Street West on Albany Street.

title: 257-259 and 291 Lake Shore Boulevard East, 2 Small Street and 200 Queens Quay East (Quayside Blocks 1 and 2) - Zoning By-law Amendment and Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: part lot control, zoning, zoning designations
brief: City Council will vote on zoning changes for the Quayside waterfront project, allowing four towers of 50 to 66 storeys with about 2,850 homes, including 553 affordable rentals. The report also lists amounts of $538 and $1076.

title: Transit Priority Measures to Support the 505 Dundas 6-Minute Network
topics: parking regulations, public transit, transportation schedules
brief: City Council will vote on parking and traffic changes so 505 Dundas streetcars can run every six minutes from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. daily. The six-minute service starts in November 2025, with the street changes in January 2026.

title: Creating More Accessible and Disability Inclusive Events
brief: Staff would write a plain-language accessibility guide for event organizers, with standards and checklists so events at city buildings work for people with disabilities.
stake: About accessibility. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 19 in favour, none against.

title: 241-243 Finch Avenue East - Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Staff recommend freeing 241-243 Finch Avenue East from a rule that blocks lots from being split, so eight townhouses can be sold as separate lots. City Council is asked to approve.

title: 6-8 and 10-12 Sumach Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: Council votes on starting heritage protection for two pairs of Victorian houses at 6-8 and 10-12 Sumach Street, built 1886-1888.

title: 39 Wynford Drive - Inclusion on the City of Toronto's Heritage Register
brief: Council votes on adding the 1962 office building at 39 Wynford Drive in Flemingdon Park to the city's Heritage Register. Listing is a first step toward heritage protection. A demolition request for the site was filed in 2025. City staff will study full heritage designation and report back by July 2026.

title: 262-264 St. George Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: Council votes on starting heritage protection for two 1893 houses at 262-264 St. George Street in the Annex.

title: 241 Yonge Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: Council votes on starting heritage protection for the 1911 building at 241 Yonge Street, built for the Art Metropole artist supply company.

title: 544-552 Eglinton Avenue East  and 12-14 Bruce Park Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Refusal
brief: Staff recommend refusing a 25-storey, 256-home building at 544-552 Eglinton Avenue East and 12-14 Bruce Park Avenue. Council is asked to refuse it, keeping the site's current rules.

title: Advancing Reconciliation and Equity via Community Funding
brief: Council would approve a new funding approach for community service partnerships and let staff hand out funding through the end of 2030, with yearly reporting. The program's 2025 budget is $32.197 million.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $1.95 million.

title: Establishing a Toronto Community Crisis Service Training Centre to Strengthen Toronto’s Fourth Emergency Service
brief: Council would approve a lease with Family Service Toronto for a crisis-response training centre at 355 Church Street, with a $2.5 million figure attached to the project. It would train the city's non-police mental health crisis team.

title: Reducing Barriers to Youth Employment
brief: Staff give an overview of city youth jobs programs, noting Toronto's 19.7 percent youth unemployment rate. The committee just receives the report.

title: 2135 Sheppard Avenue East, 325, Yorkland Boulevard, 125 Consumers Road, 15 Smooth Rose Court, and 55 Smooth Rose Court - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Staff recommend approving a taller building at 2135 Sheppard Avenue East and nearby addresses: Building A would go from 35 to 43 storeys with more homes. City Council is asked to approve. The developer would pay $350,000 toward the nearby Toronto Public Library branch.
stake: Ward 17 is named in the record.

title: Call to Order
brief: This is a routine item: the meeting opens with the call to order, O Canada, and a moment of silence. No decision is asked for.

title: Introduction of Committee Reports and New Business from City Officials
brief: This is a routine item: committee leaders and city staff introduce reports and new business. Council only hears them now; no decision is asked for.

title: Petitions
brief: This is a routine item: councillors may hand in petitions from residents to be recorded. No decision is asked for.
stake: A citywide decision. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Review of the Order Paper
brief: This is a routine item: council looks over the order paper, the list of topics for this meeting. No decision is asked for.
stake: A citywide decision. Decided by a recorded vote, 10 in favour and 13 against — every member's position is public.

title: Tenancy Update with Beech Hall Housing Co-operative and Alexandra Park Housing Co-operative
brief: Council votes on extending the lease deals with the Beech Hall and Alexandra Park housing co-operatives by up to two years while new deals are negotiated.

title: Community Improvement Plan Amendment for the Economic Development and Growth in Employment (EDGE) Incentive Program to Increase Tax Increment Equivalent Grants and Annual Program Update Report
topics: community improvement plans, subsidies and grants
brief: Council votes on temporarily boosting a tax-break program for business investment, amid U.S. tariffs. Eligible applicants by end of 2027 would get grants equal to 100 percent of the municipal tax increase over five years. The program's annual cap stays at $20 million.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $20 million.

title: Assumption of Services, Registered Plan 66M-2568, 50 Humberwood Boulevard, Humberwood Holding Corporation and Hullmark Developments Limited
brief: This is procedural: City Council will vote on taking over the municipal services in the 50 Humberwood Boulevard subdivision.

title: Permanent Closure of a Portion of the Public Laneway at 66-66Y Third Street
brief: Council votes on permanently closing part of the public laneway at 66-66Y Third Street, which runs through a parking lot. The laneway to the north is unaffected.
stake: About laneways. Decided by a recorded vote, 21 in favour and 4 against — every member's position is public.

title: Progress Update on the Implementation of the Reconciliation Action Plan
topics: First Nations, activities in community and life, implementation
brief: Staff would engage Indigenous communities on the next Reconciliation Action Plan by mid-2027, and council would approve a one-time $350,000 for the Toronto Aboriginal Support Services Centre.

title: 4050 Chesswood Drive - Designation of a Portion of the Property Used by North York Harvest Food Bank Toronto as a Municipal Capital Facility
brief: Council would make part of 4050 Chesswood Drive, leased to the North York Harvest Food Bank, tax-exempt as a city capital facility. About 31,830 square feet plus parking would be exempt from city and school taxes. The waived taxes are worth about $43,234 a year.
stake: About food banks. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 20 in favour, none against.

title: O'Connor Drive - Mid-Block Pedestrian Traffic Control Signal - at a point 145 metres North of Sunrise Avenue
brief: A pedestrian traffic signal is proposed on O'Connor Drive, 145 metres north of Sunrise Avenue. City Council approval is needed because the TTC runs transit there.

title: Mount Dennis Community For All Action Plan
brief: Council would adopt the Mount Dennis Community for All Action Plan, a ten-year plan responding to new development and transit there, and set up a city working group to carry it out. The report includes a $50,000 figure tied to the plan.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $50,000.

title: Confirmation of Minutes
brief: This is a routine item: council checks the written record of its November 12 and 13, 2025, meeting and confirms it is correct. No new decision is asked for.

title: Declarations of Interest
brief: This is a routine item: councillors say if they have a personal interest in any item, as the conflict-of-interest law requires. No decision is asked for.
stake: A citywide decision. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Presentations, Introductions and Announcements
brief: This is a routine item: the meeting includes presentations, introductions, and announcements. Council only listens; no decision is asked for.
stake: A citywide decision. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Municipal Code Chapter 608, Parks - Update
brief: Council would approve 25 updates to the Parks rules, including new definitions for drones, gliders, and harassment. The changes affect activities across all city parkland.

title: 1 Herons Hill Way - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: applications, official plan amendments, zoning bylaws
brief: Staff recommend approving a 34-storey, 343-home building at 1 Herons Hill Way, keeping the existing two-storey office building. City Council is asked to approve the planning changes.

title: 36-40 Avondale Avenue - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Appeal
topics: official plan amendments, residential properties, zoning bylaws
brief: Staff recommend refusing a 49-storey, 504-home building at 36-40 Avondale Avenue. Council is asked to refuse it, keeping current rules; staff would defend the refusal if appealed.

title: 71 Talara Drive - Official Plan Amendment, Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: applications, official plan amendments, zoning bylaws
brief: Staff recommend approving a 36-storey, 385-home building at 71 Talara Drive, with 29 rental replacement units. City Council is asked to approve. The item also references $600,000.00 and $2,850,000.00.

title: Update on the Working Group to Advance the Widening of Steeles Avenue East Between Ninth Line and Beare Road to Support Regional Growth
topics: advisory committees, road reconstruction, road transportation
brief: Council will get an update on the working group for widening Steeles Avenue East between Ninth Line and Beare Road to support growth.

title: Proposed Parking Signage Pilot
brief: Approval of an 18-month test of four new parking sign designs with bigger text and plainer language to cut confusion and tickets, with staff reporting the results is before council.

title: Federation of Municipalities (FCM) October 2025 Advocacy Days
brief: This is a report for information only: Councillor Paul Ainslie reports back on Toronto's participation in the Federation of Canadian Municipalities' October 2025 advocacy days on Parliament Hill. The report cites figures of $2, $8, $1 and $15. No decision is needed.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $270.

title: Association of Municipalities of Ontario’s (AMO) Annual General Meeting August 16 - 20, 2025
brief: This is a report for information only: Councillor Paul Ainslie reports back on attending the 2025 annual meeting of the Association of Municipalities of Ontario. The province announced $1.6 billion for the Municipal Housing Infrastructure Program. The report also cites a $5 billion figure. No decision is needed.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $1.6 billion.

title: Enabling Construction at Parkdale Hub - West Block
brief: Council votes on approving up to $17,724,000 for the Neighbourhood Land Trust to build the community space at Parkdale Hub's West Block.

title: 45 to 47 Sheppard Avenue East - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Staff recommend approving four towers (30 to 59 storeys, 2,377 homes) at 45-47 Sheppard Avenue East, with shops, underground parking and a new park. City Council is asked to approve the planning changes.

title: Housing Action Plan: Avenues Policy Review Phase Two: Initial Study of Wards 9 and 11
brief: Council votes on Official Plan changes for lands along Avenues in Wards 9 and 11, allowing mid-rise housing.
stake: About avenue study. Decided by a recorded vote, 22 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: FIFA Traffic Management
brief: The item asks City staff how the 2026 FIFA World Cup is expected to affect traffic and how the City is getting ready.
stake: About road closures. Decided by a recorded vote, 13 in favour and 10 against — every member's position is public.

title: City of Toronto / Ministry of Transportation of Ontario Agreement for the Maintenance and Operation of Ministry Owned Traffic Control Devices
brief: Staff could sign a new deal with Ontario's transportation ministry spelling out who handles traffic signals, signs, and road markings on highway ramps, if council agrees.

title: Expanding the Diversity Youth Fellowship Program
topics: community & life (sc), persons with a disability, youth, youth programs
brief: Staff would study a part-time fellowship for youth with disabilities, like the existing Indigenous, Black, and Muslim youth fellowships, and report back by spring 2026.
stake: About community & life (sc). Its recorded vote was unanimous — 19 in favour, none against.

title: Authority to Accept In-kind Archival Donation to Toronto Archives
brief: Council would accept a gift of old architecture materials from George Robb Architect, valued at $65,632, for the Toronto Archives. Council approval is needed because the gift is over the $50,000 staff limit.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $65,632.

title: Metrolinx’s Ontario Line Construction within the North York District - Fourth Quarter 2025 Update
brief: A routine update: staff report on Metrolinx's Ontario Line construction and transit-oriented projects in North York for the fourth quarter of 2025. North York Community Council is asked to receive it; no decision is needed.

title: 2925 Keele Street (Stanley Greene Block G) Subdivision - Assumption of Services, Registered Plan 66M-2520
topics: agreements, assumption of services, municipal services
brief: A technical item: City Council is asked to formally take over the roads and underground services in the Stanley Greene Block G subdivision from the developer. The city would then maintain them.

title: Accepting a Donation and Entering into Agreements with the Chinese Cultural Centre of Greater Toronto for an Asian Garden Project at Cynthia Lai Park
brief: A donation of up to $15.0 million from the Chinese Cultural Centre of Greater Toronto to build an Asian Garden at Cynthia Lai Park, at no cost to the City would be accepted, if council agrees.
stake: About donation. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 22 in favour, none against.

title: Ontario’s Big City Mayors Caucus Meeting Update to Council - Thunder Bay, October 17, 2025
brief: This is a report for information only: Councillor Paul Ainslie reports back on attending the Ontario's Big City Mayors meeting in Thunder Bay on Oct. 17, 2025, on the Mayor's behalf. No decision is needed.

title: Amendments to the Administrative Penalty Tribunal Composition
brief: Council would create a Vice-Chair role on the Administrative Penalty Tribunal, the body that hears challenges to city fines, chosen by tribunal members, to keep hearings running when the Chair is absent. The report cites a $6,250 figure.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $6,250.

title: 847-855 Kingston Road - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions ahead of an April 2026 hearing on the tribunal appeal for an 11-storey building at 847-855 Kingston Road. The legal strategy is confidential.
stake: About planning & development (sc). Decided by a recorded vote, 17 in favour and 6 against — every member's position is public.

title: Reimbursing Certain Reasonable Legal Expenses of Shelter Consultants - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
brief: The City Solicitor would keep opposing court challenges to new housing and shelter projects, and named shelter consultants would be reimbursed up to $50,000 each for legal costs not covered by insurance, if council agrees.
stake: About homelessness. Decided by a recorded vote, 18 in favour and 3 against — every member's position is public.

title: 550 Broadview Avenue - Designation of a Portion of the Property Used by East End Arts Toronto as a Municipal Capital Facility
topics: arts and culture, municipal facilities, properties (real estate), taxes
brief: City Council will vote on a tax exemption for the East End Arts community centre space at 550 Broadview Avenue.

title: 160 Eglinton Avenue East - Designation of a Portion of the Property used by Central Eglinton Community Centre as a Municipal Capital Facility
topics: community centres, municipal facilities, properties (real estate), taxes
brief: City Council will vote on a tax exemption for the Central Eglinton Community Centre space at 160 Eglinton Avenue East.

title: Councillors' Constituency Offices - Designation of Portions of Properties used as Municipal Capital Facilities
topics: councillors, municipal facilities, properties (real estate), taxes
brief: City Council will vote on tax exemptions for two councillor constituency offices at 622 College Street and 215 Morrish Road.

title: Licence Extension and Amending Agreement for Air Quality Monitoring Station at Metro Hall, 55 John Street
topics: air quality, city-owned properties, heating, ventilation and air conditioning systems, licences
brief: City Council will vote on a five-year extension for the province's air quality monitoring station at Metro Hall.

title: Mayors and Regional Chairs of Ontario (MARCO) update to City Council
brief: This is a report for information only: Councillor Paul Ainslie reports back on attending the meeting of the Mayors and Regional Chairs of Ontario (MARCO) on the Mayor's behalf. No decision is needed.

title: Expropriation of Property Interests near Summerhill Station for the Secondary Exit Project - Stage 2
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, expropriations, properties (real estate), subway stations
brief: City Council will vote on stage two of expropriating easements near Summerhill Station for the TTC second exit project.

title: Amendment to Non-Competitive Blanket Contract 47025889 with EnergyCAP Inc., for Utility Invoice Processing Services
topics: accounts payable, computer programs, power utilties
brief: City Council will vote on adding $60,000 ($61,056 net of HST recoveries) to the EnergyCAP utility billing contract, stated as rising from $1,057,297 ($1,075,905 net of HST recoveries) to $1,763,464 ($1,794,501 net of HST recoveries); source documents also list $300 million and $2.5 million.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $60,000.

title: George Weston Recital Hall Renovations at the Meridian Arts Centre
topics: performing arts facilities, building, tenancy agreements
brief: City Council will vote on procurement authority for the donation-funded George Weston Recital Hall renovations; source documents list $500,000, plus $500,000, as a figure with a trailing comma.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $500,000.

title: Weston Loop Master Plan
brief: A councillor wants Council to adopt the Weston Loop Master Plan, a community vision for 74 acres of connected parkland across five parks along the Humber River in Weston, built over 25 years.

title: Kingston Road - Pay-and-Display Parking
brief: Staff suggest adding pay-and-display parking on the south side of Kingston Road between Birchmount Road and Cliffside Drive, changing existing bans to fit, at a $3.00 rate. This needs a City Council vote.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Cornerstone OnDemand Inc., for the City's Enterprise Talent Management System and Online Learning
topics: contracts, purchasing, science & technology (sc), workplace training and development
brief: City Council will vote on a $4,796,753 ($4,881,176 net of HST recoveries) non-competitive Cornerstone talent management contract for 2027-2029; source documents also list $500,000.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $4,796,753.

title: Cycling Network Plan - 2025 Cycling Infrastructure Fourth Quarter Update
topics: bike lanes, bike paths, bikeway networks, cycling
brief: Approval of 20.5 kilometres of new bike lanes and trails at several spots, including Keele Street, Kingston Road, Kipling Avenue, and Albion Road, is before council. No car lanes would be removed.

title: Dupont Street - Parking Amendments
brief: The item proposes a one-hour parking limit on the south side of Dupont Street near Campbell Avenue, weekdays 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., after businesses said customers cannot find parking.

title: Non-Competitive Contracts with Various Suppliers for the Purchase of Proprietary Parts and Services for Maintenance of Specialized Laboratory Instruments for Toronto Water
topics: contracts, maintenance, purchasing, water, water laboratories
brief: City Council will vote on $236,650 ($240,815 net of HST recoveries) in non-competitive laboratory instrument contracts with Thermo Fisher and Waters; source documents also list $500,000, $81,853 ($83,294) and $154,797 ($157,521).
stake: The official summary names a figure of $236,650.

title: Emergency Non-Competitive Contract with Alberici Constructors Ltd., for the Roof Replacement at the Humber Treatment Plant Operations and Control Centre
topics: contracts, municipal facilities, repairs, sewer and water infrastructure, wastewater treatment plants
waste water treatment plants, sewer and water services
brief: City Council will be advised of an emergency $1,741,076 ($1,771,719 net of HST recoveries) Alberici contract for the Humber Treatment Plant roof replacement; source documents also list $1,741,076, as a figure with a trailing comma.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $1,741,076.

title: George Street Revitalization Project - Progress Update and Project Delivery Model
topics: community & life (sc), construction, housing services, projects
brief: City Council will consider the George Street Revitalization progress update and delegated delivery authorities; source documents list $500,000, $480,000 and $488,448.

title: TransformTO Net Zero Strategy: Action Plan (2026-2030)
brief: The TransformTO Net Zero action plan for 2026 to 2030, the City's next steps toward net zero by 2040, is before council to note, with staff reporting back in 2028 on the costs. The City has put $1.95 billion in its 2025 capital budget toward climate action, plus $13.87 billion in the 10-year plan.
stake: About climate. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 24 in favour, none against.

title: Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Cities Initiative (GLSLC) - Climate Mayors Leadership Forum
topics: climate, climate change, energy efficiency, housing
brief: This is a report for information only: Councillor Paul Ainslie reports back on attending the Sept. 24, 2025 Climate Mayors Leadership Forum in New York City as the Mayor's representative. No decision is needed.

title: Occupational Health and Safety Report: End of Year 2024
brief: City Council will receive the 2024 health and safety report: injuries down, but WSIB costs up from $57.3 million to $65.9 million.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $57.3 million.

title: City of Toronto Investment Report for the Six Month Period Ending June 30, 2025
brief: This is a report for information only: staff present the city's six-month investment report, covering fund performance through June 30, 2025, market updates, and whether investments followed city policy. The General Fund earned 1.7 percent and made $179.0 million. The report also cites figures of $2 billion and $32.6 million. No decision is needed.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $179.0 million.

title: Largest Property Tax Debtors with Tax Arrears Greater than $500,000 as at December 31, 2024
brief: City Council will review the 27 properties owing $500,000 or more in property tax as of December 31, 2024; source documents list $500,000.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $500,000.

title: Community Groups Animation of City Hall Podium Rooftop Floral Gardens
topics: community gardens, green roofs, natural gardens, natural lawn and garden care
brief: The item asks City Council to let community groups plant and maintain the City Hall rooftop floral gardens from spring 2026.

title: Amendment to Authority to Execute Blanket Contract with Salesforce.com Canada Corporation for Cloud-Based Services
topics: city initiatives, contracts, information and communication technology, licences
brief: City Council will vote on adding $6,751,001 ($6,869,819 net of HST recoveries) to the Salesforce contract authority for 2026-2030.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $6,751,001.

title: Report from the Mayor’s Designate to the Metropolis World Congress in Seoul, Korea
brief: This is a report for information only: Councillor Nick Mantas reports back on attending the Metropolis World Congress in Seoul, Korea, in September 2025 as the Mayor's designate. No decision is needed.

title: Amendment to Non-Competitive Contract Number 47023371 with 2790584 Ontario Inc for Catering for Multiple Toronto Shelter and Support Services Locations
topics: food preparation, housing services, transitional housing
brief: City Council will vote on extending the shelter catering contract to August 31, 2026; source documents list $500,000.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $500,000.

title: Award of Doc5080239163 to Premier Racquet Clubs Corp., for Operation and Maintenance of Seasonal Sports Bubbles for Tennis and Related Services for Eglinton Flats Park
topics: community & life (sc), contracts, parks, sports facilities, tennis, tennis courts
brief: A new ten-season agreement would let Premier Racquet Clubs run two seasonal tennis bubbles at Eglinton Flats Park, doubling winter court capacity, with the first bubble expected by fall 2026.

title: Execution of Construction Agreement with Kilmer-Tricon for the Construction of a New Toronto Paramedic Services Multi-Function Station at 610 Bay Street
topics: agreements, construction, emergency medical services stations, paramedics, properties (real estate)
brief: City Council will vote on a construction agreement up to $40,976,589 ($41,697,777 net of HST recoveries) with Kilmer-Tricon for the new paramedic station at 610 Bay Street; source documents also list $500,000, as a figure with a trailing comma.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $40,976,589.

title: Progress and Priorities for Enhancing Toronto’s Climate Resilience
brief: Council would adopt a Climate Change Resilience Workplan to prepare Toronto for climate impacts, put the Environment, Climate and Forestry division in charge, and ask city boards, including housing, hydro, conservation, library, and TTC, to take part.

title: Operating Variance Report for the Nine Months Ended September 30, 2025
brief: Staff report the city's day-to-day spending for the first nine months of 2025 and forecast year-end totals. Council would approve budget changes that do not change the city's net budget. The report cites figures of $8.2 million, $97.4 million, $57.2 million and $48.8 million.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $8.2 million.

title: Obligatory Reserve Funds, Reserves and Discretionary Reserve Funds as at September 30, 2025
brief: Council would approve moving $84.0 million between reserve funds and close 20 old, unused reserves, based on a report on the city's reserve balances for the first nine months of 2025. The report cites figures of $6,726.4 million, $7,963.3 million, $1,236.9 million, $433.2 million, $5,612.8 million, $6,046.0 million, $5,752.7 million, $293.3 million, $18,849.1 million, $41,066.7 million and $14,009.3 million.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $6,726.4 million.

title: 2026 Interim Water and Wastewater Consumption Rates and Service Fees
brief: Council would adopt interim 2026 water rates up 3.75% from Jan. 1, 2026, so Toronto Water can fund its operations until the final 2026 budget is set. Council can adjust the rates when the budget is adopted. Low-income seniors and disabled persons would get a rebate rate of $1.4589 per cubic metre.

title: 2026 Tax and Rate Supported Interim Operating and Capital Spending Authorities
brief: Council would approve $5.353 billion in interim 2026 spending authority so city divisions and agencies can keep delivering current services and honour contracts until the final 2026 budget is adopted. No money for new or better services. The report cites figures of $5 and $2.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $5.353 billion.

title: Summary Report on U20 Summit in Johannesburg
brief: This is a report for information only: Councillor Alejandra Bravo reports back on attending the 2025 Urban 20 (U20) Summit in Johannesburg as the Mayor's designate. No decision is needed.

title: Amending the Lobbying By-law Roundtables and Advisory Groups
brief: Council would change the lobbying rules so that talks during city-run advisory roundtables and working groups do not count as lobbying, if the group's purpose, members, and meeting records are public, to encourage public participation.

title: Making life more affordable for families by asking luxury-home buyers to chip in more
topics: Municipal Land Transfer Tax, tax increase, taxes
brief: Council would raise land transfer tax on luxury homes, from 4.4% on homes over $3,000,000 up to 8.6% on homes over $20,000,000, starting April 1, 2026, so higher-priced buyers pay more toward city services. The item also cites thresholds of $4,000,000, $5,000,000 and $10,000,000, notes $138 million was raised in 2024, and cites a $1,200 figure.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $1,200. Decided by a recorded vote, 17 in favour and 7 against — every member's position is public.

title: Capital Variance Report for the Nine Months Ended September 30, 2025
brief: Staff report the city's big-project spending for the first nine months of 2025 was $3.140 billion, or 48.8 percent of the approved budget, and forecast year-end totals. Council would approve adjustments to the approved capital budget and plan.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $3.140 billion.

title: 2026 Interim Solid Waste Management Services Rates and Fees
brief: Council would adopt interim 2026 garbage and recycling rates up 3.75% from January 1, 2026, so staff can collect them while the final 2026 budget is set. Council can change the rates when the full budget is approved.

title: Revised and Restated Non-Competitive Master Services Agreement with SmartSimple Software Inc., for Toronto Grants, Rebates, and Incentives Portal
brief: City Council will vote on a $1,173,706 ($1,194,363 net of HST recoveries) revised SmartSimple agreement for the grants portal; source documents also list $500,000.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $1,173,706.

title: Request for Approval to Apply Proposal Fees and Break Fees on Gardiner Expressway Rehabilitation Section 4, Grand Magazine Street to York Street
brief: City Council will vote on using proposal and break fees in the Gardiner Expressway Section 4 rehabilitation procurement.

title: 29 Basin Street - Update to Ground Lease Amendments
brief: Council, as owner of the Toronto Port Lands Company, would approve changes to the ground lease for Basin Studios, a film and TV hub at 29 Basin Street, an approximately $300 million project with 12 sound stages.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $300 million.

title: Amendment to Non-Competitive Purchase Order 6055323 with Accenture for Professional Services
topics: contracts, government services, service delivery, services
brief: City Council will vote on a $343,750 ($349,800 net of HST recoveries) Accenture professional services renewal; source documents also list $500,000, $481,250, $825,000, $489,720 and $839,520.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $343,750.

title: Non-Competitive Procurement with Symphony Talent, LLC, for Skills Assessment Services
topics: agreements, contracts, government services, service delivery, services
brief: City Council will vote on a non-competitive Symphony Talent skills assessment software agreement; source documents list $500,000, $190,045 and $193,390.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $500,000.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with IBM Canada Limited for IBM Maximo Application Suite Software as a Service
brief: City Council will vote on a $34,300,219 ($34,903,904 net of HST recoveries) non-competitive IBM Maximo cloud contract for work management systems; source documents also list $500,000.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $34,300,219.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Grascan Construction Limited / Torbridge Construction Limited to Repair Select F.G. Gardiner Expressway Concrete Bents at Bay Street and Yonge Street
topics: construction, contracts, highways, projects, transportation infrastructure
brief: City Council will vote on a $4,838,911 ($4,924,076 net of HST recoveries) non-competitive Gardiner bents repair contract; source documents also list $500,000, plus $500,000, as a figure with a trailing comma.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $4,838,911.

title: Non-Competitive Procurement of Heritage-Compliant Marble from Tennessee Marble Company for Union Station Great Hall Flooring Restoration
brief: City Council will vote on a non-competitive Tennessee Marble contract to finish the Union Station Great Hall floor; source documents list $500,000, $3,100,415 and $3,154,982.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $500,000.

title: Strengthening the City's Heat Relief Strategy
topics: emergency management, emergency plans, executive committees
brief: Council would tell the city's emergency office to keep working with the Hot Weather Response Committee to finalize and carry out the draft 2026 Heat Relief Strategy, which aims to reduce health harms from extreme heat.
stake: About emergency management. Decided by a recorded vote, 3 in favour and 22 against — every member's position is public.

title: Suspension of Capital Sewer Services Inc., and Affiliated Persons
brief: City Council will vote on a five-year suspension of Capital Sewer Services and affiliated companies from city contracts; source documents list $1.1 million.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $1.1 million.

title: Endorsement of the Reinstatement of the Lakeshore-Midtown Line in Metrolinx’s Business Model
topics: executive committees, public transit, transit routes, urban transit systems
brief: Councillor Paul Ainslie asks council to request that Metrolinx bring back the cancelled Lakeshore-Midtown rail line, which would have run from Oakville through Midtown Toronto and Scarborough to Oshawa, into its planning, with city advocacy to the province.

title: Status Update: Implementation of Ombudsman’s Recommendations and Council Directives on the City’s Response to a Vital Services Outage in a Multi-Tenant Home
brief: This is a report for information only: staff update council on actions taken after the Ombudsman's recommendations about the city's handling of a six-month utilities outage in a multi-tenant home in 2023. No decision is needed.

title: Towards Implementing a Maximum Indoor Temperature Requirement for Rental Units and Cooling Rooms
topics: executive committees, heating, ventilation and air conditioning systems, public health, rental housing, temperature
brief: Council would pass a rule capping apartment indoor temperatures at 26 degrees: buildings with an amenity room but without unit-wide cooling would keep one amenity room at 26 degrees or cooler from June to September, starting 2026.
stake: About executive committees. Decided by a recorded vote, 24 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: Amendment to Authority to Execute Blanket Contract with Granicus for Development Tracking Platform Licenses and Professional Services
topics: contracts, development, external services, housing, licences
brief: City Council will vote on raising the contract ceiling for the new development tracking platform that handles about $1.4 billion in annual revenue; source documents also list $500,000.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $1.4 billion.

title: Status Update - Wider Waterfront Program
brief: Council would have staff work with the conservation authority and Waterfront Toronto on waterfront projects outside the central waterfront, including the Scarborough Waterfront Project, and report back in 2027 with funding needs and next steps. The report cites a $5 million figure.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $5 million.

title: Shelter Pressures and Access Initiatives - Updates
brief: Council would approve a new framework for reviewing shelter eligibility changes and let staff keep running the Emergency Family Shelter Support program while budget money lasts.

title: 444 Logan Avenue - Making Quality of Life and Environmental Improvements for Seniors
brief: Council votes on a new social housing deal with WoodGreen for the 160-unit seniors building at 444 Logan Avenue. The building would be exempt from property taxes for 40 years. Its annual property taxes are estimated at $239,473. Approving the deal would let WoodGreen get about $27 million in federal money to upgrade the building's heating, cooling, and homes for its senior residents.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $27 million. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 22 in favour, none against.

title: Opposition to the Amalgamation of Conservation Authorities
topics: conservation authorities, provincial governments, provincial legislation
brief: A councillor wants Council to tell Ontario it opposes merging conservation authorities by force, and to urge the province to pause, keep watershed-based management, and consult cities.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Metro Toronto Convention Centre Board
brief: This is a procedural item: a city panel is asked to recommend two candidates to council for the Metro Toronto Convention Centre Board, for a term ending December 2028. No new rules here.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the CreateTO Board
brief: This is a procedural item: a city panel is asked to recommend two people to council for the CreateTO Board and the boards of Build Toronto and the Toronto Port Lands Company, one as chair, plus re-appoint Marcie Zajdeman. No new rules here.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Committee of Adjustment
brief: Appointing Camille Clyne, Ann Crawford and Alexander Adams to the North York, Toronto-East York and Etobicoke York panels of the Committee of Adjustment, for terms ending November 14, 2026 is on council's agenda.

title: 234 Sheppard Avenue West and 223 Harlandale Avenue - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about planning and zoning applications for 234 Sheppard Avenue West and 223 Harlandale Avenue. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: Formal Approval of Gerrard-Carlaw Dogs Off Leash Area
topics: dog off-leash areas, parks, parks and open space areas
brief: A councillor wants Council to have staff work with the local councillor on proper consultation, design, and budget for rebuilding the Gerrard-Carlaw dog off-leash area after Metrolinx work ends in 2031.

title: Expropriation of 81 Bloor Street East and 40-42 Hayden Street - Request for Directions Regarding Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions for a hearing on the expropriation of 81 Bloor Street East and 40-42 Hayden Street for the Bloor-Yonge station expansion. The strategy is confidential.

title: 110-112 Adelaide Street East and 85 Lombard Street - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about a proposed 65-storey building with 600 homes at 110-112 Adelaide Street East and 85 Lombard Street. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: Appointment of Chief Building Official and Executive Director, Toronto Building
brief: Appointing a new Chief Building Official and Executive Director of Toronto Building, effective January 1, 2026 is on council's agenda. The candidate's name is confidential until they accept.

title: Award and Appointment of an External Auditor for the Annual Compliance Audit of the Accountability Offices - 2025 to 2029
brief: Appointing Kwok and Associate as external auditor for annual compliance audits of the four accountability offices for 2025-2029, at a cost of $67,000 net of taxes is on council's agenda. The firm was the lowest bidder.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $67,000.

title: Ookwemin Minising - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Direction
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about the Ookwemin Minising (Villiers Island) revitalization in the Port Lands. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: Official Plan Amendment 231 - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on tribunal cases involving 178 appeals of Official Plan Amendment 231, the city-wide policy on employment lands. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Development at 30 Tippett Road for Streetscape Improvements in the Wilson Village Business Improvement Area - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
brief: $60,000.00 of developer money this year for street upgrades in the Wilson Village business area in North York would be released, if council agrees.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $60,000.00.

title: Introduction of General Bills and Confirming Bills
brief: This is a procedural step: City Council will introduce general bills and confirming bills, which turn approved decisions into official bylaws. No new policy is decided.

title: Naming of the Central Pathway in Earlscourt Park to “Claude Bergeron Pathway” - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
brief: The central path in Earlscourt Park would be named the Claude Bergeron Pathway, honouring a community advocate who helped improve the park from the early 2000s until 2023, if council agrees.

title: Moving Forward with Transform Yonge: Visionary Public Realm and Cycling Gains, Without Losing a Lane - We Want it All! - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
brief: A councillor asks council to study whether the Transform Yonge redesign can keep its safety and bike upgrades on Yonge between Sheppard and Finch without removing a car lane, and whether it can stretch north to Steeles.
stake: About road reconstruction. Decided by a recorded vote, 20 in favour and 3 against — every member's position is public.

title: Securing More Good Jobs in Toronto: Support for Hosting the Defence, Security and Resilience Bank Headquarters - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
brief: Toronto as the head office of the new Defence, Security and Resilience Bank, an international bank, to grow the city's economy and jobs would be backed by council.
stake: About economy. Decided by a recorded vote, 19 in favour and 4 against — every member's position is public.

title: Amending Item 2024.CC20.24 - 200 University Avenue - Official Plan Amendment, Zoning By-law Amendment and Site Plan Control Applications - Appeal Report - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: affordable housing, rental housing, zoning bylaws
brief: Its earlier approval for 200 University Avenue would be updated to show 24 affordable rentals instead of 20, making those units eligible for planning and building fee waivers, if council agrees. The item lists $162,223.00 and $1,213,036.00.

title: 3386 to 3398 Bayview and 32 Brenham Crescent - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about a proposed 50-townhouse development at 3386-3398 Bayview Avenue and 32 Brenham Crescent. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: 4875 Dundas Street West - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about a proposed 45-storey building with 488 homes at 4875 Dundas Street West. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: 4466 Sheppard Avenue East - Toronto Local Appeal Body Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on an appeal hearing about converting office space into a pool and billiards hall at 4466 Sheppard Avenue East. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: 180 Queens Drive - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: An intent to designate 180 Queens Drive in Weston as a heritage property under the Ontario Heritage Act would be stated by council. If no objections are filed, a designation bylaw follows.

title: 324 Old Yonge Street - Proposed Designation By-law Under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Consideration of Objection
brief: The decision to designate 324 Old Yonge Street as a heritage property, despite the owner's objection, would be affirmed by council, proceeding with the designation bylaw.

title: 336 and 340 Jarvis Street - Proposed Designation By-Laws under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Consideration of Objection
brief: The decision to designate 336 and 340 Jarvis Street as heritage properties, despite owner objections, would be affirmed by council, moving ahead with the designation bylaws.

title: 3019 Dufferin Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about a proposed 8-storey building at 3019 Dufferin Street. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: 3377 Bayview Avenue - Request to Review Ontario Land Tribunal Decision - Request for Directions
brief: The owner of 3377 Bayview Avenue wants the tribunal to review a decision on a settlement council already accepted. The City Solicitor asks council for private directions.

title: Rallies and Protests Policy
brief: The item asks City staff when Council will get the updated staff plan on rules for rallies and protests to debate. The inquiry says managing protests has cost the City over $30 million in police time.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $30 million. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Axon Enterprise Inc., for Axon Justice Premier Licences
topics: contracts, digital libraries, information & communication (sc), legal matters, licences
brief: City Council will vote on a $511,020 ($520,014 net of HST recoveries) non-competitive Axon evidence management contract, $170,340 ($173,338 net of HST recoveries) per year for 85 licences; source documents also list $500,000 and $511,020, as a figure with a trailing comma, and $511,020.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $511,020.

title: Seeking Clarity on the City of Toronto’s Application to the Community Sport and Recreation Infrastructure Fund
brief: The item asks City staff about the City's application to the province's $200 million Community Sport and Recreation Infrastructure Fund, which offers grants up to $10 million.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $200 million. Decided by a recorded vote, 18 in favour and 5 against — every member's position is public.

title: Safety on all City Sidewalks; E-bikes Enforcement - by Councillor Jon Burnside, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
brief: Transportation staff would report on legal options to let police seize e-bikes and e-scooters ridden on sidewalks, where they are already illegal and dangerous to walkers, if council agrees.
stake: About enforcement. Decided by a recorded vote, 21 in favour and 2 against — every member's position is public.

title: Bayside Land Development Agreement - Sunset Date Extension for C1
brief: Council would extend the deadline in the land deal with Hines for the Bayside waterfront's Block C1 to April 30, 2026, to give more time to find a workable office plan. Any ground lease still needs council's approval.
