title: Designation of the Properties Used by Toronto Shelter and Support Services as Municipal Capital Facilities
topics: housing, municipal facilities, properties (real estate), supportive housing, taxes
brief: City Council will vote on tax exemptions for eight leased shelter properties across six wards.

title: Business Improvement Areas - Update on the 2024 Audited Financial Statements
topics: annual reports, boards of management, business associations, business improvement areas, neighbourhoods
business improvement associations, boards of directors
brief: Council will vote on approving the audited 2024 financial statements for 50 Business Improvement Areas, which all got clean audit opinions. Ten got minor tips to improve their controls; twenty more statements are still being finished.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Zoll Medical Canada Inc., for the Provision of Cardiac Monitors / Defibrillators with all Accessories, Proprietary Consumables and Extended Maintenance Agreements
topics: contracts, emergency medical services, paramedics, purchasing
brief: City Council will vote on a $24,758,371 ($25,194,118 net of HST recoveries) non-competitive Zoll cardiac monitor contract for paramedics and fire services; source documents also list $500,000.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $24,758,371.

title: Amendment to Purchase Order 6046601 with Graham Construction and Engineering LP and Purchase Order 6046595 with AECOM CANADA ULC, for the Ashbridges Bay Treatment Plant UV Disinfection Facility Construction Project
topics: construction, contracts, purchasing, wastewater treatment plants, water treatment plants
brief: City Council will vote on two Ashbridges Bay UV disinfection amendments: Graham up $9,680,000 ($9,850,368 net of HST recoveries) from $209,363,500 ($213,048,298 net of HST recoveries) to $219,043,500 ($222,898,666 net of HST recoveries), and AECOM up $4,591,755 ($4,672,570 net of HST recoveries) from $16,214,983 ($16,500,367 net of HST recoveries) to $20,806,738 ($21,172,936 net of HST recoveries, $16,500,366 also listed).
stake: The official summary names a figure of $9,680,000.

title: 2024 Annual Human Rights Office Report
topics: complaints, human rights, policy development, workplaces
brief: City Council will vote on adopting the amended Human Rights and Anti-Harassment / Discrimination Policy, alongside the Human Rights Office 2024 report: 1,574 inquiries, up 32 percent in one year.

title: Application for Approval to Expropriate a Portion of 20 Humberview Crescent and 50 St. Phillips Road - Stage 1
brief: City Council will vote on starting expropriation of parts of two properties for the Mid Humber Gap trail project.
stake: About easements. Decided by a recorded vote, 22 in favour and 3 against — every member's position is public.

title: Amendment to Purchase Order Number 6050742 with CIMA Canada Inc., for Upgrades to Raw Water Valves at F. J. Horgan Water Treatment Plant
topics: contracts, engineering, projects, purchasing, water treatment plants
brief: City Council will vote on adding $175,000 ($178,080 net of HST recoveries) to the CIMA water valve engineering order, raising it from $1,067,017 ($1,085,796 net of HST recoveries) to $1,242,017 ($1,263,876 net of HST recoveries).
stake: The official summary names a figure of $175,000.

title: Appointment of a Public Member to the Toronto Global Board
brief: The Civic Appointments Committee picks 4 people to interview for the Toronto Global Board, then recommends one to council. Candidate names are kept private.

title: Appointment of Members to the Confronting Anti-Black Racism Advisory Committee
brief: Appointing 3 new community members to the Confronting Anti-Black Racism Advisory Committee, filling 3 resignations, for terms ending November 14, 2026 is on council's agenda. Names are kept private.

title: 150 College Street (Medical Sciences Building - 1 King's College Circle) - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: Council votes on starting heritage protection for the Medical Sciences Building at 150 College Street, built 1966-1970.

title: 54, 66 and 68 Fraser Avenue - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: Council votes on starting heritage protection for three old factory buildings at 54, 66 and 68 Fraser Avenue in Liberty Village.

title: Non-Competitive Agreement with Trecan Combustion Limited for the Rent-to-Own Option and Supply and Delivery of Original Equipment Manufacturer Services for Trecan Snowmelters
topics: contracts, purchasing, snow, snow melting machines, winter
brief: City Council will vote on a non-competitive Trecan snowmelter rent-to-own and service agreement; source documents list $2,869,780, $2,852,013, $2,820,145, $3,940,350, $4,452,595, $3,872,199 and $500,000.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $2,869,780.

title: 164 and 166 Isabella Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: Council votes on starting heritage protection for two 1887 houses at 164 and 166 Isabella Street.

title: Technical Amendments to Zoning By-law 569-2013 and By-law 335-2024
brief: Council votes on technical fixes to the city-wide zoning by-law: typos, wording and map boundaries. Nothing about what is allowed changes.

title: 81 Isabella Street - Proposed Designation By-Law under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Consideration of Objection
brief: Council votes on protecting the 1927 Merlan Apartments at 81 Isabella Street as heritage, using a revised statement that answers the owner's objection.

title: Amendment to Blanket Contract 47025543 with OpenText Corporation for Enterprise Document and Records Management Products and Professional Services Leveraging the Provincial Volume Licensing Agreement
brief: The General Government Committee will vote on adding $8,970,589 ($9,128,471.00 net of HST recoveries) to the OpenText document management contract, raising it from $1,440,328 ($1,465,678 net of HST recoveries) to $10,410,917 ($10,594,149 net of HST recoveries), and extending it to 2030.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $8,970,589.

title: Creating a Small Business Friendly Approach to Licensing and Permitting
brief: Council sent the idea of a small-business-friendly approach to licences and permits to the Economic and Community Development Committee. The committee will consider it; no recommendation is attached.

title: Provincial Planning Statement 2024 Consistency Exercise Phase 1 - Recommendation Report
brief: Council votes on Official Plan Amendment 846, the first phase of updates to line up the city's Official Plan with the province's new 2024 planning rules.

title: Strategic Expansion of the Association of Community Centres in New Development Projects to Strengthen Toronto Communities
brief: Staff would develop a multi-year plan for community centre facilities and operating costs, reporting back in early 2028, if council agrees.

title: Canada-wide Early Learning and Child Care Expansion - Update
brief: A request that the province and federal government provide more sustained capital and operating funding for Toronto's child care expansion targets goes to council.

title: FIFA World Cup 2026 Toronto: Procurement Plan Update
brief: Council would approve an updated buying plan for goods and services to host the 2026 FIFA World Cup in Toronto, and let staff negotiate and award contracts with vendors that meet cost targets.

title: Metrolinx Eglinton Crosstown LRT - At-grade Segment - Traffic and Parking By-law Amendments
brief: Approval of traffic and parking rule changes for Eglinton Avenue East between Kennedy Road and Brentcliffe Road to match the final layout of the Eglinton Crosstown LRT, before it opens is before council.

title: Redesign Study of the Intersection of Eglinton Avenue West and the Allen Road Expressway - Update
brief: Council will get an update on redesign options for the Eglinton Avenue West and Allen Road expressway intersection. No new rules are proposed.

title: Palmerston Area Character Study and Heritage Evaluation
topics: heritage conservation districts, land use designations
brief: City Council will consider starting a 2026 study of Palmerston Avenue and nearby streets, to guide future building design and judge whether the area should become a heritage district.

title: Weston Road from King Street to Denison Avenue (West/East) - Parking Regulation Changes
brief: City Council will vote on standardizing rush-hour no-parking rules on Weston Road between King Street and Denison Avenue.

title: Enhancing the Basement Flooding Protection Subsidy Program to Reduce Basement Flooding Risks
topics: basement flooding, city initiatives, stormwater management
basement flooding response, city council priorities
brief: The Basement Flooding Protection Subsidy Program would be boosted from May 2026, raising payments for backwater valves and sump pumps and adding up to $500 for a plumbing check, if council agrees. Other amounts: up to $300 for a sump pump battery backup, up to $6,650 per home in total, within a $12,000 per-home cap.

title: Creating Community Opportunities through the 4610 Finch Avenue East Long-Term Care Home Project
topics: community & life (sc), long term care homes, seniors housing
brief: Staff would work with community partners to build specialized care for Black seniors and Caribbean/African diaspora residents at the 378-bed care home at 4610 Finch Avenue East, and apply the city's Community Benefits Framework.
stake: About community & life (sc). Its recorded vote was unanimous — 20 in favour, none against.

title: FIFA World Cup 2026 Toronto: Legacy Update
brief: Council would move $37,500 of World Cup 2026 legacy funding to parks programs and $120,000 to social programs, at no extra cost to taxpayers, so community programs benefit from Toronto hosting the tournament. The report also cites a $5 million figure.

title: Toronto Local Appeal Body - Chair's 2024 Annual Report
brief: This is a routine item: council receives the 2024 annual report from the Toronto Local Appeal Body, which hears appeals of Committee of Adjustment decisions. No policy change.

title: Council Member Appointments to Fill Vacancies on Committees, Boards and External Bodies
brief: This is a routine item: the Striking Committee suggests councillors to fill empty seats on several committees and boards, including the Executive and Budget Committees and Board of Health, until November 2026. Council makes the final choices.

title: Next Generation Water Metering, Advanced Metering Infrastructure - Procurement Strategy
topics: sewer and water infrastructure, water billing, water meters
remote water meters, sewer and water services
brief: Planning for a new water metering system to replace the 2015 one, including hiring an expert to write requirements and help pick a vendor would start, if council agrees.

title: 10-Year Circular Economy Road Map
brief: A 10-year plan to cut landfill waste by reusing and recovering materials would start, and staff could sign supporting deals through 2036, if council agrees. The plan would need $2.4 million in 2026: $1.2 million for capital and about $1.2 million to run it.

title: Infrastructure Cost Sharing - Regent Park Phase 4
brief: Council votes on adding Regent Park Phase 4 infrastructure costs to the 2026-2035 capital budget and repaying Toronto Community Housing for eligible costs.

title: 4350 Steeles Avenue East - City of Markham - Development Submission - Update Report
brief: Council votes on sending Toronto's comments on a huge Markham development proposal — about 5,500 homes at Steeles Avenue East — to Markham's planners.

title: Automated Speed Enforcement Program Update
topics: enforcement, speed limits, traffic cameras, traffic speed
brief: Council will get an update on the speed camera program, which grew from 50 to 150 cameras by early 2025 under the Vision Zero safety plan. Council also asked the province to repay $31.2 million for crossing guards, $3.9 million for traffic officers, and $210 million in road safety capital spending.
stake: About enforcement. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 25 in favour, none against.

title: Property Standards By-law: Phase II Review and Other Property Items
brief: Council votes on rewriting the property standards by-law and creating a new pest-management by-law, both starting May 1, 2027. The report references $50,000 and $250,000.

title: Transition of the Blue Box Program to Extended Producer Responsibility: Post-Transition Plan
topics: blue bin materials, blue bins, recyclables, recycling, solid waste, solid waste management, waste diversion
refuse, single stream recyclable materials, solid waste management planning
brief: Staff could sign deals with producer groups for recycling things like batteries, tires, and electronics through 2031, as the Blue Box shifts to producer responsibility from 2026, if council agrees.

title: 2024-2025 Annual Progress Report - HousingTO 2020-2030 Action Plan and Housing Action Plan (2022-2026)
brief: Council receives the 2024-2025 progress report on the city's housing plans, and asks Ottawa and CMHC for $163 million and $2.6 billion to build supportive homes and mixed-income communities. The report also cites $13 million, $150 million, $48 million, $16 million, $23 million and $50,000.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $13 million. Decided by a recorded vote, 18 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: High Pollution Days and Two Stroke Engines
topics: air pollution, air quality, air quality health index, air quality indicators, diesel fuel, fuels, leaf blowers
brief: A councillor wants Council to ask City crews, businesses, and residents to avoid smoky engines, like gas leaf blowers and old diesel engines, on days when air quality is bad.

title: 2025 Chief Information Security Officer's Report on Agencies and Corporations
brief: This is a report for information only: staff update council on cyber security at city agencies and corporations, noting a 37% improvement in overall cyber resilience scores. No decision is needed.

title: Property Taxes: 2026 Interim Levy By-Law
brief: Council would pass a by-law for the interim 2026 property tax, about $3.053 billion, or half of each property's 2025 bill, to cover city costs until the final 2026 budget and tax rate are set. The report cites a $3 figure.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $3.053 billion.

title: Impacts of Provincial Legislation that Weakens Rental Protections
brief: Council would tell Ontario it opposes Bill 60 changes that would weaken renter protections, including rent control and security of tenure, and renew its call for rent control on rentals first occupied after 2018. Council also renewed its request for a Build More Homes Rebate of at least $596 million for 15,830 purpose-built rental homes.
stake: A citywide decision. Decided by a recorded vote, 23 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: Community Centre 55 - 2024 Audited Financial Statements
topics: audits, boards of management, community centres, financial reports
brief: This is a routine item: council is asked to accept the checked 2024 financial statements for the one remaining community centre. No policy change is proposed.

title: Metrolinx Ontario Line - Cosburn Station, Bain Emergency Exit Building and Gerrard Portal - Temporary Road Closures and Transportation Impacts
topics: parking regulations, regional transportation agencies, road closures, transportation projects
brief: Council would approve temporary lane and laneway closures, new pedestrian crossings, and traffic rule changes from 2026 to 2030 to make room for Ontario Line subway construction around Cosburn Station, the Bain emergency exit, and the Gerrard portal.
stake: About parking regulations. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 25 in favour, none against.

title: Arenas - 2024 Audited Financial Statements and Status of Outstanding 2024 Audited Financial Statements
topics: arenas, audits, boards of management, community & life (sc), financial reports
boards of governors, indoor hockey rinks
brief: This is a routine item: council is asked to accept the checked 2024 financial statements for four city arenas. Two more arenas' statements are still to come.

title: Auditor General’s Office 2026 Work Plan and Budget Highlights
brief: The Auditor General's 2026 work plan goes to Council as information. It lists planned audits and notes her $9.119 million budget request, which the Budget Committee will consider separately. No new spending is proposed here.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $9.119 million. Decided by a recorded vote, 16 in favour and 3 against — every member's position is public.

title: St. Clair-Old Weston Station and 2025 GO Expansion Program Updates
brief: Council would approve switching the planned St. Clair-Old Weston station from GO trains to UP Express trains, but only if the province pays all costs, keeps trains at least every 15 minutes, and works on integrated fares.
stake: About public transit. Decided by a recorded vote, 20 in favour and 2 against — every member's position is public.

title: Arena Boards of Management Settlement of Operating Results for the Year Ended 2023; and 2022 Specifically for Ted Reeve Arena
brief: Council would close the 2022 and 2023 books for eight city-run arenas. Surpluses of $309,478 from three arenas will cover deficits of $341,723 from six others, leaving the city to cover a net $32,245.

title: Utility Construction Photo Documentation
brief: This is a routine item: council is asked to accept a report on upgrades that make utility companies send before-and-after photos of road work. No new decision is proposed.
stake: About infrastructure. Council sent it back for more work.

title: Progress Report on the Toronto Ferry Service
brief: This is a report for information only: staff update council on the Toronto ferry service, covering the operational review, new electric boats, and customer experience at the Jack Layton Ferry Terminal. No decision is needed.

title: Audit of Toronto Water: Stormwater and Wastewater Contract Management
brief: The Auditor General checked how Toronto Water manages sewer construction contracts and found it could track delays and time extensions better. Council is asked to have staff tighten paperwork and monitoring.

title: Toronto Community Housing Corporation - 2025 Follow-up - Status of Previous Auditor General’s Recommendations, and Toronto Community Housing Corporation - Results of 2021 Follow-up of Previous Audit Recommendations
topics: audits, financial reports, housing, housing providers, housing services
brief: This is a routine item: council is asked to accept a Toronto Community Housing board report on past Auditor General recommendations as information. No new decision is proposed.

title: Reimagining Weston Lions Arena through a Nominal Lease with MLSE LaunchPad
brief: Council would approve a very low-cost 20-year lease, with two possible 10-year extensions, letting MLSE LaunchPad use the city-owned Weston Lions Arena to expand free, high-quality youth recreation programs in the area. The report cites a $25 million figure.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $25 million. Decided by a recorded vote, 23 in favour and 2 against — every member's position is public.

title: Audit of Parks Branch Operations - Phase 1 and 2: November 2025 Status Update
brief: This is a routine item: council is asked to accept an update on how staff are carrying out the Auditor General's ideas to improve park maintenance and repairs. No new decision is proposed.

title: Legal Review of Complaint Relating to Toronto Parking Authority Parking Access and Revenue Control System Request for Proposals Process
brief: Council receives for information the City Manager and City Solicitor's legal review of the Toronto Parking Authority's bid process for a parking system contract, done after a complaint. No decision is proposed.

title: Call to Order
brief: This is a routine item: the meeting opens with the call to order, O Canada, and a moment of silence. No decision is asked for.
stake: A citywide decision. Decided by a recorded vote, 19 in favour and 6 against — every member's position is public.

title: Confirmation of Minutes
brief: This is a routine item: council checks the written record of its October 8 and 9, 2025, meeting and confirms it is correct. No new decision is asked for.

title: Introduction of Committee Reports and New Business from City Officials
brief: This is a routine item: committee leaders and city staff introduce reports and new business. Council only hears them now; no decision is asked for.

title: Declarations of Interest
brief: This is a routine item: councillors say if they have a personal interest in any item, as the conflict-of-interest law requires. No decision is asked for.
stake: A citywide decision. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Petitions
brief: This is a routine item: councillors may hand in petitions from residents to be recorded. No decision is asked for.
stake: A citywide decision. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Presentations, Introductions and Announcements
brief: This is a routine item: the meeting includes presentations, introductions, and announcements. Council only listens; no decision is asked for.
stake: A citywide decision. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Review of the Order Paper
brief: This is a routine item: council looks over the order paper, the list of topics for this meeting. No decision is asked for.

title: Understanding the Impacts of Bill 60 on Health and Well-Being in Toronto
brief: The Medical Officer of Health would review Bill 60 and provincial rent control proposals, and assess their possible health impacts in Toronto, if the Board agrees. Housing stability is a key factor in health.
stake: A citywide decision. Decided by a recorded vote, 23 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: Toronto Sports and Culture Should Be For Everyone
brief: Staff would explore consumer protection for major sports events, and council would ask Ontario to ban reselling event tickets above face value. The motion cites 1993 World Series tickets under $32 versus resale tickets now up to $10,000.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $32.

title: Understanding the Impacts of Bill 60 on Homelessness in Toronto
brief: Staff would report in November 2025 on how provincial Bill 60 could affect Toronto renters and homelessness, and the Association of Municipalities of Ontario would be asked to convene province-wide research, if the committee agrees.
stake: About homelessness. Decided by a recorded vote, 23 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: Accepting an In-Kind Donation from Hillcrest Tennis Club to Refurbish the Tennis Courts at Cresthaven Park - by Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Nick Mantas
brief: Up to $150,000.00 in donated tennis-court repair work from the Hillcrest Tennis Club at Cresthaven Park in 2026, under the city's tennis club policy would be accepted, if council agrees.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $150,000.00.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2025.TE22.3 - 72 Perth Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
brief: This is a technical fix: council is asked to drop one set of terms from its earlier approval for 13 affordable rentals at 72 Perth Avenue, changing the required mix of unit sizes. No new rules here.

title: 32, 36 and 38 Olive Avenue - Development Charges Complaint - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a development-charges complaint for 32, 36 and 38 Olive Avenue. Details are legally confidential.

title: 2 Tippett Road - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about a proposed 33-storey building with 417 homes at 2 Tippett Road. The legal strategy is confidential.
stake: About planning & development (sc). Decided by a recorded vote, 25 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: 1601 to 1603 Bathurst Street - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about a proposed 7-storey building with 74 homes at 1601-1603 Bathurst Street. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: 847-855 Kingston Road - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about a proposed 11-storey mixed-use building at 847-855 Kingston Road. The legal strategy is confidential.
stake: About planning & development (sc). Council put off deciding this item.

title: 155 Saint Dennis Drive - Appeal of Ontario Land Tribunal Decision
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on whether to challenge a tribunal decision approving planning and zoning changes for 155 Saint Dennis Drive. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: 2025 Winter Maintenance Program Review Update
topics: contracts, road maintenance, snow emergencies, snow management, winter storms
brief: Council would require a report on how this winter's snow-clearing improvements are working, and update city rules on parking and standing during major snowstorms, including on streets with streetcar tracks. The report cites a $130 million figure. The improvements cost about $1.3 million.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $130 million. Decided by a recorded vote, 21 in favour and 4 against — every member's position is public.

title: Results of Collective Bargaining Negotiations between the City of Toronto and Canadian Union of Public Employees Local 2998
brief: The new labour agreement with CUPE Local 2998, the union for city community centre staff would be ratified by council. The agreement details are confidential.
stake: About labour relations. Decided by a recorded vote, 21 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Development at 871 to 899 College Street for Lakeview Avenue Parkette Improvements - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
brief: An extra $131,014 of developer money on fixing up the Lakeview Avenue Parkette on Dundas Street West, on top of $200,000 approved in 2024 is before council for approval.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $200,000.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for the Fabrication and Installation of a Commemorative Plaque at Halbert Pool in Honour of Dave Harper - by Councillor Parthi Kandavel, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
brief: $2,882.00 of developer money on a plaque at Halbert Pool honouring Dave Harper, a longtime Scarborough community member and pool regular of 59 years is before council for approval.

title: 151 and 161 to 181 Mulock Avenue and 6 Lloyd Avenue - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: multi-residential properties, official plan amendments, zoning bylaws
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about Official Plan Amendment 231, which changed land-use rules for parts of Mulock Avenue and Lloyd Avenue. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: 2 Whitney Avenue (135 Glen Road) - Injunction to Prevent Removal of Encroachments Pending Court Application
brief: The City Solicitor asks council to adopt private directions about a court injunction over structures built on city property at 2 Whitney Avenue. The owners are challenging the removal order.

title: 1196 to 1204 Yonge Street, 1206 to 1210 Yonge Street and 2 to 8 Birch Avenue - Request to Review Ontario Land Tribunal Decision - Request for Directions
brief: The owner of 1196-1210 Yonge Street and 2-8 Birch Avenue wants the tribunal to review a decision on a settlement council already accepted. The City Solicitor asks council for private directions.

title: Introduction of General Bills and Confirming Bills
brief: This is a procedural step: City Council will introduce general bills and confirming bills, which turn approved decisions into official bylaws. No new policy is decided.

title: Adding Swim to Survive to the Ontario Curriculum to Improve Water Safety and Save Lives - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
brief: Ontario's Ministry of Education would be urged by council to add water safety and Swim to Survive lessons to the elementary school curriculum for all students.

title: Expanding the Listening to Toronto Survey to Support Ward-Level Insights - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
brief: The City Manager would look at growing the Listening to Toronto survey so results are useful by ward, and report back with options in spring 2026, if council agrees.

title: Advancing Affordable and Supportive Housing for Veterans - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
brief: Staff would report by fall 2026 on ways to build veterans' housing on city-owned land under the Toronto Builds plan, if council agrees.

title: Rehabilitating Amsterdam Bridge at Harbourfront Centre - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
brief: $640,000.00 in developer money to fix the Amsterdam Bridge footbridge at Harbourfront Centre, closed since 2021 is before council for approval. The $790,000 total is $350,000 in Section 37 funds, $150,000 from Harbourfront Centre and $290,000 from city capital budgets.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $350,000.00.

title: Protecting Playgrounds and Parks: Ensuring Safety for Children and Families - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside
topics: playground structures, public safety, tent cities
brief: A councillor asks council to change city rules so homeless encampments within 200 metres of a school, daycare or playground are removed first, within 48 hours of being reported.
stake: About homeless encampments. Decided by a recorded vote, 20 in favour and 6 against — every member's position is public.

title: Waiving Permit Fee Charges for the Annual Heroes of Suicide March - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
brief: The $151.58 permit fee for the yearly Heroes of Suicide Memorial March, honouring veterans and first responders lost to mental health struggles, for 2025 and future years would be waived, if council agrees.

title: Comments on the Request for a Minister’s Zoning Order to Restrict Building Heights - 1875 Steeles Avenue West to Protect Operational Viability of the Sanofi Pasteur Limited Manufacturing Facilities and Headquarters - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
brief: A provincial order capping building heights at 1875 Steeles Avenue West at 33 metres, to protect the Sanofi Pasteur vaccine plant next door would be backed by council.
stake: About zoning. Decided by a recorded vote, 23 in favour and 2 against — every member's position is public.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2025.TE21.7 - 315-325 Front Street West - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
brief: This is a technical fix: council is asked to update its earlier approval for 315 to 325 Front Street West with refined wording on parkland funds, public art, the child care centre and easements. No new rules here.

title: 712 Eglinton Avenue East - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councilor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng
brief: The city's lawyer would be authorized to appeal the committee's approval of zoning rule exceptions for a garden suite at 712 Eglinton Avenue East, and oppose the development at the local appeals board.
stake: About zoning bylaws. Decided by a recorded vote, 25 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Surface Impression LTD for the Provision and Completion of a Digital Learning Resource Where the Water Met the Land for Economic Development and Culture - by Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Alejandra Bravo
brief: Approval of a no-bid contract of $31,225.25 ($31,774.81 net of HST recoveries) with Surface Impression Ltd to finish an online learning resource about Fort York and Spadina Museum (the $500,000 is the spending limit that sends the deal to council for approval) is before council.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $31,225.25.

title: Respecting Local Authority Over Road Design - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Dianne Saxe
brief: A councillor asks council to oppose proposed provincial changes on road-design power and ask the province to confirm that cities can decide their own road designs.
stake: About road safety. Decided by a recorded vote, 19 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: Allowing Staff to Tow Unlicensed Vehicles on City Streets - by Councillor Anthony Perruzza, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
brief: Transportation staff, police and the Parking Authority would report on what rule changes would let unlicensed or abandoned vehicles on city streets be towed without warning, if council agrees.

title: Relief from Environmental Peer Review Requirements for Affordable Housing and Long-Term Care Development at 640 Lansdowne Avenue - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
brief: The planned 256-bed seniors' home and 57 affordable rentals at 640 Lansdowne Avenue from a city rule requiring an environmental review of land being given to the city would be exempted, if council agrees.

title: Driving Efficiencies at Toronto Parking Authority to Reduce 2026 Budget Pressures - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
brief: The Toronto Parking Authority board would change to include five city staff serving without extra pay, to streamline the agency and ease 2026 budget pressure, if council agrees. The budget faces a $1.072 billion opening pressure, after $680 million and $620 million in offsets in 2025 and 2024; the authority has over $144 million in operating costs and a capital plan of just under $400 million.

title: Accelerating Rehabilitation of the Cross Harbour Tunnel - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley

stake: The official summary names a figure of $53 billion. Decided by a recorded vote, 22 in favour and 2 against — every member's position is public.

The Board also asked City Council to fund a proposed route extension: about $467,000 a year to run it, plus about $450,000 to build 16 new stops.

topics: Toronto Transit Commission, advisory committees, board members, human resources
brief: The HR committee's focus would broaden to people, culture, governance, diversity, equity, and inclusion, with the committee renamed the People, Culture and Governance Committee, if the TTC Board agrees.

title: Creating a Late-Night Service for Major Special Events Policy - by Chair Jamaal Myers, seconded by Commissioner Josh Matlow
brief: After late-night transit fell short for World Series Game 7 fans, Chair Myers wants the TTC to build a late-night service policy for events, covering routes, staffing, and rider communications.

title: Selection of Candidates for Interview for the Metro Toronto Convention Centre Board
brief: This is a procedural item: a city panel is asked to select six candidates to interview for the Metro Toronto Convention Centre Board. No new rules here.

brief: This is a procedural item: a city panel is asked to select six candidates to interview for the CreateTO Board, including a chair. No new rules here.

title: 2026 Operating Budget
brief: The board would approve the 2026 operating budget and send it to the city, and approve a one-time loan repayment of up to $2.5 million. The report notes $595 million in annual economic impact and cites figures of $2 and $8. The budget targets a $2.2 million net profit.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $595 million.

title: Lease Agreement for Bandshell Restaurant (Acqua Dolce Supper Club)

title: 2026 Proposed Capital Works Budget as Part of Ten-Year (2026-2035) Program
brief: The board would approve the 2026 building budget: $22.525 million for repairs and $45.819 million for World Cup projects, as part of the ten-year plan, and send it to the city. The report also cites $56.7 million. The ten-year plan totals $253.9 million.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $17.154 million.

title: Ceremonial Renaming of Nunavut Road
brief: The board would rename Nunavut Road to One of a Kind Road for one day, November 27, 2025, to celebrate the One of a Kind Show's 50th anniversary at Exhibition Place.

title: Toronto Public Health's Preparation for FIFA World Cup 2026
brief: Toronto Public Health would stay involved in 2026 World Cup planning, if the Board agrees. Toronto hosts six matches June 11 to July 2, 2026, and the agency is preparing for health risks like disease, heat, and wildfire smoke.

brief: A public website launching January 1, 2026, where Toronto Public Health will post infection inspection results for licensed child care centres would get the Board's endorsement. It works like the DineSafe site and will show results on a map.

body: Two-Spirit, Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender and Queer Advisory Committee

brief: The owner of 186 Danforth Road disagrees with a city repair order. The Property Standards Committee will decide whether to keep, change, or cancel it.

brief: The owner of 2372 Midland Avenue disagrees with a city repair order. The Property Standards Committee will decide whether to keep, change, or cancel it.

brief: Council votes on refusing a big electronic roof sign at 2 College Street. The sign is banned outside the Dundas Square area and would be 18 times bigger than the rules allow.
stake: About signs. Decided by a recorded vote, 20 in favour and 3 against — every member's position is public.

brief: Council votes on refusing a big electronic ground sign at 3 Bestobell Road, where third-party signs are banned.

brief: Council votes on refusing a big electronic ground sign at 496 Evans Avenue, where third-party signs are banned.

title: 3807-3815 and 3819-3829 Lake Shore Boulevard West - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
brief: City Council will set its position on the appealed 39-storey, 490-home proposal for Lake Shore Boulevard West, including 14 rental replacement units.

title: Maniza Road - Parking Restrictions - Referral of item NY23.28 from Toronto City Council
brief: City Council sent proposed parking restrictions for Maniza Road back to North York Community Council for another look. The council is asked to reconsider the item.

brief: The committee will consider a new free-floating car-share program, including how it affects snow clearing and parking rules, and whether shared cars can use off-street spots for pickup and drop-off.
stake: About car sharing. Decided by a recorded vote, 22 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: City-Initiated Zoning By-law Amendment - Re-allocating Section 37 Funds within Ward 23 - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Staff suggest a city-led rule change to move $674,905.89 in unspent community benefit money from several Ward 23 building approvals to nearby capital projects. No new building is proposed; city council decides.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $674,905.89.

title: Review of Automated Speed Enforcement (ASE) Ticket Appeals Process
brief: A councillor wants Court Services to review how people fight speed camera tickets, which residents say is confusing, and suggest fixes by October 2025.

title: 2335 St. Clair Avenue West - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision - Approval
topics: zoning bylaw amendments, residential real estate
brief: City Council will vote on an 11-storey building with 72 homes at 2335 St. Clair Avenue West.

title: 126 Bellamy Road North -  Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: zoning bylaw amendments, residential real estate
brief: Council votes on changing zoning rules to allow a new eight-storey building with 184 homes at 126 Bellamy Road North, keeping the existing 16-storey tower and adding a new public park.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Toronto Atmospheric Fund Board
brief: The committee recommends 3 candidates for council to appoint to the Toronto Atmospheric Fund Board, for terms ending October 11, 2029. Candidate details are kept private.

title: 2950 Birchmount Road and 3600 Finch Avenue East Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Council votes on changing zoning rules to allow a 12-storey building at 2950 Birchmount Road and 3600 Finch Avenue East, with 356 homes and ground-floor shops and offices.

title: 1304-1318 King Street West and 143, 143a and 145 Cowan Avenue - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City Council will vote on tearing down 8 rental homes at 1304-1318 King Street West and 143 Cowan Avenue, on condition the owner builds 8 replacement rental units and helps current tenants. If the owner fails to finish the new building on time, a $20,000.00 charge per unit would be added to the property tax bill.

title: Assumption of Services, Registered Plan 66M-2378, Malvern (McLevin) Subdivision - Pinery Trail
brief: The city would take over the roads and underground pipes in the Malvern (McLevin) subdivision, also called Pinery Trail, built under a 2001 deal. The city's guarantee would be released; council is asked to approve.

title: Lane Designation - Kipling Avenue at Steeles Avenue West
brief: City Council will vote on marking the northbound curb lane of Kipling Avenue south of Steeles Avenue West as right-turn-only, except for buses.

title: York Mills Road and Ness Drive - All-Way Stop Control
brief: The pedestrian crossover on York Mills Road near Ness Drive would be replaced with all-way stop signs. City Council approval is needed because the TTC runs transit on York Mills Road.

title: York Mills Road and Upjohn Road - Traffic Control Signals
brief: Traffic signals are proposed for York Mills Road and Upjohn Road to improve safety. City Council approval is needed because the TTC runs transit on York Mills Road.

title: 564-580 Evans Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment - Adding a Holding Provision
brief: This is procedural: City Council will vote on moving a leftover approval condition into a holding provision for the approved Evans Avenue development with a seniors' residence, townhouses and four towers.

title: 875 The Queensway - Class 4 Noise Area Classification (NPC-300)
brief: City Council will vote on designating 875 The Queensway a Class 4 Noise Area, recognizing noise from nearby commercial and industrial uses.

title: Toronto Fire Services 2024 Annual Report
topics: annual reports, fire and rescue services
brief: The Toronto Fire Services 2024 annual report is presented, and council receives it for information.

title: 3138 Bayview Avenue - Zoning Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Staff recommend approving five three-storey townhouses at 3138 Bayview Avenue, each with one parking space. City Council is asked to change the zoning to allow them.

title: 40, 42, 44, 46 and 48 Hendon Avenue - Official Plan Amendment, Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Staff recommend approving an 11-storey, 148-home building at 40-48 Hendon Avenue. City Council is asked to approve the planning changes.

title: 1648-1664 Dupont Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City Council will vote on zoning changes for an 11-storey building with 163 homes and shops at 1648-1664 Dupont Street, extending a 2024 approval to cover 1648 Dupont Street.

title: 824 Sheppard Avenue West and 181 Cocksfield Avenue - Construction Staging Area
brief: The builder of a 12-storey residential building at 824 Sheppard Avenue West and 181 Cocksfield Avenue wants to temporarily use the road for construction. City Council approval is needed because the TTC runs transit on Sheppard Avenue West.

title: 1149 and 1153 Queen Street West - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
brief: City Council will vote on directing the city lawyer to oppose, at a provincial tribunal, a developer's appeal for a 27-storey, 367-home building at 1149 and 1153 Queen Street West, while discussions continue.

title: 4949 Bathurst Street - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Staff recommend approving a 26-storey mixed-use building at 4949 Bathurst Street, scaled down from 39 storeys, with shops, offices, a daycare and homes. City Council is asked to approve the zoning change.

title: 6 Foxdale Court - Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Staff recommend approving six two-storey houses at 6 Foxdale Court, with 12 parking spaces, through a future condominium plan. City Council is asked to approve the zoning change.

title: 2, 4 and 80 Union Street - Official Plan and Zoning  By-law Amendment - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, by-laws, official plan amendments, rezoning
brief: City Council will vote on directing the city lawyer to oppose, at a provincial tribunal, a developer's appeal for three 39-to-49-storey towers at 2, 4 and 80 Union Street, while discussions continue.

title: 135 St. Clair Avenue West - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City Council will vote on zoning changes to allow a 49-storey building with 576 homes at 135 St. Clair Avenue West, with a walkway linking Foxbar Road and Avenue Road.

title: Intention to Expand the Riverside District Business Improvement Area
topics: business improvement areas, polling, public opinion polls
brief: An intent to expand the Riverside District Business Improvement Area would be stated by council, with the City Clerk polling local businesses on support.

title: Bloem Avenue - Turn Prohibition
brief: City Council will vote on banning southbound right turns from Dufferin Street onto Bloem Avenue on weekday afternoons, 3:30 to 6:30 p.m., to cut speeding and near-misses on the small residential street.

title: 27 Grosvenor Street and 26 Grenville Street - Zoning By-law Amendment and Amendment to Section 37 Agreement
brief: City Council will vote on updating the deal for a two-tower project at 27 Grosvenor Street and 26 Grenville Street: fewer one-bedroom but new studio affordable rentals, a longer 99-year affordability period, and a relocated child care centre.

title: 307 Sherbourne Street - Construction Staging Area
brief: City Council will vote on closing the east sidewalk and northbound bike lane on Sherbourne Street near Gerrard Street East for eight months, with detours for walkers and cyclists, for an 18-storey student residence at 307 Sherbourne Street.

title: 425 Bloor Street West - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City Council will vote on zoning changes to allow a 30-storey building with 472 homes and shops at 425 Bloor Street West, with parkland provided at another nearby site.

title: Milner Avenue and Executive Court/Mid-Dominion Acres - Pedestrian Crossing Protection
brief: Staff checked Milner Avenue at Executive Court and do not suggest a marked crossing, and also say crossings should not be banned there. Since buses run on Milner Avenue, City Council must vote on the staff recommendation.
stake: About pedestrian crossovers. Decided by a recorded vote, 22 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: Improving the Speed and Reliability of the 7 Bathurst
topics: parking regulations, public transit, traffic regulations, transportation
brief: City Council will vote on longer no-stopping hours on the east side of Bathurst Street and new turn bans at Davenport Road and Dupont Street, to keep 7 Bathurst buses moving through congestion. The changes would cost about $30,000, paid from the TTC's capital budget.
stake: About parking regulations. Decided by a recorded vote, 20 in favour and 3 against — every member's position is public.

title: 15 Toronto Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: by-laws, official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning
brief: City Council will vote on zoning changes to allow a 56-storey building with 394 homes at 15 Toronto Street, including about 13 social housing units and street-level shops.

title: Temporary Amendments to Traffic and Parking Regulations and Transit Priority Measures to Support Transit Diversions during the Queen Street East Closures
topics: parking regulations, traffic, traffic regulations, transportation
brief: City Council will vote on temporary traffic and parking changes on Queen Street East from October 2025 to May 2026 during watermain and streetcar track work, plus transit priority measures on Dundas Street East. The report also lists a $3.00 rate.

title: Sheppard Avenue East, at a point 130 metres east of Allanford Road - Traffic Control Signals
brief: Staff suggest replacing the pedestrian island on Sheppard Avenue East, 130 metres east of Allanford Road, with full traffic lights for safer crossings. Since buses run there, this needs a City Council vote.

title: Dupont by the Castle Business Improvement Area Minor Boundary Expansion
topics: business improvement associations, office real estate
brief: The Dupont by the Castle Business Improvement Area boundary would expand slightly to include the commercial property at 1100 Bathurst Street, if council agrees.

title: 26 Laing Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City Council will vote on zoning changes for a 14-storey building with 170 homes and shops, plus a four-storey townhouse block, at 26 Laing Street.

title: 2323-2329 and 2345 Yonge Street - Official Plan Amendment Application and 2323-2329 Yonge Street Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning bylaws
brief: City Council will vote on zoning changes for a 65-storey, 784-home building at 2323-2329 Yonge Street, with affordable housing at this site and 2345 Yonge Street instead of replacement offices.

title: Call to Order

brief: This is a routine item: council checks the written record of its July 23 and 24, 2025, meeting and confirms it is correct. No new decision is asked for.

title: Introduction of Committee Reports, New Business and Business Previously Requested from the Mayor and City Officials
brief: This is a routine item: committee leaders and city staff introduce reports and new business. Council only hears them now; no decision is asked for.

stake: A citywide decision. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Petitions
brief: This is a routine item: councillors may hand in petitions from residents to be recorded. No decision is asked for.
stake: A citywide decision. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Presentations, Introductions and Announcements
brief: This is a routine item: the meeting includes presentations, introductions, and announcements. Council only listens; no decision is asked for.
stake: A citywide decision. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

brief: This is a routine item: council looks over the order paper, the list of topics for this meeting. No decision is asked for.

brief: The owner of 1117 Queen Street West appealed council's refusal of heritage alteration permits. The City Solicitor asks council for private directions. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: 1117 Queen Street West - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The owner of 1117 Queen Street West appealed council's refusal of planning and zoning amendments. The City Solicitor asks council for private directions. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: Washburn Way - Traffic Safety Improvement
brief: Staff suggest safety changes on Washburn Way, including lowering the speed limit from 40 to 30 km/h and adding speed cushions. The ideas come from a Malvern West streets plan; since buses run there, this needs a City Council vote.

topics: assessment, finance (sc), financial write-offs, property taxes, taxes
financial write offs, levies, municipal taxes
brief: City Council will vote on writing off $824,656 in uncollectible property taxes across 13 accounts; source documents also list $1,893,544 and $3,492,998.47.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $824,656.

title: Amendment to Purchase Order Number 6053584 to Crestline Coach Ltd., for the Provision of a Ministry of Health Certified Multi-Patient Ambulance for Toronto Paramedic Services
topics: ambulances, city vehicles, emergency medical services, paramedics, purchasing

stake: The official summary names a figure of $2,406,813.

title: 4913 Bathurst Street - Designation of a Portion of the Property used by the Toronto Public Library as a Municipal Capital Facility
topics: libraries, library branches, municipal facilities, property (sc), taxes
brief: City Council will vote on a tax exemption for the temporary Centennial library branch location at 4913 Bathurst Street.

title: Status of Outstanding Payments in Lieu of Tax Amounts for Federal, Provincial and Municipal Properties
topics: finance (sc), municipal services, payment, property (sc), taxes
brief: City Council will receive an update showing $1,188,452 in payments in lieu of taxes still outstanding from government properties for 2024.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $1,188,452.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Ontario Medical Supply Inc., for the Supply and Delivery of Pharmaceuticals for Toronto Paramedic Services
topics: contracts, emergency medical services, paramedics, suppliers
brief: City Council will vote on a $1,500,000 ($1,526,400 net of HST recoveries) one-year Ontario Medical Supply pharmaceuticals contract for paramedics; source documents also list $500,000.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $1,500,000.

title: 115 Broadway Avenue - Below Market Sublease Agreement with Macaulay Centres for Children For Child Care Services
topics: child care, child care facilities, community & life (sc), leasing, properties (real estate)
brief: City Council will vote on a ten-year nominal sublease with Macaulay Centres for Children for a new child care centre at 115 Broadway Avenue.

title: Expropriation of Property Interests near St. Clair West Station for the Fire Ventilation Upgrade Project - Stage 2
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, expropriations, land acquisition, properties (real estate), subway stations
brief: City Council will vote on expropriating easements at 396 St. Clair Avenue West for a fire ventilation room at St. Clair West Station.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Vermeer Canada Incorporated for the Provision of Proprietary Original Equipment Manufacturer Parts and Service for Parks and Recreation
brief: City Council will vote on a $30,009 ($30,528 net of HST recoveries) one-year Vermeer equipment parts contract, up to $194,408 ($197,830 net of HST recoveries) with extensions; source documents also list $500,000.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $30,009.

title: Micromobility Update
topics: city initiatives, personal mobility devices, public education
brief: Council will get an update on e-scooters and other small electric vehicles, covering their benefits, risks to people on foot, and the need for clear rules.
stake: About city initiatives. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 23 in favour, none against.

title: 21-31 Windsor Street, 18 Buckingham Street, 60 Newcastle Street and 95 Portland Street - Designation of a Municipal Shelter as a Municipal Capital Facility
brief: Council votes on a by-law for the new shelter building at 21-31 Windsor Street, which will replace the Elisa House women's shelter with 36 supportive homes, 32 emergency beds and 72 shelter beds. About $88,000 in building permit fees would also be waived.

title: 87 Ethel Avenue and 2595 St. Clair Avenue West - Fee Removal for Lifting of Hold Applications
brief: City Council will vote on waiving fees to lift holding provisions at two Ward 5 housing sites, 87 Ethel Avenue and 2595 St. Clair Avenue West, planned for nearly 2,000 homes including 141 affordable units.

title: Administrative Penalty Tribunal Chair's 2024 Annual Report
brief: City Council will receive the Administrative Penalty Tribunal's 2024 annual report on parking violation dispute hearings.

title: Review and Renewal of Technology Maintenance Contracts for Sustainment of City Services from 2026 - 2030
topics: contracts, infrastructure, maintenance, purchasing, science & technology (sc)
brief: City Council will vote on renewing 219 technology maintenance contracts non-competitively for 2026-2030; source documents list $14.56 million, $500,000, $226,894,541, $230,887,885, $16,750,326 and $17,045,132.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $14.56 million.

title: 1151 Weston Road - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: Council votes on starting heritage protection for the 1949 Bank of Nova Scotia building at 1151 Weston Road in Mount Dennis.

title: 85 Hanna Avenue and 109 Atlantic Avenue - Official Plan Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Council votes on changing 85 Hanna Avenue and 109 Atlantic Avenue from job lands to mixed-use, so any future rebuild must include affordable rental homes and work space.

title: 134 Carlton Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: Council votes on starting heritage protection for the LaVerne Apartments at 134 Carlton Street, built in 1926.

title: 506, 510, and 512 Jarvis Street - Notice of Intention to Designate Properties under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: Council votes on starting heritage protection for three old houses at 506, 510 and 512 Jarvis Street.

title: Property Included on the City's Heritage Register - Consideration of Objection for 1771 Bayview Avenue and 36 Green Valley Road
brief: Council decides whether to keep 1771 Bayview Avenue and 36 Green Valley Road on the city's Heritage Register, despite the owners' objections.

title: 207, 209, 211, 213, 215, 217 and 219 Jarvis Street - Notice of Intention to Designate Properties under   Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: Council votes on starting heritage protection for seven old buildings at 207 to 219 Jarvis Street in Moss Park.

title: 336, 340, and 342-344 Jarvis Street - Notice of Intention to Designate Properties under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: Council votes on starting heritage protection for three old buildings at 336, 340 and 342-344 Jarvis Street.

title: Open and Accessible In-Person Public Transit Oriented Community Open Houses
brief: Council asks Infrastructure Ontario to hold all Transit Oriented Community meetings in person, after residents asked for face-to-face answers about the Ontario Line.

title: Green Lane Landfill Renewable Natural Gas Project Update
brief: The committee will get an update on turning Green Lane Landfill gas into renewable natural gas with Enbridge Gas, which no longer wants to proceed. Staff will look at other options.

title: Transferring Secretary Role for Dangerous Dog Review Tribunal and Property Standards Committee to Court Services
brief: Council would move the secretary job for the Dangerous Dog Review Tribunal and the Property Standards Committee from the City Clerk to Court Services starting Jan. 1, 2026, along with two staff and $0.209 million gross ($0.169 million net) in budget funding.

title: Amendments to Zoning By-law 569-2013 relating to Accessible and Bicycle Parking Requirements for New Development
topics: accessible permit parking, bicycle parking, change, zoning bylaws
brief: Council votes on minor fixes to the city-wide rules for accessible parking and bike parking at new developments. No real policy change.

title: Appointment of Public Members and Tenant Directors to the Toronto Seniors Housing Corporation Board of Directors
brief: This is a procedural item: a city panel is asked to recommend five public members and two tenant directors to council for the Toronto Seniors Housing Corporation board, and to recommend one as chair. No new rules here.

title: Tree Maintenance Review Update 2025
topics: city-owned trees, privately-owned trees, tree maintenance
trees on public property, private owned trees
brief: Staff would start moving tree maintenance from contractors to City crews, aiming for an even split, following the Auditor General's advice, if council agrees.
stake: About city-owned trees. Decided by a recorded vote, 22 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: Creating a Small Business Friendly Approach to Licensing and Permitting
brief: A request that staff report in October 2025 on a more business-friendly, compliance-focused approach to small business licensing and permits goes to council.
stake: About business licences. Council sent it back for more work.

title: Western Beaches Breakwaters Action Plan Progress Update
brief: Council would have staff work with the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority on repairs and funding for high-risk breakwaters along the western beaches, from the Humber River to Ontario Place, and report back in spring 2026.

title: Advancing Affordable Rental Housing in Quayside -Phase 1
brief: Council would approve a deal to speed up building affordable rental homes in the first phase of the Quayside waterfront neighbourhood at Queens Quay East and Parliament, working with Waterfront Toronto and a private partner. The report cites a $975 million figure and a $500,000 figure.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $975 million.

title: Capital Variance Report for the Six Months Ended June 30, 2025
topics: annual reports, capital budgets, financial reports
brief: Staff report the city's big-project spending for the first half of 2025 was $1.850 billion, or 29.6 percent of the approved budget, and forecast year-end totals. Council would approve adjustments to the approved capital budget and plan.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $1.850 billion.

title: Operating Variance Report for the Six Months Ended June 30, 2025
topics: annual reports, financial reports, operating budgets
brief: Council would approve 2025 day-to-day budget changes that do not change the net budget, and update benefit plans for staff and elected officials retiring on or after Nov. 1, 2025. The report cites figures of $31.7 million, $105.4 million, $19.0 million and $44.4 million.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $31.7 million.

title: Deferred Revenue (Obligatory Reserve Funds), Reserves and Discretionary Reserve Funds as at June 30, 2025
topics: financial reports, reserve funds, revenue generation
financial statements, reserves and reserve funds, revenue tools
brief: Council would move $8 million from waste reserves to the Green Lane landfill reserve, and about $80.1 million into a reserve that steadies land transfer tax revenue when the housing market is slow. The report cites figures of $6,728.9 million, $7,514.7 million, $785.8 million, $70.8 million, $5,610.6 million, $5,681.4 million, $5,454.1 million, $227.3 million, $18,849.1 million, $41,066.7 million, $13,196.1 million, $8 million and $80.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $6,728.9 million.

title: Toronto Parking Authority - State of Good Repair Program
brief: City Council will consider the Toronto Parking Authority's state-of-good-repair strategy; source documents list $280 million, $20.17 million, $15.38 million, $12.6 million, $128 million and $152 million.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $280 million.

title: Harbord/Hoskin Reconstruction
brief: The item asks City staff about road construction delays on Harbord and Hoskin Streets, where the road was dug up again through most of 2025 after watermain work finished.
stake: About road reconstruction. Council sent it back for more work.

title: Toronto Parking Authority 2024 Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) Report
topics: community development, environment (sc), governance, parking authorities
brief: Council would take the Toronto Parking Authority's first report on its environmental and social work for information. It describes the agency's green efforts. No policy change is proposed.
stake: About community development. Decided by a recorded vote, 19 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: Proposed Incentive Pilot Programs to Collect and Manage Stormwater on Private Property in Support of Climate Resilience
topics: climate change, pilot projects, stormwater management
brief: Approval of two pilot programs for managing rainwater at home: discounted rain barrels and downspout diverters for one year, and cash back for rain gardens for three years is before council.

title: Toronto Water 2025 Capital Budget and 2026-2034 Capital Plan Adjustments
brief: Council would move money within Toronto Water's budget and 10-year plan: $38.7 million in timing shifts and $7.9 million from under-budget or finished projects to ones needing more. The total budget stays the same. The report cites figures of $38 and $7.

title: Ookwemin Minising Implementation Update
brief: Council would let Waterfront Toronto run a contest to pick a building partner for the first homes-and-shops development on Ookwemin Minising, the new Port Lands island. Staff will help with the call. The three governments announced $975 million for the island's revitalization.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $975 million.

title: Establishing a Community Safety Zone on Dovercourt Road, between College Street and Dundas Street West
brief: City Council will vote on making Dovercourt Road between College Street and Dundas Street West a Community Safety Zone with higher speeding fines, on a route linking families to schools, a daycare, a YMCA and parks.

title: Kingston Road - Community Safety Zone
brief: A councillor suggests creating a Community Safety Zone on both sides of Kingston Road between Valhalla Boulevard and Birchmount Road, where groups raised traffic safety concerns. The label would allow speed cameras in the area; council is asked to approve.

title: Wellington Street Loading Zone
brief: City Council will vote on moving a 15-minute loading zone used by 1Hotel back to its original spot on Wellington Street near Bathurst Street, after the temporary spot caused snow-clearing and traffic problems.
stake: Ward 10 is named in the record.

title: 505 University Avenue - Demolition of a Designated Heritage Property under Section 34(1)2 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Request for Directions
topics: demolitions, heritage properties, property (sc), zoning, zoning bylaws
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about demolishing the heritage Shell Oil Building at 505 University Avenue for a 64-storey building with 704 homes. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: 2490-2515 Yonge Street, 10 - 20 Castlefield Avenue, 565 - 567 Duplex Avenue - Development Charges Complaint - Request for Directions

title: Fare Collection Update

brief: The Board gets an update on the TTC's fare-collection deal with Metrolinx, which ends in November 2027. It is asked to approve recommendations kept private until final talks are done.

title: Authorization for Payment of Additional Legal Expense relating to Integrity Commissioner’s Report of July 7, 2025 - by Chair Jamaal Myers, seconded by Vice-Chair Joe Mihevc
brief: Approving paying $2,589.08 to a law firm for Chair Myers's legal costs from an Integrity Commissioner investigation. It goes to the TTC Board for approval. The Board had agreed to cover up to $5000 each; his invoice was $6,716.00, or $7,589.08 with tax.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $5000.

title: Approved Minutes of the Advisory Committee on Accessible Transit (ACAT) General Monthly Meeting of August 28, 2025
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, accessibility, specialized paratransit services
brief: This is routine business. The accessible transit advisory committee sends its approved August 28, 2025 meeting notes to the TTC Board for information. No decision is needed.
stake: About Toronto Transit Commission. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: TTC Wayfinding Strategy
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, bus stops, streetcar stops, subway stations, wayfinding
brief: TTC staff want the Board to approve a new wayfinding plan with better signs, maps and digital tools, plus a first-year plan and a 10-year roadmap. The report cites a $210 million figure.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $173.

title: Audit, Risk and Compliance - 2025 Audit Plan Status Update - IT Disaster Recovery
brief: This is routine business. The TTC Board is asked to receive the IT disaster recovery audit report and keep the details private, since they cover security of TTC systems.

title: Chief Executive Officer’s Report - October 2025
brief: This is routine business. The TTC Board receives the CEO's October 2025 report for information. No decision is needed.
stake: About Toronto Transit Commission. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Foundations of Inclusive Governance
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, accessibility, equity, human rights, racial discrimination
brief: This is routine business. The TTC Board gets training on inclusive governance in a private session and is asked to approve releasing the training materials publicly.

title: Naming of the Leslie Barns Carhouse  - by Chair Jamaal Myers, seconded by Commissioner Josh Matlow
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, garages, public transit
brief: Chair Myers asks the TTC Board to name the Leslie Barns carhouse after former mayor David Miller, who helped secure $1 billion over five years for the TTC. The Board would vote on the naming.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $1 billion.

title: Publicly Honouring the Service and Contributions of Veterans
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, bus stops, ceremonies, streetcar stops, subway stations
brief: Approving planning 2026 programs honouring veterans, like station displays, digital stories and public art. It goes to the TTC Board for approval. A digital tribute launches in October 2025 through Remembrance Day week.

title: 150 Eighth Street - Education Development Charges Complaint
brief: The Canadian Helen Keller Centre wants a $184,408.00 refund of school development fees for its 56-unit affordable housing project at 150 Eighth Street. Council would take the report for information.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $184,408.00. Council sent it back for more work.

title: Efforts to Improve End-to-End Customer Experience
topics: customer service, information and communication technology, non emergency municipal services
brief: Council would have city divisions report back by spring 2026 with a step-by-step plan to simplify 311 service requests, starting with parks by making request types clearer and combining similar codes.

title: 2025 Listening to Toronto Survey
topics: customer satisfaction surveys, non emergency municipal services
brief: Staff report the results of the 2025 Listening to Toronto survey by Ipsos, covering how happy residents are with city services and quality of life. For information only.

title: Transition of the Blue Box Program to Extended Producer Responsibility - Post-Transition Communications Strategy
topics: blue bin materials, city initiatives, solid waste
brief: The committee will get the City's plan for telling residents about Blue Box recycling changes before and after the program shifts to producer responsibility on January 1, 2026.

title: Proposed 2026 Schedule of Toronto Investment Board Meetings
brief: The Board will approve its 2026 meeting dates: March 23, June 22, September 28, and December 14, held both at City Hall and online.

title: 1555 Danforth Avenue: Jurisdictional Transfer and Park Naming
brief: The committee will get a report on the steps to hand the green space at 1555 Danforth Avenue to Parks and Recreation and name it Coxwell Commons.

title: Response to Information Request Related to Solid Waste Trucks for IE22.5 - Authorized Vehicles in Parks Report
topics: heavy trucks, park maintenance, parks, parks and open space areas, solid waste, solid waste management, trucks
brief: The committee will get details on how many garbage trucks drive on park grass in 186 parks and what fixing the grass costs: about $500 for a minor repair, $1000 for a medium one, and $2500 or more for a large one.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $500.

title: Feasibility of Pedestrian Priority Phase at Yonge Street and Eglinton Avenue
topics: pedestrian infrastructure, pedestrian priority phase, signalized intersections
brief: Council will get a study on a pedestrian scramble at Yonge and Eglinton, with staff recommending against building it even though foot traffic seemed high enough.
stake: About pedestrian infrastructure. Council sent it back for more work.

title: Update on the City’s Long-term Residual Waste Management Work Plan
topics: public consultation, solid waste management, work plans
public hearing, solid waste management planning
brief: The committee will get an update on talks about long-term garbage options, like burning waste for energy versus landfills, with staff returning for direction in 2027.

title: Presentations from Investment Managers
brief: The Board will hear presentations on two global stock funds run by Fiera Capital and its partners.
stake: About investment. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Investment Consultant Contract - Option to Extend
brief: The Board will extend its consultant contract with Aon for two more years and let the Chair or Vice-Chair sign it. The evaluation stays private.
stake: About investment. Council put off deciding this item.

title: Review of Investment Manager Mandate (Global Equity)
brief: The Board will keep private a detailed look at a global stock investment contract that its consultant Aon will present and discuss.
stake: About investment. Council put off deciding this item.

title: Sinking Fund and Long Term Fund - Performance and Compliance Update for the Second Quarter 2025
brief: The Board will hear how two City investment funds did in mid-2025 and whether they followed the investment rules.

title: Environmental, Social, and Governance Reporting Update
brief: The Board will keep four private ESG reporting documents secret, covering checks on how outside money managers handle environmental and social issues.

title: Investment Manager and Other Updates
brief: The Board will get an update on fund transfers made in July 2025 and fund balances at the end of July.

title: Implementation of a Permanent Memorial Program Utilizing Engraved Steel Braces on Utility Poles
brief: A councillor wants staff to study whether the City could offer permanent roadside memorials, like engraved metal braces on utility poles, for traffic crash victims, and report back by early 2026.

title: Status Update for 2025.MM26.12 - Study of Redesign Options to Address the High Level of Congestion and Neighbourhood Traffic at the Intersection of Eglinton Avenue West and the Allen Expressway
brief: A councillor wants transportation staff to give an update by October 2025 on redesign options for the busy Eglinton Avenue West and Allen Expressway intersection.

title: Planning for Future Servicing Needs in a Growing City

refuse, industrial real estate, local transit
brief: A councillor wants a rule that no City work yard can be changed or closed without first checking whether the yards can support the needs of all City teams, now and later.

title: Comprehensive Review of the Sign By-law and Establishing a Port Lands Special Sign District
brief: The Planning and Housing Committee asks staff to review the city's sign rules and study a special sign district for the Port Lands, with a report due by mid-2027.

title: Procurement Policy Updates - Adoption of the Mayor's Economic Action Plan to United States Tariffs
body: Toronto Parking Authority - Audit and Risk Management Committee
brief: The Toronto Parking Authority board votes on updating its buying rules to match the Mayor's Economic Action Plan in response to U.S. tariffs.

title: Delegation of Authority Update: June 2 - August 31, 2025
body: Toronto Parking Authority - Audit and Risk Management Committee
brief: This is a routine item: the Toronto Parking Authority board receives an update on decisions made under delegated authority from June 2 to August 31, 2025. The President can commit up to $500,000 and award non-competitive contracts up to $250,000. No policy change.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $250,000.

title: Cyber Security Update
body: Toronto Parking Authority - Audit and Risk Management Committee
brief: The Toronto Parking Authority board hears a private update on its cyber security. Details stay secret because they involve the security of city property.

title: Major Transit Station Areas and Protected Major Transit Stations Areas and Inclusionary Zoning Implementation - Status Update and Work Plan

stake: The official summary names a figure of $471.1 million.

title: Summary of Legal Disputes Update
body: Toronto Parking Authority - Audit and Risk Management Committee
brief: The Toronto Parking Authority board votes on keeping its legal disputes update secret, since it contains court advice covered by lawyer-client privilege.

title: Toronto Parking Authority - 2026 Operating Budget and 2026-2028 Capital Budget
body: Toronto Parking Authority - Audit and Risk Management Committee

Forecasts: net income $45.5 million, EBITDA $57.9 million, revenue $177.3 million, operating expenses $119.4 million, plus figures of $3.6 million, $2.9 million, $5.4 million, $1.6 million, $2.4 million and $52.6 million. stake: The official summary names a figure of $45.5 million.

brief: This is a routine item: the Toronto Parking Authority board receives its financial results for the first eight months of 2025, with net income of $34.7 million. The report cites revenue of $118.8 million, operating costs of $76.3 million, $23.6 million invested in capital projects, a $51.9 million capital plan, $20.8 million in city Bike Share funding, and figures of $5.6 million, $3.9 million, $0.6 million, $9.9 million, $1.7 million, $1.1 million, $3.5 million, $2.4 million, $10.1 million, $2.8 million, $44 million, $47 million, $2 million and $5 million. stake: The official summary names a figure of $34.7 million.
