title: 2026 Schedule of Meetings
brief: The board sets its 2026 meeting schedule, avoiding conflicts with council meetings and days of cultural or religious importance. No rule change is proposed.
stake: About committee meetings. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: 15 Toronto Street - Demolition of a Building Within the St. Lawrence Neighbourhood Heritage Conservation District and Approval of a Replacement Building
brief: Recommending that council approve tearing down the 11-storey building at 15 Toronto Street in the St. Lawrence heritage district, and approve a replacement design. It goes to the board for a decision.

title: 120 Bloor Street East and 1286 Bloor Street West - Inclusion on the Heritage Register
brief: Adding 120 Bloor Street East and 1286 Bloor Street West to the city's Heritage Register. It goes to the board for a decision. Listing requires notice before any demolition.

title: 1151 Weston Road - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: The board votes on whether to recommend starting heritage protection for 1151 Weston Road. Starting designation would limit future demolition and changes to the property.

title: 134 Carlton Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: The board votes on whether to recommend starting heritage protection for 134 Carlton Street. Starting designation would limit future demolition and changes to the property.

title: Property Included on the City's Heritage Register - Consideration of Objection for 1771 Bayview Avenue and 36 Green Valley Road
brief: The owners of 1771 Bayview Avenue and 36 Green Valley Road object to their properties being on the Heritage Register. The board is asked to review the objections and recommend whether the listings should stay.

title: 4200 Eglinton Avenue West- Demolition of a Heritage Attribute under Section 34 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Approval with Conditions
brief: Recommending that council approve tearing down the stone wall and gate posts at the protected heritage property at 4200 Eglinton Avenue West, with conditions. It goes to the board for a decision.

title: Proposed 2026 Meeting Schedule for Toronto Preservation Board
brief: A routine item: the board is asked to approve its 2026 meeting schedule.

title: Coliseum Complex Walkways, Driveways, and Masonry Rehabilitation
brief: The board would agree with an earlier approval of an $883,000.00 contract to Clifford Restoration for walkway, driveway, and masonry repairs at the Coliseum Complex, won by the lowest qualified bidder. The report also cites $65,000.00.

title: Agreement with the Festival Management Corporation for the Toronto Caribbean Carnival 2025
topics: Exhibition Place, agreements, festivals and special events
brief: The board would agree with an earlier approval of a one-year deal for the 2025 Caribbean Carnival Grand Parade on August 2, 2025, on the same terms as 2024.

title: Lighting Upgrade at the Princes' Gates and Automotive Building
brief: The board would agree with an earlier approval of a $341,419.00 contract to Rogul Electric for lighting upgrades at the Princes' Gates and Automotive Building, won by the lowest qualified bidder. The report also cites $30,000.00.

title: Business Travel GSX - Global Security Exchange Conference
topics: Exhibition Place, business travel (municipal), expenses, travel
brief: The board would approve travel costs of up to $5,100 plus tax for security manager Vasilis Androutsos to attend a security conference in New Orleans in late September 2025.

title: Response to Demonstrations Policy

brief: The board would approve its Response to Demonstrations Policy, written to match council's December 2024 policy on how the city responds to protests.

brief: Staff report a full financial summary of all Exhibition Place programs for the second quarter of 2025. The board just receives it, keeping the private attachment private.

title: 1693, 1695 and 1705-1709 Weston Road and 10 Victoria Avenue East - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City Council will vote on a 43-storey, 599-home tower on Weston Road with 15 rental replacement and six affordable rental units, and on setting $1,076.00 per reduced long-term bike parking space as the cash-in-lieu rate.

title: 4231, 4237 and 4241 Dundas Street West, Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City Council will vote on an 11-storey building with 318 homes and ground-floor shops at 4231-4241 Dundas Street West.

title: 4610 Finch Avenue East - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City staff suggest changing zoning rules to allow a 13-storey building at 4610 Finch Avenue East with a 378-bed long-term care home, an ambulance base, and medical offices.
stake: About long term care homes. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 22 in favour, none against.

title: 1410 Eglinton Avenue West - Zoning By-law Amendment - Appeal Report
brief: A 43-storey, 442-home building is proposed at 1410 Eglinton Avenue West. The applicant appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal, and North York Community Council is asked to have the City Solicitor oppose the appeal.

title: Association of Community Centres Settlement of Operating Results for Year Ended 2023
topics: community associations, community centres, operating budgets
brief: Council would settle the 2023 results of ten community centres: $137,646 in surpluses from two centres would partly cover $539,724 in deficits at seven centres, leaving $402,078 for the city to pay.

title: 240-242 Finch Avenue West - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Staff recommend approving a four-storey rental building with 41 homes at 240-242 Finch Avenue West. City Council is asked to change the zoning to allow it.

title: 47 Stadacona Drive and 22, 24, 26 and 28 Richelieu Road - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Staff recommend approving a 12-storey building with 190 homes and shops at 47 Stadacona Drive and 22-28 Richelieu Road, including 13 replacement rental units. City Council is asked to approve the zoning change.
stake: Ward 6 is named in the record.

title: 36 South Station Street - Residential Demolition Application
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve demolishing a detached house at 36 South Station Street, since no replacement building permit has been issued.

title: Keele Street and Whitburn Crescent / Downsview Park Boulevard - Traffic Control Signal Modifications
brief: Changes to the traffic signals at Keele Street and Whitburn Crescent / Downsview Park Boulevard are proposed, following a new road built for a nearby subdivision. City Council approval is needed because the TTC runs transit there.

title: 3725 Bloor Street West - City-initiated Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Council votes on a zoning change for 3725 Bloor Street West that would allow a 43-storey building with about 698 rental homes, including 230 affordable.

title: 110 Sheppard Avenue East - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Refusal
topics: Official Plans, development, official plan amendments, zoning bylaws
brief: Staff recommend refusing a plan for two towers (49 and 53 storeys, 1,313 homes) at 110 Sheppard Avenue East. Council is asked to refuse it, keeping the site's current rules.

title: 5799-5915 Yonge Street and 46 and 47 Averill Crescent - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Staff recommend approving changes at 5799-5915 Yonge Street: non-residential uses could expand above the second floor, and a 10,000-square-metre office requirement would become general non-residential space. City Council is asked to approve.

title: Dedicate Lands as Public Highway to Form Part of Esther Shiner Boulevard, Provost Drive, and McMahon Drive
brief: A technical item: land along Esther Shiner Boulevard, Provost Drive and McMahon Drive would be formally marked as public highway so the city can maintain it. City Council is asked to approve the dedication.

title: Lake Shore Boulevard West - U-Turn Prohibitions
brief: City Council will vote on banning westbound U-turns on Lake Shore Boulevard West near Legion Road.

title: Business Improvement Areas - Update on the 2023 and 2024 Audited Financial Statements
topics: audits, business improvement areas, finance (sc), financial reports
brief: Council will vote on approving the checked 2023 and 2024 financial statements for the listed Business Improvement Areas, which got clean audit opinions. Six got minor tips to improve their controls.

title: 123 Garratt Boulevard (Taxiway West District) - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Staff recommend approving a large mixed-use project at 123 Garratt Boulevard: about 2,957 homes (10 percent affordable rental), shops and offices, plus new parks and streets. City Council is asked to approve the zoning change.

title: 2674-2704 Yonge Street and 19 Alexandra Boulevard - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Staff recommend approving a 13-storey seniors residence with 251 units at 2674-2704 Yonge Street and 19 Alexandra Boulevard, with 31 rental replacement units and a tenant assistance plan. City Council is asked to approve. The item also references $950,000.00.
stake: About buildings. Decided by a recorded vote, 21 in favour and 2 against — every member's position is public.

title: 2 Old George Place - Alterations to a Designated Property in the North Rosedale Heritage Conservation District - Refusal
brief: Council will vote on refusing alterations to a designated property at 2 Old George Place. Staff say the proposed addition doesn't fit the heritage district's plan.

title: 101-105 Spadina Avenue and 363 Adelaide Street West - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Council will vote on a 50-storey building with 452 homes at 101-105 Spadina Avenue. The site was approved for 39 storeys in 2023.

title: 462 Wellington Street West - Class 4 Noise Area Classification (NPC-300)
brief: Council will vote on classifying 462 Wellington Street West as a Class 4 noise area. This allows higher sound limits because noise controls are built into the project.

title: 445, 447, 449 and 451 Adelaide Street West - Demolition and New Construction on Designated Heritage Properties Under Part V, Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Refusal
brief: Council will vote on refusing a heritage permit to demolish four heritage properties at 445-451 Adelaide Street West. A 17-storey hotel and restaurant building is proposed.

title: 358-360 Dufferin Street (including structure address at 350 Dufferin Street) - Alterations to and Demolition of Heritage Attributes of Designated Heritage Property under Sections 33 and 34 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
brief: Council will vote on allowing changes and partial demolition of the heritage Dominion Radiator complex at 358-360 Dufferin Street. Three mixed-use buildings are proposed.

title: Audit of the Toronto Transit Commission’s Non-Union Workforce Planning and Management
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, audits, employees, human resources
brief: This is a routine item: council is asked to accept the Auditor General's report on TTC workforce planning for non-union staff, sent by the TTC board. No new decision is proposed.

title: 6 and 8 Cawthra Square - Alterations to Heritage Properties Designated Under Part IV of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
brief: Council will vote on allowing changes to the heritage houses at 6 and 8 Cawthra Square. They would be part of a new 63-storey building.

title: 126, 128 and 130 Avenue Road - Demolition and New Construction on Designated Heritage Properties Under Part V, Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Approval
brief: Council will vote on demolishing three non-heritage-rated buildings at 126-130 Avenue Road. An 11-storey replacement building is proposed.

title: Mid-Block Pedestrian Traffic Control Signal - Lawrence Avenue East, at a point 285 metres west of Kingston Road
topics: pedestrian push-buttons, traffic signal control systems
brief: Staff suggest a mid-block pedestrian traffic light on Lawrence Avenue East, 285 metres west of Kingston Road, to make crossing safer. Since buses run there, this needs a City Council vote.

title: Our Scarborough Centre Secondary Plan Study - Status Report
brief: Staff update council on a study guiding growth around the future Scarborough Centre subway extension. Council is asked to send rule changes to a public meeting in fall 2025; no zoning change is decided here.

title: 1675 and 1685 Eglinton Avenue West - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: Official Plans, official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning bylaws
brief: City Council will vote on zoning changes to allow a 37-storey building with 424 homes, including 75 replacement rental units, plus shops at 1675 and 1685 Eglinton Avenue West. The report also lists amounts of $538 and $1,076.

title: Danforth Avenue - Removal of Taxicab Stand
brief: Council will vote on removing the taxi stand on Danforth Avenue west of Woodbine. The space would join the existing paid parking area.

title: Sheppard Avenue East and Rainbow Ridge Avenue - Traffic Control Signals
brief: Staff suggest traffic lights at Sheppard Avenue East and Rainbow Ridge Avenue to protect people crossing the road. Since buses run on Sheppard Avenue East, this needs a City Council vote.

title: Permanent Closure and Dedication of a portion of the public laneway abutting 1747 and 1753 St. Clair Avenue West
brief: Council will vote on closing part of a laneway behind 1747 and 1753 St. Clair Avenue West. The land would be sold into the adjacent development.
stake: Ward 9 is named in the record.

title: 2025 Road Openings and Closures in the Port Lands: Don Roadway and Villiers Street
brief: Council will vote on road openings and closures in the Port Lands for flood-protection work. The Don Roadway closure would extend to December 2025.

title: 276-294 Main Street - Extension of Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Council will vote on extending the land-splitting exemption at 276-294 Main Street for three more years. Remaining property transfers would be completed.

title: 21-25 Imperial Street - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Council will vote on a 19-storey building with 228 homes and retail at 21-25 Imperial Street. Two ground-level units would be live-work spaces.

title: 699-707 Yonge Street, 1-17 Hayden Street, and 8 Charles Street East - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Refusal
brief: Council will vote on refusing a 64-storey tower with 514 homes at 699-707 Yonge Street. Staff say the tower's size and heritage impacts don't fit the area's plans.

title: Kingston Road, between Midland Avenue and Brimley Road/Brimley Road South - Speed Limit Review
brief: Staff suggest lowering the speed limit from 60 to 50 km/h on Kingston Road between Midland Avenue and Brimley Road, matching the limit west of Midland Avenue. Since buses run there, this needs a City Council vote.

title: Kennedy Station Public Realm Master Plan - Final Report
brief: A long-term plan for public spaces like sidewalks, plazas, and parks around Kennedy Station would run 30-plus years. Council decides whether to adopt it; the plan responds to new transit and building in the area.

title: 126 - 130 Avenue Road -  Zoning By-law Amendment, Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Council will vote on an 11-storey building with 60 homes, including 11 rental replacement units, at 126-130 Avenue Road.

title: 20-22 Front Street West - Construction Staging Area
brief: Council will vote on closing part of Front Street West near Yonge for 65 months for construction at 20-22 Front Street West. The item lists a $5.00 fee.
stake: About construction. Council sent it back for more work.

title: Kennedy Road and Brigstock Road - Traffic Control Signal
brief: Staff suggest a traffic light at Kennedy Road and Brigstock Road, saying it is justified and would make things safer for all road users. Since buses run on Kennedy Road, this needs a City Council vote.

title: 340-376R Dufferin Street and 2 Melbourne Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Council will vote on three buildings of 29, 26 and 9 storeys with 768 homes at 340-376R Dufferin Street. Heritage properties would be conserved and a public courtyard added.

title: Sheppard Avenue East and Brownspring Road - Traffic Control Signal
brief: Staff suggest a traffic light at Sheppard Avenue East and Brownspring Road, saying it is justified and would make things safer for all road users. Since buses run on Sheppard Avenue East, this needs a City Council vote.

title: 1711-1741 Eglinton Avenue West - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws
brief: Council will vote on a 39-storey building with 427 homes at 1711-1741 Eglinton Avenue West, including 8 rental replacement units. The item lists fees of $538 and $1,076.

title: 2-12 Cawthra Square - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Council will vote on a 63-storey building with 590 homes at 2-12 Cawthra Square. It includes 14 rental replacement units and community space.

title: King Street East - Commercial Loading Zone
brief: Council will vote on a commercial loading zone on King Street East between Trinity Street and Gilead Place. The item lists a $3.00 fee.

title: Jones Avenue - Temporary Traffic and Parking By-law Amendments
brief: Council will vote on a temporary school bus loading zone on Jones Avenue. The school is relocating there for two years during Ontario Line construction.

title: Transit Priority Measures to Support Transit Diversions During King Street West and Dufferin Street Intersection Closure
brief: Council will vote on temporary transit-priority measures while the King and Dufferin intersection closes for track work. Streetcar and bus routes would be diverted.

title: 2720, 2726 and 2734 Danforth Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Council will vote on a mass-timber building with 64 rental homes, including six affordable units, at 2720-2734 Danforth Avenue. No car parking is proposed.

title: Advancing Six Sites for the Homelessness Services Capital Infrastructure Strategy (HSCIS) - City-Initiated Official Plan Amendment and Six Zoning By-law Amendments - Decision Report - Approval
topics: housing services, official plan amendments, rezoning
brief: Council votes on planning changes for six city shelter sites that would add about 420 shelter beds, from Dufferin Street to Wilson Avenue. The city's ten-year shelter infrastructure plan is estimated to cost $674.5 million.
stake: About housing services. Decided by a recorded vote, 22 in favour and 3 against — every member's position is public.

title: 53-55 Yonge Street - Construction Staging Area
brief: Council will vote on closing parts of Yonge and Colborne streets for 10 months for demolition at 53-55 Yonge Street.

title: Expanding Housing Options in Neighbourhoods - Garden Suites Monitoring Program - Final Report
brief: Council votes on easing the rules for garden suites, small homes built in backyards. The changes also line up city rules with new provincial rules.
stake: About housing. Decided by a recorded vote, 17 in favour and 3 against — every member's position is public.

title: Queen Street West Business Improvement Area Minor Boundary Expansion
topics: business improvement areas, land, land use
brief: The Queen Street West Business Improvement Area boundary would expand slightly to include the commercial property at 165 John Street, if council agrees.

title: Changes to Business Improvement Area Boards of Management
topics: business improvement areas, change, public appointments
brief: Appointing Frank Nhan to the Upper Village BIA Board and Angelo Moretti to the Uptown Yonge BIA Board, and removing directors from the Uptown Yonge board, is on council's agenda.

title: Downtown Community Outreach Response and Engagement (CORE) Program
brief: A recommendation that Council keep the downtown CORE program going past its one-year pilot goes to the Board. Public health nurses and police work together to help people in the Yonge-Dundas area facing homelessness, mental health, and substance use challenges.

title: Fraud Investigation Involving Multiple City of Toronto Electricity Accounts
brief: The Auditor General found that electricity accounts for 14 city properties were switched to outside energy sellers without the city knowing, in contracts worth about $4.2 million. The city could have lost $2.5 million; the accounts were switched back and the money was recovered.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $4.2 million.

title: Davenport Village Traffic Safety Plan - Left Turns on Foundry Avenue
brief: Council will vote on banning northbound left turns from Foundry Avenue onto Davenport Road during rush hours. The ban aims to reduce backups.

title: Appointment of Medical Officer of Health
topics: appointments, boards of health, public health
brief: The Board of Health will consider the hiring panel's choice for Toronto's next Medical Officer of Health, with the final appointment made by City Council. The candidate's name is confidential for now.

title: Toronto’s Early Years and Child Care Service Plan, 2025-2030
brief: Toronto's Early Years and Child Care Service Plan 2025-2030 goes to council for approval, along with a call on the province and federal government to recognize Indigenous rights and governance in early learning funding and co-develop an Indigenous-led plan.
stake: About child care. Decided by a recorded vote, 18 in favour and 4 against — every member's position is public.

title: Auditor General's Office - Report on the Results of Applying Specified Auditing Procedures to Financial Information Other Than Financial Statements for the Year Ended December 31, 2024
brief: This is a routine item: an outside auditor's check of the Auditor General's own 2024 office finances is being presented. No decision is requested.

title: Temporary Ramps for Stepped Entrances - Amendments to Chapter 743
brief: The streets by-law would change so shops can put temporary ramps on sidewalks, helping people who use wheelchairs enter stores with stepped doorways, if council agrees.

title: Toronto Water 2025 Capital Budget and 2026-2034 Capital Plan Adjustments
brief: Council would approve moving $15.166 million between Toronto Water projects in the 2025 budget and 10-year plan, and raise one project's approved cost by $2.514 million so work can start early. The total budget does not change. The report cites figures of $15, $2 and $1.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Toronto Community Housing Corporation Board of Directors
brief: This is a procedural item: a city panel is asked to recommend seven public members to council for the Toronto Community Housing Corporation board, and to recommend one as chair. No new rules here.

title: Joint Collection Schedule Discussions with Circular Materials
topics: blue bins, recycling collection, solid waste management
recycling pickup, solid waste management planning
brief: Staff could sign a deal with Circular Materials, the new Blue Box manager, so recycling pickup day info can appear in the City's waste schedule for up to five years, if council agrees.

title: Renaming of Balmoral Park to Michael Mostyn Park
topics: facility naming, naming, parks and open space areas
brief: Balmoral Park would be renamed Michael Mostyn Park, honouring the late community leader and human rights advocate Michael Mostyn. City Council is asked to approve the renaming.

title: Business Licence and Permit Applications Action Plan: Chapter 545, Licensing (2025 to 2029)
brief: Council would overhaul business licensing: drop four application requirements, stop licensing seven trades (boats for hire, school bus drivers, transient traders, building cleaners, chimney repairmen, fallout-shelter builders, second-hand-goods collectors), let licensing staff add conditions to licences, and require an email contact from applicants. Removed licence fees ranged from $281.87 to $758.01. A new $239.11 zoning review fee would apply. Changes start January 1, 2026.

title: Rat Response Plan
brief: The city's Rat Response Plan, focused on removing food, water and shelter for rats, would take effect if council adopts it, with rat management plans included in construction projects.

title: Audit of the City's Low Dollar Value Purchases: Increasing Efficiency and Cost Savings While Balancing Other Procurement Objectives and Maintaining Compliance
brief: The Auditor General checked small city purchases under $3,000, which are 96.5 per cent of all buying transactions. The office wants wider use of purchasing cards and a review of approval limits.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $3,000.

title: 2024 Audited Financial Statements - Consolidated City, Sinking Funds, and Consolidated Trust Funds
brief: Council will vote on approving the city's checked 2024 financial statements (main, sinking fund and trust fund accounts), which got a clean audit opinion from KPMG. No new spending is involved.

title: 21, 23, 25, 27, 29, 31, 33, 35, and 37 Kensington Avenue - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: Council votes on starting heritage protection for nine old buildings at 21 to 37 Kensington Avenue in Kensington Market.

title: 877 and 885 Lawrence Avenue East - Proposed Designation By-law Under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Consideration of Objection
brief: Council decides whether to protect the two old bank buildings at 877 and 885 Lawrence Avenue East as heritage properties, despite the owner's objection.

title: Hesketh Court - Proposed New Sidewalk Construction
brief: A councillor wants Council to drop the planned new sidewalks on Hesketh Court and Tinder Crescent from the 2026-27 road contract, after most residents said no. Resurfacing would still go ahead.

title: 324 Old Yonge Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: Council votes on starting heritage protection for the 1935 house at 324 Old Yonge Street in North York.

title: 667 King Street West - Proposed Designation By-Law under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Consideration of Objection
brief: Council decides whether to protect the Wheat Sheaf Tavern at 667 King Street West, Toronto's oldest bar, as a heritage property despite the owner's objection.

title: Audit of Transportation Services: Improving Utility Cut Permit and Inspection Processes
topics: road maintenance, roads, traffic, transportation, utilities
brief: The Auditor General checked the permit process for utility digging to reach underground pipes and cables, and wants faster, more consistent reviews. Council is asked to direct Transportation Services to act.

title: Award of Doc4989142973 to KPMG LLP for Non-Exclusive External Audit Services and Other Professional Services for the City and Certain Agencies and Corporations
brief: Rehiring KPMG LLP as the city's outside auditor for five years (2025 to 2030), for $5,120,000 ($5,210,112 net of HST recoveries). It goes to Council for a vote. KPMG was the top scorer in the bidding.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $5,120,000.

title: City of Toronto 2025-2029 Disability Inclusion Action Plan
brief: The committee would recommend that council adopt the city's 2025-2029 Disability Inclusion Action Plan, with 85 actions to find and remove accessibility barriers.

title: Arenas - 2024 and 2023 Audited Financial Statements and Status of Outstanding 2024 Audited Financial Statements
topics: arenas, audits, community & life (sc), financial reports
brief: This is a routine item: council is asked to accept checked financial statements for several city arenas covering 2024 and 2023. No policy change is proposed.

title: Casa Loma Corporation - Annual General Meeting and 2024 Audited Financial Statements
brief: Council owns the Casa Loma Corporation. Part of the meeting will act as its yearly shareholder meeting: council will review its 2024 annual report and audited financials, and hire Welch LLP as its 2025 auditor.

title: Toronto Transit Commission Traction Power Upgrade Projects - Lane Closure Information
topics: road closures, transportation infrastructure management, transportation projects
brief: The transportation boss could approve road closures of up to a year through 2032 for TTC projects that upgrade the power supply to the subway, if council agrees.

title: Updated Coyote Coexistence and Response Strategy
brief: Reviewing the updated Coyote Coexistence and Response Strategy would continue, with public sessions in each community council area and wildlife guidelines included in development reviews, if council agrees. Putting the plan in place would cost about $1.4 million, mainly for a new Wildlife Response Team.
stake: About animal services. Its recorded vote was close — 10 in favour, 12 against.

title: Proposed Licensing Regulations for Animal-Related Businesses
brief: City licensing rules for animal-related businesses like kennels, pet daycares and grooming salons, currently unregulated except for pet shops, would be created, if council agrees. Figures in the report include $2,000,000, $758.01 and $370.08. Running the new licensing system would cost the city about $293,500, mainly for extra staff.
stake: About animal services. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 22 in favour, none against.

title: Community Centres - 2024 Audited Financial Statements
topics: audits, boards of management, community & life (sc), community centres, financial reports
brief: This is a routine item: council is asked to accept the checked 2024 financial statements for nine community centres (one audit was still underway). No policy change is proposed.

title: Review, Analysis and Service Delivery Model Recommendations for City-Wide Mechanical Litter Removal Operations
topics: blue bin materials, litter collection, solid waste management
sidewalk maintenance, single stream recyclable materials, solid waste management planning
brief: City staff would take over litter vacuum work when the current contracts end in late 2026 and early 2027, instead of renewing private deals, if council agrees.

title: Lakeshore Arena Corporation - Annual General Meeting and 2024 Audited Financial Statements
brief: Council owns the Lakeshore Arena Corporation. Part of the meeting will act as its yearly shareholder meeting: council will review its 2024 annual report, audited financials, and executive pay disclosure, and hire Welch LLP as its 2025 auditor.

title: City of Toronto Audit Findings Report for the Year Ended December 31, 2024
brief: This is a routine item: KPMG's findings report on the city's 2024 financial statements is being presented. It shares the outside auditor's conclusions; no decision is requested.

title: Auditor General's 2025 Consolidated Follow-up Report Status of Outstanding Recommendations for City Divisions, Agencies and Corporations
topics: annual reports, audits, finance (sc), housing, police services
brief: This is a routine item: the Auditor General reports that 120 of 157 checked recommendations are done, 7 no longer apply and 30 are still outstanding. No new decision is proposed.

title: Audit of Parks Branch Operations - Phase 1 and 2: July 2025 Status Update
topics: audits, park maintenance, parks, parks and open space areas, repairs
brief: This is a routine item: council is asked to accept an update on staff progress with the Auditor General's ideas to improve park maintenance and repairs. No new decision is proposed.

title: Amendments to Municipal Code Chapter 103: Heritage
brief: Council votes on technical updates to the heritage by-law to match new provincial rules, and on letting the Chief Planner handle routine heritage decisions.

title: FIFA World Cup 2026 - Toronto, Governance Lessons Learned for Bidding and Planning to Host Future Mega Events
topics: audits, festivals and special events, international events, soccer, sports tournaments, stadiums
brief: The Auditor General reviewed the city's FIFA World Cup 2026 bid and planning and wants stronger council oversight earlier for future big events, plus clearer staff authority rules.
stake: About audits. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 24 in favour, none against.

title: Status of the Financial Statement Audits of the City’s Agencies and Corporations for the Year Ended December 31, 2024
brief: This is a routine item: council is asked to accept a status report on the 2024 financial audits of the city's agencies and corporations. No new decision is proposed.

title: 2025 Winter Maintenance Program Follow-Up: Status of Auditor General’s Previous Recommendations
topics: audits, information and communication technology, transportation, winter, winter storms
brief: The Auditor General checked whether past snow-clearing ideas were followed before the February 2025 winter storm: eight are done, two no longer apply and nine are still in progress. The report adds three new ideas on route maps and field checks of contractors.

title: Below Market Lease Agreement with Network Child Care Services for Child Care Services - 292 Dundas Street West
topics: child care, child care facilities, city-owned properties, community & life (sc), leasing
brief: City Council will vote on a ten-year nominal lease with Network Child Care Services for a new child care centre at 292 Dundas Street West.

title: Fossil Fuel Advocacy Advertising on City Assets
brief: A statement against greenwashing would be written for the City website, and advertisers on City property would sign a promise that their green claims are honest, if council agrees.
stake: About advertising. Decided by a recorded vote, 2 in favour and 19 against — every member's position is public.

title: Cycling Network Plan - 2025 Cycling Infrastructure and Missing Sidewalk Installation - Second Quarter Update
brief: Bike lanes would be upgraded to protected cycle tracks on Blue Jays Way, Peter Street, and Davenport Road, with one stretch on Jones Avenue downgraded, and staff could tweak these projects through 2028, if council agrees. The bike lane work would cost $500,000 and the new sidewalks $2.0 million, all from the transportation capital budget.

title: Approach to Public Electric Vehicle Charging Delivery Model
brief: A joint plan for Toronto's public electric car charging network would move ahead, with staff negotiating with short-listed companies and reporting back by early 2026, if council agrees.

title: Advancing Truth, Reconciliation and Justice: Nominal License Agreement with Aboriginal Legal Services Inc., for the Giiwedin Anang Council at 1125 Danforth Avenue
topics: aboriginal services, child care facilities, city-owned properties, community & life (sc), leasing, legal matters
brief: City Council will vote on a nominal ten-year licence letting Aboriginal Legal Services run the Giiwedin Anang Council dispute resolution program at 1125 Danforth Avenue.

title: Community Space Tenancy Lease Agreement with The Neighbourhood Group Community Services and Municipal Capital Facility Designation - 5220 Yonge Street
topics: city-owned properties, community & life (sc), community centres, leasing, services, taxes
brief: City Council will vote on a five-year nominal lease with The Neighbourhood Group Community Services for a community hub at 5220 Yonge Street.

title: Application for Approval to Expropriate Property Interests near Summerhill Station for the Second Exit Project - Stage 1
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, construction, expropriations, projects, subway stations, transportation (sc)
brief: City Council will vote on starting expropriation of easements at 10 and 20 Scrivener Square for a second exit at Summerhill station.

title: Toronto Seniors Housing Corporation Annual General Meeting and 2024 Audited Financial Statements
topics: annual reports, financial reports, seniors housing
brief: Council owns the Toronto Seniors Housing Corporation. Part of the meeting will act as its yearly shareholder meeting: council will review its 2024 annual report, audited financials, and executive pay disclosure, and skip appointing an auditor.

title: Ensuring Continued Transparency in the Procurement Process in the Absence of the Bid Award Panel
brief: City Council will vote on keeping procurement transparent after eliminating the Bid Award Panel, with awards up to $30 million delegated to the Chief Procurement Officer; source documents also list $133,800.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $30 million.

title: Acquisition of Future Toronto Public Library Site - St. Lawrence Branch
topics: land acquisition, library branches, properties (real estate), property sales, real estate transactions
brief: City Council will vote on buying a property for the relocated St. Lawrence branch of the Toronto Public Library.

title: Amendment to Non-Competitive Purchase Order 6055315 with Osler, Hoskin and Harcourt LLP for Legal Services for Union Station
topics: expropriations, external services, legal matters, purchasing, regional transportation agencies, transportation projects
brief: City Council will vote on adding $174,111 ($177,176 net of HST) to the Osler legal services order for the Union Station expropriation case, raising it from $599,895 ($610,453 net of HST recoveries) to $774,006 ($787,629 net of HST recoveries).
stake: The official summary names a figure of $174,111.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Nederman Canada Limited for Manufactured Parts and Services for Corporate Real Estate Management
topics: city vehicles, contracts, external services, maintenance, properties (real estate), purchasing
brief: The General Government Committee will vote on a $636,000 ($647,194 net of HST recoveries) three-year Nederman exhaust extraction parts contract; source documents also list $500,000.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $636,000.

title: Request to Review Supplier Suspensions and Reinstate IPAC Paving Limited and Pave-1 Construction Limited
brief: City Council will vote on reinstating IPAC Paving and Pave-1 Construction as eligible city suppliers after permanent suspensions imposed in 2012.
stake: About construction. Decided by a recorded vote, 19 in favour and 3 against — every member's position is public.

stake: The official summary names a figure of $1,000,000.

title: Lease Extension and Amending Agreement for Toronto Employment and Social Services - 700 Lawrence Avenue West
topics: employment & labour (sc), leasing, properties (real estate), services, social services
brief: City Council will vote on extending the lease for Toronto Employment and Social Services' office at 700 Lawrence Avenue West, serving about 6,700 Ontario Works cases.

title: Award of Negotiated Request for Proposal Doc4833008494 to UAP Inc. (Operating as NAPA Auto Parts) for the Supply of Automotive Equipment Parts and Inventory Management Solution
stake: The official summary names a figure of $41,929,448.

title: Waterfront East Light Rail Transit - Advancing Enabling Work with the Quayside Infrastructure and Public Realm Project
brief: Council would tell Waterfront Toronto to do early work for the Waterfront East streetcar line, worth up to $5.05 million, in the Quayside area, including moving cables under Queens Quay East. The report cites a $5 figure.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $5.05.

title: Non-competitive Procurement with Fer-Pal Construction Ltd., for Urgent Watermain Cured-in-Place Pipe Lining at Various Locations in Ward 6
brief: City Council will vote on a non-competitive $6,000,000 ($6,105,600 net of HST recoveries) Fer-Pal contract for urgent Ward 6 watermain lining, part of $11.8 million in 2025 work with $5.8 million from unspent funds; source documents also list $500,000.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $11.8 million.

title: Annual Report on City Loans and Loan Guarantees
brief: Council would approve renewing the city's $4,047,660 interest-only loan to the Lakeshore Arena Corporation for one year, from November 2025 to October 2026. The report also cites figures of $5, $67.5 million, $42.5 million, $800,000 and $4.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $5.995 million.

title: Application for Approval to Expropriate Laneway East of 129 Peter Street - Stage 1

brief: City Council will vote on starting expropriation of the laneway east of 129 Peter Street for the Streets to Homes homelessness support hub.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Kronos Canadian Systems Inc., for Proprietary Workforce Management Software Licenses, Cloud Subscriptions and Related Services
topics: contracts, information and communication technology, software, suppliers
brief: City Council will vote on a five-year non-competitive Kronos contract for workforce management software; source documents list $500,000.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $500,000.

title: 2025 Heads and Beds Levy on Institutions
brief: Council would approve the 2025 Heads and Beds tax on colleges, universities, hospitals, and jails at $75 per student, bed, or resident, expected to raise about $20.8 million. Had the rate been indexed since 1987, it would be $182.79, raising an extra $29.9 million.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $20.8 million.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Fluree Europe Middle East and Asia for Proprietary Software Licences, Professional Services and Related Maintenance
topics: contracts, external services, information & communication (sc), purchasing, software licences
brief: City Council will vote on a non-competitive Fluree software contract to maintain licensing after the current deal expires July 31, 2025; source documents list $500,000.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $500,000.

title: Missing Middle and Midrise Housing Implementation Initiative
brief: Council asks planners to report by mid-2026 on progress in building more mid-range housing like garden suites and small apartment buildings.
stake: About housing. Decided by a recorded vote, 22 in favour and 2 against — every member's position is public.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Fortran Traffic Systems Ltd., for the City's Transportation Services Vision Zero Project
topics: contracts, information and communication technology, traffic, transportation, transportation projects
brief: City Council will vote on a $2,008,750 ($2,044,104 net of HST recoveries) non-competitive Fortran contract for flashing beacons; source documents also list $500,000.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $2,008,750.

title: 2025 Levy on Railway Roadways and Rights-of-Way and on Power Utility Transmission and Distribution Corridors
brief: Council would approve the 2025 property tax on railway land and power utility corridors, worth about $6,992,485 in tax revenue. The municipal share is $6,483,956 and the education share is $508,529; the 2024 total was $6,996,373, with a $6,487,844 municipal share. The report also cites figures of $3,759,677 and $3,483,926.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $6,992,485.

title: Operating Variance Report for the Four Months Ended April 30, 2025
brief: Staff report budget changes for the four months ending April 2025, with year-end forecasts, citing figures of $62.9 million, $0.8 million, $5.5 million and $32.2 million, and ask council to approve budget amendments that do not change the city's net budget.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $62.9 million.

title: Call to Order
brief: This is a routine item: the meeting opens with the call to order, O Canada and a moment of silence. No decision is asked for.
stake: A citywide decision. Decided by a recorded vote, 13 in favour and 8 against — every member's position is public.

title: Confirmation of Minutes
brief: This is a routine item: council checks the written record of its June 25 and 26, 2025 meeting and confirms it is correct. No new decision is asked for.

title: Ontario Line - Construction Update - Second Quarter 2025
brief: Community council will receive the quarterly Ontario Line construction update, referred from City Council. No policy change is proposed.

title: From Concept to Construction: Creating More Homes Across the Housing Continuum
brief: Council asks staff to help get approved affordable housing projects into construction, as housing starts are at historic lows. The report lists figures of $85.7 million, $85,718,027, $16.9 million, $67.2 million, $67,199,200, $13 million, $596 million, $500 million, $800 million, $6.5, $8 billion and $60 million.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $85.7 million. Decided by a recorded vote, 23 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: Amendment to the Composition of the Board of Directors of Heritage Toronto
brief: Council would shrink the Heritage Toronto board from 23 members to 13, cutting public members from 21 to 11, to make the board work better.

title: Toronto Pan Am Sports Centre Annual General Meeting and 2024 Audited Financial Statements
brief: Council is a shareholder of the Toronto Pan Am Sports Centre. It would approve decisions receiving the 2024 audited financials, rehiring Welch LLP as auditor, and letting directors set the auditor's pay.

title: Operating Variance Report for the Year Ended December 31, 2024
brief: Staff report how day-to-day city spending differed from budget for 2024, citing figures of $114.4 million and $34.2 million. Council would approve budget changes that do not affect the city's net operating budget.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $114.4 million.

title: Capital Variance Report for the Four Months Ended April 30, 2025
brief: Staff report the city's big-project spending for the first four months of 2025 was $1.056 billion, or 17.1 percent of the approved budget, and forecast year-end totals. Council would approve budget adjustments to the approved capital budget and plan.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $1.056 billion.

title: Capital Variance Report for the Twelve Months Ended December 31, 2024
brief: Staff report the city spent $4.740 billion on big projects in the year ending Dec. 31, 2024, or 73.8 percent of the $6.422 billion approved budget. Council would approve budget adjustments within the approved capital budget and plan. The report cites figures of $4, $6, $3 and $1.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $4.740 billion.

title: ConnectTO Program Update
brief: Staff report an update on the ConnectTO program, including public Wi-Fi installation and a plan for picking future sites to help close the digital divide. The committee just receives it.
stake: About public consultation. Decided by a recorded vote, 18 in favour and 5 against — every member's position is public.

title: Amendment to Blanket Contract 47024775 with DragonAgile Consulting Inc., for Atlassian Software Licences and Cloud Subscriptions
topics: application software, contracts, software, software licences, system software
brief: City Council will vote on funding two more years of Atlassian licences with DragonAgile after a competitive re-tender drew no bids; source documents list $1,268,256, $1,737,510, $1,290,577, $1,768,090, $1,197,770 and $2,488,347, at $1 USD = $1.37 CAD.

title: Toronto Community Housing Corporation - Annual General Meeting and 2024 Audited Consolidated Financial Statements
brief: Council owns Toronto Community Housing Corporation. Part of the meeting will act as its yearly shareholder meeting: council will review its 2024 annual report and audited financials.

title: Deferred Revenue (Obligatory Reserve Funds),Reserves and Discretionary Reserve Funds as at December 31, 2024
brief: Council would change the Paver Maintenance reserve fund's purpose and withdrawal rules, and move the Housing Allowance reserve's $4,543,300 balance into the Social Housing Stabilization reserve, closing the old reserve. The report also cites figures of $6,362.1 million, $6,728.9 million, $366.8 million, $318.9 million, $5,291.7 million, $5,610.6 million, $5,381.7 million, $228.9 million, $17,119.6 million, $15,720.8 million and $95,002.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $6,362.1 million.

title: Introduction of Committee Reports, New Business and Business Previously Requested from the Mayor and City Officials
brief: This is a routine item: committee leaders and city staff introduce reports and new business. Council only hears them now; no decision is asked for.

title: Declarations of Interest
brief: This is a routine item: councillors say if they have a personal interest in any item, as the conflict-of-interest law requires. No decision is asked for.
stake: A citywide decision. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Petitions
brief: This is a routine item: councillors may hand in petitions from residents to be recorded. No decision is asked for.
stake: A citywide decision. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Presentations, Introductions and Announcements
brief: This is a routine item: the meeting includes presentations, introductions, and announcements. Council only listens; no decision is asked for.
stake: A citywide decision. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Review of the Order Paper
brief: This is a routine item: council looks over the order paper, the list of topics for this meeting. No decision is asked for.
stake: A citywide decision. Decided by a recorded vote, 21 in favour and 3 against — every member's position is public.

topics: by-laws, compliance, municipal codes, property standards, repairs

stake: About by-laws. Council put off deciding this item.
