brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on next steps after the tribunal approved a property split and variances at 579 Glencairn Avenue. The advice stays confidential.
stake: About activities in planning and development.

title: Temporary Traffic Amendments, Bathurst Street at Lennox Street
brief: Council will vote on temporary turn bans at Bathurst Street and Lennox Street. The bans stop illegal traffic on one-way Markham Street.

title: 2161 Yonge Street - Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Council will vote on exempting 2161 Yonge Street from land-splitting rules for two years. Minor property boundary adjustments would be allowed.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Development at 1 Bloor Street West to St. Clare’s MultiFaith Housing to enhance accessibility and add recording space to the new performance centre at 877 Yonge Street - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
brief: $109,586 of developer money to St. Clare's MultiFaith Housing for accessibility upgrades and a recording space at the Jackman Performance Centre, 877 Yonge Street would be granted, if council agrees. The budget increase is $150,000, with $109,586 forwarded to St. Clare's.

title: Designating a Portion of Fort York Boulevard as a Community Safety Zone
brief: City Council will vote on making Fort York Boulevard between Spadina Avenue and Dan Leckie Way a Community Safety Zone with higher speeding fines, near schools and a child care centre where drivers often speed.

title: Parking Amendments - Carlaw Avenue at Badgerow Avenue (Pape Avenue Junior Public School and Pape Children’s House)
brief: City Council will vote on a temporary school bus loading zone on Carlaw Avenue at Badgerow Avenue, weekdays 7:30 a.m. to 6 p.m. from September 2025 to June 2027, for buses serving the relocated Pape Avenue school and child care centre. It would replace the existing $3.00 per hour parking machine rules there.

title: Building Faster: Streamlining Housing Delivery and Strengthening the City’s Development Capacity
brief: Council would have the Housing Development Office build a three-year work plan for the Toronto Builds housing program, and ask for budget money for early-stage work to speed up housing delivery. The item cites a $5 million figure.
stake: About buildings. Decided by a recorded vote, 22 in favour and 2 against — every member's position is public.

title: Traffic and Parking Non-Delegated By-Law Changes for the 2025 Canadian National Exhibition  (Non-Delegated)
brief: Council will vote on temporary traffic and parking changes near Exhibition Place for the 2025 CNE. Full council approval is needed because the TTC runs transit there.

title: Assumption of Services from Toronto Community Housing Corporation, 66M-2491, Regent Park Phase 2
brief: This is routine paperwork: City Council will formally take over the roads and city services built in Regent Park Phase 2 from Toronto Community Housing, release the builder's guarantee, and transfer street lighting to Toronto Hydro.

title: 931 Kingston Road - Accessible Loading Zone
brief: Council will vote on an accessible loading zone on Kingston Road near Silver Birch Avenue. It would operate weekday daytime hours.

title: Appointment of a Public Member to the Toronto Zoo Board
brief: The committee recommends one person for council to appoint to the Toronto Zoo Board, for a term ending November 14, 2026. Candidate details are kept private.

title: 1117 Queen Street West - Alterations to a Designated Property and Demolition of Heritage Attributes of a Building on a Designated Property under Sections 33 and 34(1)1 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about heritage changes at 1117 Queen Street West. The legal strategy is confidential.
stake: About heritage designation. Council put off deciding this item.

title: Appointment of a Public Member to the Toronto Public Library Board
brief: The committee recommends one person for council to appoint to the Toronto Public Library Board, for a term ending November 14, 2026. Candidate details are kept private.

title: 2025 Winter Maintenance Program Review
brief: Council would remove the pause on winter snow-service requests at the start of snow events, figure out extra equipment needed for big storms, and keep working with consultant Municipal VU on the winter review.
stake: About snow. Its recorded vote was close — 12 in favour, 10 against.

title: 65 Ookwemin Street (Formerly 309 Cherry Street) - Amendment to Item 2024.CC19.9 - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: An earlier decision would be amended and private directions adopted on a tribunal case about the 65 Ookwemin Street development in the Port Lands, if council agrees. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: 11 Polson Street - Appeal of Licence Appeal Tribunal Decision
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for directions on whether to appeal a tribunal decision about liquor licence conditions for the Rebel Nightclub and Cabana Pool Bar at 11 Polson Street.

title: Expanding Housing Options in Neighbourhoods: Major Streets Study - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about the Major Streets Study, which allows townhouses and small apartments along major streets. The legal strategy is confidential.
stake: About houses. Decided by a recorded vote, 18 in favour and 2 against — every member's position is public.

title: Mayor’s Economic Action Plan in Response to United States Tariffs - Update to Council
brief: Council would build a plan to protect and grow factory and industrial jobs in Toronto, report back by mid-2026, and bring options for the EDGE job-incentive program by late 2025. The EDGE program is worth about $1.9 million in tax breaks.
stake: About economic development. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 20 in favour, none against.

title: 123 Bellamy Road North - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about three buildings of 44, 35 and 9 storeys at 123 Bellamy Road North. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: 670, 680 and 690 Progress Avenue - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about seven buildings with 2,245 homes at 670-690 Progress Avenue. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: Authority to Accept a Donation and Enter Into an Agreement for Baseball Diamond Improvements at Christie Pits Park - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
brief: Up to $190,000 in donated baseball-field upgrades at Christie Pits Park: a $100,000 bequest and a $90,000 Jays Care Foundation grant (the item also lists $50,000) would be accepted, if council agrees. Work would finish by October 2025.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $100,000.

title: City Foundation Drainage Policy
topics: development review process, drainage areas, natural drainage systems
brief: Council asks staff to review the rule that makes builders handle groundwater on their own site, and to report back in early 2026. The rule adds costs to building homes.
stake: About development review process. Decided by a recorded vote, 23 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: Parks and Recreation Funding Allocation
topics: funding, parks and open space areas, recreational facilities, recreational programs
brief: The item asks City staff how the $2 million in Parks and Recreation money approved in the 2024 budget for youth programming in priority neighbourhoods is being spent.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $2 million. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: 81 Isabella Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: An intent to designate 81 Isabella Street as a heritage property under the Ontario Heritage Act would be stated by council. If no objections are filed, a designation bylaw follows.

title: 464 Royal York Road - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about a proposed 12-storey rental building with 112 homes at 464 Royal York Road. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: Creating More Affordable Housing Options in Our Neighbourhoods - by Councillor Jamaal Myers, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
brief: Building fees on the second, third and fourth units in buildings of up to six homes would be waived, if council agrees. This would encourage more multiplex-style housing like Scarborough's.
stake: About urban planning. Decided by a recorded vote, 20 in favour and 4 against — every member's position is public.

title: 450 Rustic Road - Proposed Designation By-Law under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Consideration of Objection
brief: The decision to designate 450 Rustic Road as a heritage property, despite the owner's objection, would be affirmed by council, moving ahead with the designation bylaw.

title: Speeding up Transit in Ward 11 - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
brief: On-street parking prices along busy Ward 11 bus and streetcar routes could be reset to discourage long-term parking and speed up surface transit. Council would have the Toronto Parking Authority report on setting rates on routes like Bathurst Street — where consultations showed parked cars slow buses and streetcars — plus reviewing parking times and turn permissions on local streets. The motion cites the Toronto Board of Trade's recommendation to use parking prices to redirect parking off arterial roads. Riders on Ward 11 surface routes would benefit if transit moves faster.
stake: About parking fees. Decided by a recorded vote, 22 in favour and 2 against — every member's position is public.

title: Re-Opening and Amending Item 2025.EY20.2 - 56, 58 and 60 Fieldway Road - Community Benefits Charge In-Kind Report - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
brief: This is a technical fix: council is asked to raise the developer's required on-site public art payment at 56, 58 and 60 Fieldway Road from 33 percent to 55 percent of the developer community fee. No new rules here.

title: 220, 230 and 240 Lake Promenade and 21 and 31 Park Boulevard - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case that would replace five rental buildings with five new ones and 2,021 rental homes near Lake Promenade. The legal strategy is confidential.
stake: About zoning. Decided by a recorded vote, 3 in favour and 20 against — every member's position is public.

title: 321-355 Symington Avenue and 350 Campbell Avenue - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about two towers with 847 homes at 321-355 Symington Avenue. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Committee of Adjustment
brief: Appointing Katie Plaizier and Dino Lombardi to the Toronto and East York panel of the Committee of Adjustment, for terms ending November 14, 2026 is on council's agenda. Details are confidential.

title: Accepting an In-Kind Donation from East York Tennis Club for Capital Improvement at Cosburn Park - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
brief: Up to $400,000 in donated court repairs from the East York Tennis Club for the tennis courts at Cosburn Park would be accepted, if council agrees. Work would start in fall 2025.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $0.400 million.

title: Implementation Strategy for Business Improvement Area Streetscape Master Plans - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
brief: Planning staff would use business-area street master plans when reviewing building applications and the city's Streetscape Manual, if council agrees. This would make the plans official guidance.

title: 2726 and 2734 Danforth Avenue - Demolition of Designated Heritage Properties - Approval with Conditions
brief: Approval of demolishing the heritage buildings at 2726 and 2734 Danforth Avenue, including the Little York Hotel, with conditions such as a commemoration plan is before council. New eight-storey and four-storey buildings would follow, with the hotel facade reconstructed.

title: No More Weeds and Tree Coffins Across our Public Right of Way - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
brief: Planning staff would include ideas on who should maintain planters and landscaping on public land next to private buildings, if council agrees. The report is due late in 2025.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Vision Zero Streetscape Improvements at Redpath and Erskine and Erskine and Yonge - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
brief: $239,311.40 ($27,691.58 plus $211,619.82) of developer money on safety fixes at the Redpath-Erskine and Erskine-Yonge intersections is before council for approval. The work would be bundled with planned repaving.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $239,311.40.

title: Entering into an Agreement with ArtHubs Toronto Inc. at Spectrum Park (Regent Park Boulevard Park) - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
brief: Parks staff could sign a three-year nearly free licence deal with ArtHubs Toronto Inc. to run community programs at Spectrum Park in Regent Park, if council agrees.

title: External Compliance Audit Reports for the Integrity Commissioner, Lobbyist Registrar and Ombudsman Offices for the Year Ended December 31, 2024
brief: Council receives for information the 2024 external audit reports for the Integrity Commissioner, Lobbyist Registrar and Ombudsman offices. No decision is proposed.

title: Taking Action to Protect Tenants - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
brief: A colour-coded rating system for apartment buildings: red for serious problems, yellow for minor ones, green for good repair would be created, if council agrees. Signs would be posted on each building and on the city website.
stake: About rent. Decided by a recorded vote, 20 in favour and 3 against — every member's position is public.

title: Accepting an In-Kind Donation from Valley Tennis Club for Improvements at York Mills Valley Park - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
brief: Donated tennis-court resurfacing work worth $74,450.00 plus HST from the Valley Tennis Club at York Mills Valley Park would be accepted, if council agrees. The earlier summary put the value at up to $90,000.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $74,450.00.

title: Re-Opening and Amending Item 2024.EX18.7 - CaféTO Business Improvement Area (BIA) Pilot Programs Update and Toronto Municipal Code Amendments for 2025 - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor Stephen Holyday
brief: CaféTO patio rules would change so a patio can only be refused if more than 25% of nearby residents who were told about it object, if council agrees. The goal is easier patio approvals.

title: 849 Eglinton Avenue East - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about a 40-storey tower, a 21-storey tower and an office building at 849 Eglinton Avenue East. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: Toronto City Council Support for CHIN Radio/TV International’s Canadian Radio-television Telecommunications Commission Application to Relocate its AM Broadcast Service to AM900 - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
brief: A letter would go to the CRTC backing CHIN Radio's bid to move to the AM900 frequency, if council agrees. CHIN lost its Toronto Islands transmitter site and its signal got worse.

title: Annual Report of the Toronto Lobbyist Registrar for the Year 2024
brief: Council receives the Lobbyist Registrar's 2024 annual report, and asks the Registrar to report back in late 2025 on clarifying the lobbying bylaw for roundtable and advisory body participants.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Ward 13 2024 Participatory Budgeting Projects for Cabbagetown Neighbourhood - New Street Benches for Cabbagetown Business Improvement Area - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
brief: $46,800 of developer money, picked by resident vote, on 25 new benches for the Cabbagetown business area is before council for approval. The money comes from a $750,000 resident-voted fund.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $750,000.

title: Temporary Delegation: Authority During the Summer Recess to Direct Attendance on Appeals of Committee of Adjustment Decisions - by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
brief: This is a procedural item: council is asked to let the city's lawyer handle Committee of Adjustment appeals during the summer recess, when council is not meeting. No new rules here.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2025.CC31.10 - 2346 Yonge Street - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
brief: This is a procedural item: council is asked to reopen a decision on 2346 Yonge Street so one confidential attachment stays confidential. No new rules here.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Design and Construct New and Expanded Sports Courts at Clairlea Park - by Councillor Parthi Kandavel, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
brief: $67,412.88 ($10,000 plus $57,412.88; also shown as $11,349.88 plus $56,063) of developer money on new and bigger sports courts at Clairlea Park is before council for approval. Pickleball and basketball are planned.

title: 850 Carlaw Avenue - Liquor Licence Application - Dopapen Coffee - License Number 3213857 - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: food service establishments, liquor sales licences
brief: Ontario's alcohol regulator would be told that a liquor licence for Dopapen Coffee at 850 Carlaw Avenue is not in the public interest unless neighbours' concerns are fixed, if council agrees. The objection deadline is August 5, 2025.

title: Keeping our Sidewalks Clear - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
brief: How food-delivery e-bikes and scooters block sidewalks for walkers, especially people with strollers and wheelchairs, would be studied, if council agrees. Staff would report on quick and long-term fixes.

title: Removal of Section 118 Notice of Restrictions from Title to 429 Pape Avenue - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
brief: This is a procedural item: council is asked to remove a land-title notice on 429 Pape Avenue so Metrolinx can buy it for Ontario Line work without forcing a sale. No new rules here.

title: Accepting an Award From Bloomberg Philanthropies as Part of the Finalist Stage of the 2025 Global Mayors Challenge - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos-Lin
brief: A US $50,000 (CAD $68,500) award from Bloomberg Philanthropies to develop a universal school food program idea would be accepted, if council agrees. 25 finalists will later get USD $1,000,000 (about CAD $1.37 million).
stake: The official summary names a figure of $50,000.

title: Working Collaboratively Towards a Positive Outcome for the Future Indigenous Women and Children’s Shelter at 68 Sheppard Avenue West by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
brief: Shelter and real estate staff would look at buying properties next to 68 Sheppard Avenue West, if council agrees. This would support the planned Indigenous women and children's shelter there.
stake: About First Nations. Decided by a recorded vote, 21 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: Requesting Legal Review of Bid Process Complaint Relating to Toronto Parking Authority RFP-PARCS-202407 - by Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
brief: The City Manager and the city's lawyer would review the Toronto Parking Authority's bidding process for a new parking payment system, if council agrees. A bidder filed a complaint; the report is due late in 2025.

title: Authority to Accept In-Kind Donation and Issue Tax Receipt - Dafoe Urn Restoration Project at Craigleigh Gardens Park - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
brief: The donation of a 19th-century cast-iron urn, with $33,117.31 from Blake Melnick and $25,098.00 from Adrian Dafoe for its repair and installation at Craigleigh Gardens Park would be accepted, if council agrees. The earlier summary valued it at up to $65,000.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $33,117.31.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2025.PH21.9 - Providing Housing Opening Today Toronto Inc., with Section 37 Funds for Purchase of Affordable Rental Housing Building - by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
brief: An earlier decision that gave $1,500,000.00 ($205,966.27 plus $478,208.82 plus $815,824.91) of developer money to a non-profit to buy a rental building would be widened, if council agrees. The building would become affordable over time.

title: Update Downsview: Downsview Secondary Plan - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about the Downsview Secondary Plan, guiding 115,000 new residents and 52,000 workers around the former airport. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: 645-655 Northcliffe Boulevard - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about a proposed 15-storey building with 159 homes at 645-655 Northcliffe Boulevard. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: 3019 Dufferin Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about a proposed 8-storey building at 3019 Dufferin Street. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: 1117 Queen Street West - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about refused planning and zoning applications for 1117 Queen Street West. The legal strategy is confidential.
stake: About zoning. Council put off deciding this item.

title: 2485 Eglinton Avenue West - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Direction
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about a proposed 45-storey building at 2485 Eglinton Avenue West. No hearing is scheduled yet.

title: A Better Way to Replace your Furnace: Helping Homeowners Switch to Heat Pumps
topics: heating, ventilation and air conditioning systems
brief: Council would build a program helping Toronto homeowners switch from furnaces to heat pumps, with coaching, a trusted contractor list, installation help, discounts for lower-income homes, and financing options.

title: Ookwemin Minising - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about the Ookwemin Minising (Villiers Island) revitalization in the Port Lands. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: Authorization to Terminate the 1992 Social Housing Agreement for 285-291 Jarvis Street Between the City of Toronto and Toronto Community Housing Corporation - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
brief: This is a procedural item: council is asked to end the 1992 social-housing deal for 285-291 Jarvis Street when the property moves to Homes First Society, and sign a new deal. No new rules here.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to the Transportation Services Division for the Reconstruction of the Rosedale Valley Multi-Use Trail - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
brief: $2,483,625.13 ($142,858.14 plus $571,432.53 plus $169,334.46 plus $1,600,000.00) of developer money to rebuild the Rosedale Valley multi-use trail between Bayview Avenue and Park Road is before council for approval.

title: Amending an Encroachment Agreement with the University of Toronto to enable low Carbon District Energy - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Parthi Kandavel
topics: heating, ventilation and air conditioning systems
brief: The $50,000 yearly licence fee the University of Toronto pays for geothermal pipes to its Oak House residence would be dropped, if council agrees. Staff would report in 2026 on a standard approach for such low-carbon projects.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $50,000.

title: Helping Evicted Tenants Access Shelter and Support - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
brief: A call on Ontario's Landlord and Tenant Board to give evicted tenants contact info for city housing help when an eviction order is issued goes to council. The motion cites a 91-year-old tenant who did not know where to turn.

title: 2801 Keele Street and 6 Paxtonia Boulevard - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment - Appeal Report - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about a proposed 11-storey building with 156 homes at 2801 Keele Street. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: 2350-2352 Yonge Street - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about a proposed 50-storey building with 323 homes at 2350-2352 Yonge Street. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Support the Redesign of the Vale of Avoca Ravine to Include a Missing Walking Trail Connection - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: urban wilderness trails, ravine protection areas
brief: $250,000 of developer money on detailed plans for a new walking trail link in the Vale of Avoca ravine is before council for approval. The item also lists $40 million, $1.5 million and $1 million.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $35.

title: Safer Shores at Woodbine Beach: Protecting the Safety of Our Waterfront and Everyone Who Enjoys It - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside
brief: A call on Ports Toronto to create a no-go zone of at least 100 metres from the Woodbine Beach shoreline for motorized watercraft goes to council. This follows safety worries about unlicensed jet ski rentals.

title: Review of Automated Speed Enforcement (ASE) Ticket Appeals Process - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Anthony Perruzza
topics: enforcement, tickets, traffic speed, traffic violations
brief: Court staff would review how people dispute speed-camera tickets and report back in October 2025, if council agrees. Residents reported broken websites, wrong emails and long phone waits.
stake: About enforcement. Decided by a recorded vote, 15 in favour and 8 against — every member's position is public.

title: Authorization to Release Sections 37 Funds for Pedestrian Safety on Avenue Road - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
brief: $200,000 of developer money to build a crosswalk with traffic lights on Avenue Road between Davenport Road and Dupont Street is before council for approval.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $200,000.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Property Standards Committee
brief: Appointing eight people to the Property Standards Committee, two for each of the Etobicoke York, North York, Scarborough and Toronto-East York panels, for terms ending July 25, 2029 is on council's agenda.

title: Strengthening Protections for Toronto's Tree Canopy - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
brief: Planning and forestry staff would build stronger tools to protect trees covered by the tree rules, if council agrees. This follows a protected tree cut down without permits at a Leaside building site.
stake: About tree canopy. Decided by a recorded vote, 18 in favour and 2 against — every member's position is public.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Support the Redesign of the Vale of Avoca Ravine to Include a Missing Walking Trail Connection - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
brief: $250,000 ($250,000.00) of developer money from the 1331 Yonge Street project on detailed plans for a trail link in the Vale of Avoca ravine is before council for approval. The item also lists $40 million, $1.5 million and $1 million.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $35.

title: Feasibility of Limiting the Number of Automated Speed Enforcement Infractions an Individual Vehicle Owner can Receive from a Single Camera Location Prior to Receiving Their First Infraction in the Mail
topics: speed limits, traffic cameras, traffic speed
brief: Council receives for information a report on whether the city can limit how many speed-camera tickets a vehicle owner gets from one camera before their first ticket arrives in the mail. No decision is proposed.
stake: About speed limits. Council sent it back for more work.

title: Authorization to Release Section 45 Funds from the Developments at 4726-4728 Yonge Street, 9-31 Bogert Avenue and 2-28 Poyntz Avenue for the Capital Improvements to the Schoolyard at Avondale Public School - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
brief: $50,000.00 of developer money to the public school board for upgrades to the schoolyard at Avondale Public School would be granted, if council agrees. The school serves about 1,000 students, beyond its 861 capacity.

title: Introduction of General Bills and Confirming Bills
brief: This is a procedural step: City Council will introduce general bills and confirming bills, which turn approved decisions into official bylaws. No new policy is decided.

title: 2026 Schedule of Meetings
topics: committee meetings, council meetings, municipal officials
brief: The 2026 meeting schedule for council and its committees goes to council for approval, along with a request that city agencies avoid conflicts with it.

The six bids were $54,000.00, $2,098,497.50, $2,135,79.00, $2,167,800.00, $2,304,660.00 and $2,519,359.00.

The annual figure is $2,351,554 ($2,657,256 including HST; $2,392,941 net of HST recoveries). Five-year totals are $11,757,770 / $13,286,280 / $11,964,707.

The bids were $208,500.00, $229,350.00, $295,027.50, $297,190.50, $298,502.50, $456,558.50 and $612,603.50; the option years are $257,706 / $291,208 / $262,242, $265,437 / $299,944 / $270,109, $273,400 / $308,942 / $278,212 and $281,602 / $318,211 / $286,559, for a five-year total of $1,328,346 / $1,501,031 / $1,351,725.

The bids were $4,143,861, $5,496,496 and $5,675,432.

The bids were $349,820.00 and $1,800,539.20; the option period is $1,947,283 / $2,200,430 / $1,981,555, for a four-year total of $3,837,849 / $4,336,770 / $3,905,395.

title: Bluffer’s Park Action Plan - by Councillor Parthi Kandavel, seconded by Councillor Nick Mantas
brief: Parks staff, with conservation authorities and the community, would plan priority upgrades for Bluffer's Park ahead of its 50th anniversary, if council agrees.

title: Off-Site Parkland Dedication for 289 to 299 Balliol Street and 305 Balliol Street - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
brief: A call on the builder of a 31-storey project at 289 to 299 Balliol Street to try to find parkland elsewhere to give the city, instead of paying cash goes to council. Staff would work with the builder to find a site.
stake: Ward 12 is named in the record.

title: Request for City-Initiated Zoning By-law Amendment 1049-2022 to Re-allocate Section 37 Funds - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
brief: $250,000 in unspent developer money from the 91-101 Raglan project, once set aside for public art, would move to street upgrades in the Bathurst-St. Clair area, if council agrees.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $250,000.

title: Renaming of Diamond 1 at Wishing Well Park as “Darryl Harding Memorial Diamond” - by Councillor Nick Mantas, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
brief: The baseball diamond at Wishing Well Park would be renamed the Darryl Harding Memorial Diamond, if council agrees. Harding was a longtime Scarborough youth baseball coach who died in August 2024.

title: Bloordale Village Business Improvement Area - 2025 Operating Budget - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
brief: This is a procedural item: council is asked to approve the Bloordale Village business area's 2025 budget of $285,000 and its $163,000 levy, paid by local businesses. No city money is used.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $0.285 million.

title: CityServeTO - A Youth-based Community Service Initiative - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside
brief: The first round of CityServeTO, a youth community-service program, with up to $700,000 each for two community health centres would be funded, if council agrees. The program runs September 2025 to June 2026.

title: 42 Donalda Crescent - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Nick Mantas, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
brief: The city's lawyer would be authorized to appeal the committee's approval of a garden suite at 42 Donalda Crescent, and oppose it at the local appeals board. Staff had recommended approval with conditions.
stake: About zoning bylaws. Decided by a recorded vote, 5 in favour and 17 against — every member's position is public.

title: 131 McCormack Street - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
brief: The city's lawyer would appeal a Committee of Adjustment decision that allowed an entertainment venue at 131 McCormack Street for two years, if council agrees. Planning staff had said the use needed a zoning change, not a variance.

title: 250 Wincott Drive - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Ontario Land Tribunal - by Councillor Stephen Holyday, seconded by Councillor Parthi Kandavel
brief: The city's lawyer would go to Ontario's land tribunal to support the committee's refusal of parking and height exceptions for a big project at 250 Wincott Drive, if council agrees.
stake: About zoning bylaws. Decided by a recorded vote, 9 in favour and 12 against — every member's position is public.

title: Accepting In-Kind Donation from Scarborough Cricket Association for Facility Improvements at Milliken Park - by Councillor Jamaal Myers, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
brief: Up to $150,000 ($0.150 million) in donated cricket-facility work from the Scarborough Cricket Association for Milliken Park would be accepted, if council agrees. The park could get a cricket pitch and/or batting cages.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $0.150 million. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 22 in favour, none against.

title: 125 The Esplanade - Interim Park Implementation - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
brief: Parks staff would build a temporary park at 125 The Esplanade once the temporary market building is removed, if council agrees. The site would stay public while long-term planning continues.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to The Humber Bay Park East Shoreline Design Improvements - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
brief: $155,000.00 of developer money on design upgrades to the shoreline at Humber Bay Park East is before council for approval. Residents raised concerns after the beach was replaced with cobble stones.

title: Assistance to the Society of Saint Vincent de Paul’s Project at 21-31 Windsor Street, 18 Buckingham Street, 60 Newcastle Street and 95 Portland Street - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
brief: Building-plan fees for the Society of Saint Vincent de Paul's women's shelter project near King and Dufferin would be dropped, if council agrees. The project has 36 support units and 88 shelter beds.

title: Potential Future Community Recreation Centre in Liberty Village - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
brief: Studying whether Liberty Village needs a new community centre as part of the Liberty for All planning study would continue, if council agrees. Ideas are due in early 2026.

title: Request the Federal Government to Restore 100 Percent of the Funding to Shelter and Support Refugee Claimants - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng
brief: Ottawa would be asked to again cover the full cost of sheltering refugee claimants and set up a national system for newcomers, under a council motion. The federal government has spent $1.1 billion on hotel housing and $1.5 billion through its aid program since 2017.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $1.1 billion.

brief: City staff suggest changing zoning rules to allow two L-shaped buildings of 10 to 23 storeys at 3434 Lawrence Avenue East, with 855 homes, some shops, a new public road, and a new park.

brief: City Council will vote on a major redevelopment at 1025 The Queensway: ten towers of 18 to 46 storeys with 4,077 homes, affordable units, shops, workplaces and three new streets.

zoning bylaw amendments, residential real estate

brief: Council will vote on adding seven properties on Dundas Street West and Jefferson Avenue, including the 1907 Wineberg Apartments, to the Heritage Register.

brief: The owner of 640 Sheppard Avenue East disagrees with a city repair order. The Property Standards Committee will decide whether to keep, change, or cancel it.

brief: Changing zoning rules to make it simpler to add infill housing on existing apartment sites, speeding up approvals for new homes in the city's apartment neighbourhoods. It goes to Council for a decision. The source text also cites $471.1 million. Council decides.

brief: Adding 36 Green Valley Road to the city's Heritage Register. It goes to City Council for a decision. Listing marks the property as historically significant and requires notice before any demolition.

brief: Adding 2255 Sheppard Avenue East to the city's Heritage Register. It goes to City Council for a decision. Listing marks the property as historically significant and requires notice before any demolition.

brief: City Council will vote on applying the new city-wide parking standards to two properties: 1400 Weston Road and 300-330 Sidney Belsey Crescent.

brief: Council would move remaining approval conditions for the six-storey mixed-use building at 3471 Lake Shore Boulevard West, with 19 homes and ground-floor shops, into a holding provision on the zoning by-law, instead of requiring them before the by-law is enacted.

It goes to Council for a decision. Toronto's Housing Accelerator Fund deal with the federal government is worth $471.1 million. Council decides.

title: 15 Glen Morris Street - Alterations to and Demolition of Heritage Attributes of a Designated Property under Sections 33 and 34 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
brief: Council will vote on allowing changes and partial demolition of the heritage Samuel Bennett House at 15 Glen Morris Street. An 8-storey building would rise behind its facades.

title: 105 Thirty First Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Adding a Holding Provision
brief: This is procedural: City Council will vote on moving leftover approval conditions into a holding provision for the approved eight stacked townhouses at 105 Thirty First Street.

title: 911X Castlefield Avenue - Request to Demolish the Non-Residential Building
brief: The owner of 911X Castlefield Avenue wants to tear down the non-residential building there. City Council must decide whether to grant the permit, grant it with conditions, or refuse it.

title: 16-26 Earlington Avenue and 4161- 4169 Dundas Street West - Construction Staging Area Time Extension
brief: City Council will decide whether to extend the construction staging area on Dundas Street West at Earlington Avenue for a 10-storey residential and townhouse project, after the developer reported unforeseen delays.

brief: City Council will vote on tightening parking rules on St. Albans Road and its Kipling Avenue ramp, banning standing and stopping to keep the road clear for TTC buses.

title: 5576 Yonge Street - Official Plan Amendment, Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Refusal
brief: Staff recommend refusing a plan for two buildings (35 and 25 storeys, 608 homes) at 5576 Yonge Street. One issue is a city sewer running through the site that would have to move. Council is asked to refuse it.

stake: About buildings. Decided by a recorded vote, 21 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: 5507-5509 Dundas Street West - Class 4 Noise Area Classification (NPC-300)
brief: Council would designate 5507-5509 Dundas Street West as a Class 4 Noise Area, a provincial label for developments near stationary noise sources, and send the decision to the Ministry of the Environment.

brief: Two mixed-use buildings (32 and 28 storeys, 705 homes) are proposed at 690-720 Sheppard Avenue East. The applicant appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal, and North York Community Council is asked to have the City Solicitor oppose the appeal.

brief: Council will vote on sending city lawyers to oppose a proposed 7-storey rental building at 1601-1603 Bathurst Street. The developer appealed after council missed its deadline.

title: 5, 5A, 5B and 9 Leslie Street - City Initiated Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Council will vote on zoning changes for City-owned land at 5-9 Leslie Street near the Ashbridges Bay Treatment Plant. The land would host new infrastructure and natural areas.

title: Use of Nathan Phillips Square for Various Events - October 1, 2025 - April 30, 2026
topics: arts and culture, festivals and special events
brief: Council will vote on letting event organizers at Nathan Phillips Square serve alcohol in wine gardens from October 2025 to April 2026. Provincial and health approvals are required.

title: Downtown Homelessness Addiction Recovery and Treatment (HART) Hub
topics: health, rehabilitation (people), substance abuse, supportive housing
brief: Creating the downtown HART Hub is before council for approval, with the Medical Officer of Health to sign the agreements setting it up. It would help people who use drugs get treatment, mental health care, and housing supports.

title: City-Initiated Zoning By-law Amendments - Re-allocating Section 37 funds within Ward 13 - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Council will vote on letting unspent developer funds at Ward 13 sites be redirected to buy community space for non-profits.

title: 604-610 Bay Street and 130 Elizabeth Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning bylaws
brief: Council will vote on two buildings with 858 rental homes, including 245 affordable units, at 604-610 Bay Street and 130 Elizabeth Street. The heritage Coach Terminal would be kept.

title: 2 Tecumseth Street and 125-133 Niagara Street - Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Council will vote on exempting 2 Tecumseth Street and 125-133 Niagara Street from land-splitting rules for two years. This allows phased construction of the approved development.

title: Renaming of the Community Garden in Joel Weeks Park
brief: Council will vote on renaming the community garden in Joel Weeks Park 'Carol Sutton Garden'. She was an artist and longtime park volunteer.

title: Dundas Street West - Accessible Loading Zone
topics: loading zones, parking regulations, traffic regulations
brief: Council will vote on a new accessible loading zone on Dundas Street West near Pacific Avenue for Wheel-Trans users. The item lists a $3.00 fee.

title: 120 Bouchette Street - Application for an Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment - Appeal Report
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning bylaws
brief: Council will vote on sending city lawyers to oppose three proposed towers with 1,626 homes at 120 Bouchette Street. The developer appealed after council missed its deadline.

title: Changes to Business Improvement Area Boards of Management
topics: board members, business improvement areas, change, removal
brief: Matthew Kutas from the Mount Pleasant Village BIA Board and Jocelyn Leung from The Eglinton Way BIA Board of Management would be removed, if council agrees.

title: Corporate Drive - Accessible Loading Zone

brief: Staff suggest an accessible loading zone on the north side of Corporate Drive near the dialysis clinic at 78 Corporate Drive, with nearby pay parking at $3.00 per hour shifted to fit. Since buses run on this street, this needs a City Council vote.

title: Pay-and-Display Parking - Various Streets - June 2025 (Non-Delegated)
brief: Council will vote on paid parking changes on TTC-served streets in Wards 9 and 14. Full council approval is needed because the TTC runs transit there.

title: 1799 St Clair Avenue West - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment and Draft Plan of Subdivision Applications - Appeal Report
brief: Council will vote on sending city lawyers to oppose three proposed towers of 30, 40 and 45 storeys at 1799 St. Clair Avenue West. The developer appealed after council missed its deadline.

title: 0, 119-125, 160 and 200 Benny Stark Street and 116-122 Turnberry Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, official plan amendments, zoning bylaws
brief: Council will vote on sending city lawyers to oppose a proposed development with towers up to 46 storeys on Benny Stark Street and Turnberry Avenue. The developer appealed after council missed its deadline.

title: Ontario Line - Construction Update - Second Quarter 2025
brief: Community council will receive a quarterly update on Ontario Line construction. No policy change is proposed.
stake: About construction. Council sent it back for more work.

title: Parking and Traffic Amendments - Dundas Street West - Findings Report on Pilot Initiative
brief: Council will vote on making permanent the parking and traffic changes on Dundas Street West between Spadina and McCaul. The changes supported the 505 Dundas streetcar. The item lists costs of $322,000.00 and $6,780.00.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $322,000.00.

title: 25 Dalhousie Street and 30 Mutual Street - Amendment to Section 37 Agreement to Permit a Seasonal Outdoor Patio
brief: Council will vote on letting two seasonal outdoor patios operate in the public walkway at 25 Dalhousie Street and 30 Mutual Street.

title: 234 Sheppard Avenue West and 223 Harlandale Avenue - Official Plan Amendment, Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Appeal
brief: Staff recommend refusing a plan for 234 Sheppard Avenue West and 223 Harlandale Avenue: a 4-storey, 15-unit condo and an 11-storey building with 43 rental homes. Council is asked to refuse it, keeping current rules; staff would defend the refusal if appealed.

title: 1350 Sheppard Avenue West - Zoning Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: At 1350 Sheppard Avenue West, the developer wants to raise the unit count from 1,400 to 1,700 and shrink minimum two- and three-bedroom sizes. City Council is asked to approve the change. The item also references $5,000,000.00.

title: Toronto Parking Authority Security Approach and Framework
brief: The Parking Authority's report on security at garages and lots is before council to note, with a related private document kept secret because it concerns City property security. Security spending rose by $2.9 million since 2021 to $3.9 million a year, with $4.1 million for cameras and $2.7 million for access control, plus $25.7 million more planned over five years.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $2.9 million.

title: 2823, 2825, 2827 and 2829 Eglinton Avenue East - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City staff suggest changing zoning rules to allow a 14-storey building with 190 homes and shops at 2823-2829 Eglinton Avenue East.
stake: About zoning. Decided by a recorded vote, 7 in favour and 14 against — every member's position is public.

title: Property Included on the City's Heritage Register - Consideration of Objection for 1751 Bayview Avenue
brief: Keeping the 1930s apartment building at 1751 Bayview Avenue on the city's Heritage Register despite the owner's objection. It goes to Council for a decision. Council decides.

brief: Council votes on bringing about 323 North York properties under the city-wide zoning by-law. These lots would then follow the same rules as the rest of the city, including new permissions for more housing.

title: Toronto Pearson Annual Update
brief: Toronto Pearson gives its annual update to the committee, covering airport performance, the economic impact of the airport zone, the ten-year Pearson LIFT capital program, and governance. No decision is proposed.

title: Housing Action Plan: Avenues Policy Review - Phase Two Work Plan
brief: Council votes on a work plan to write new zoning for more mid-rise housing along Toronto's main streets, with public input along the way.

title: TransformTO Net Zero Strategy - 2024 Annual Report on Implementation Progress
topics: city initiatives, environmental plans, greenhouse effect
municipal initiatives, environment plans, greenhouse gas emissions
brief: The 2024 progress report on the TransformTO Net Zero Strategy, which aims for net zero emissions by 2040 is before council to note.

title: 2025 Toronto Heritage Grant Awards

The grants should generate about $660,225.61 in private spending. House-form buildings get up to $10,000.00, or up to $20,000.00 for a full cedar or slate roof. Council decides.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $317,000.00.

title: F.G. Gardiner Expressway and Don Valley Parkway Closure - Bike for Brain Health 2026
brief: The Gardiner Expressway and Don Valley Parkway would close on Sunday, May 31, 2026, from 2 a.m. to 4 p.m., for the Bike for Brain Health charity ride, if council agrees.

title: Temporary Street Closure for Eastbound F.G. Gardiner Expressway and Northbound Don Valley Parkway - 2026 Toronto Triathlon Festival
brief: Eastbound Gardiner Expressway and northbound Don Valley Parkway lanes on the morning of Sunday, July 26, 2026, for the Toronto Triathlon Festival would close, if council agrees.
stake: About highways. Decided by a recorded vote, 19 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: Expanding Housing Options in Neighbourhoods - Multiplex - Monitoring Program - Final Report
brief: Approving city-wide zoning changes for multiplexes, updating the rules for this low-rise housing type and the land-development part of the city's rulebook, based on a monitoring program's final report. It goes to Council for approval. Council decides.

title: Authorized Vehicles in City Parks - Review of Operating Procedures and Policies
topics: city vehicles, parks vehicles, policies and procedures
brief: Staff would update the rules for vehicles allowed in parks and run a public education campaign on proper vehicle use, how to report problems, and how park assets are protected, if council agrees.

title: A Strategic Parking Framework for the City of Toronto
brief: A citywide parking plan goes to council for approval, along with studying whether some on-street parking enforcement could move from Toronto Police to the Parking Authority.
stake: About city initiatives. Decided by a recorded vote, 19 in favour and 2 against — every member's position is public.

title: Garratt Boulevard - Heavy Truck Prohibition
topics: community & life (sc), community safety, heavy trucks, traffic
brief: Heavy trucks would be banned from Garratt Boulevard, between Wilson Avenue and Gilley Road. Council is asked to approve the ban, which would send truck traffic to Dufferin Street, Beffort Road and Hanover Road.

title: Updates on Vision Zero Road Safety Initiatives: Improving Crossings for Pedestrians, Updated Road Classification Criteria and Other Matters
topics: pedestrians, road safety, traffic control systems
brief: New road safety rules on crosswalks, stop signs, and traffic lights under the Vision Zero plan would take effect if council adopts them, along with thirteen new traffic signals for pedestrian safety. The 2025 Vision Zero budget is $99.1 million ($31.7 million capital, $67.4 million operating), its biggest ever. Funding continues for the Active and Safe Routes to School program, including $320,000 a year for three years to the two school boards.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $99.1 million. Its recorded vote was close — 9 in favour, 11 against.

title: Amendments to Chapter 918 as it Relates to Applications within Ward 15
topics: municipal codes, neighbourhoods, on-street parking, parking, parking pads, residential properties
off street permit parking, cultural neighbourhoods

title: Minimizing Salt Pollution that Poison Rivers and Streams
topics: pedestrian walkways, road safety, road salt management
brief: A councillor wants Council to urge the Ontario minister to protect property owners who use road salt properly from lawsuits, push for enforceable salt standards, and cut the City's own salt use.

title: Contract Amendment to Settle Legal Dispute with Innotex Inc., Concerning the Provision of Firefighter's Structural Bunker Suits
topics: contracts, fire and rescue services, firefighters, legal matters, personal protective equipment
brief: City Council will vote on confidential recommendations to settle the legal dispute with Innotex Inc. over firefighters' bunker suits.

brief: City Council will consider an emergency $898,448 ($914,261 net of HST recoveries) rigging upgrade at the Meridian Arts Centre; source documents also list $500,000.

title: Toronto Paramedic Services: Multi-Year Staffing Plan
brief: Council would approve adding 112 staff to Toronto Paramedic Services' 2025 budget, mostly frontline paramedics, pending provincial funding, and plan for more staff in future budgets as call demand grows.

title: Amendment to Non-Competitive Blanket Contract 47023385 with Atlas Polar Company Limited and Blanket Contract 47023205 with Altec Industries Ltd., for Mechanical and Structural Safety Inspections, Repairs, Training and Certifications for various Hiab, Effer and Altec Equipment
brief: City Council will vote on extending two equipment inspection contracts to ten years and raising their combined budget by $2,429,720 ($2,472,483 net of HST recoveries), from $2,119,834 to $4,549,554 ($4,629,626 net of HST recoveries), split $1,389,984 ($1,414,447 net of HST recoveries) and $1,039,736 ($1,058,036 net of HST recoveries); source documents also list $500,000.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $2,429,720.

title: 4208 Dundas Street West - Liquor Licence Application - Region Food and Bar - License No. 2261917
topics: liquor sales licences, special occasion permits
brief: City Council is being asked to object to an outdoor patio liquor licence for Region Food and Bar at 4208 Dundas Street West unless conditions are added, amid residents' concerns about disturbance in the midrise building. The final decision rests with the AGCO.

title: Strategic Contract Amendment for Integrated Telecommunications Infrastructure
topics: contracts, information and communication technology, infrastructure, projects, telecommunication infrastructure, telecommunications
brief: City Council will vote on extending the Bell Canada telecom infrastructure contract by five years to secure better rates and finish modernization; source documents list $500,000.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $500,000.

title: Leveraging City-Owned Real Estate to Support City Council Objectives - Long-Term Financial Plan Update
brief: Council would adopt rules for building housing together with parks and recreation buildings, apply them in the parks facilities plan review, and keep two private attachments about land deals private for now. The report cites a $100 figure and a $2 million figure.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $100. Decided by a recorded vote, 19 in favour and 2 against — every member's position is public.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with DocuPet Inc., for the Provision of Pet Licensing Services
topics: animal licences, animal services, contracts, licences, pets, wildlife
brief: City Council will vote on a $680,730 ($692,711 net of HST recoveries) five-year DocuPet pet licensing contract, up to $1,537,136 ($1,564,190 net of HST recoveries) with extensions; source documents also list $500,000.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $680,730.

title: A Vision and Strategy for a Universal School Food Program in Toronto
brief: Council would ask Ontario to raise school nutrition funding to match the city's, ask Ottawa for more school food money, and create a $7.492 million project for a universal morning meal program. The city already puts $31.1 million a year into the Student Nutrition Program.
stake: About food. Decided by a recorded vote, 17 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: Appointment of Public Member to the Toronto Hydro Board
brief: This is a procedural item: a city panel is asked to recommend two public members to council for the Toronto Hydro Board, for terms ending June 2027. No new rules here.

title: Toronto Hydro Corporation Annual General Meeting and 2024 Audited Financial Statements
brief: Council, as owner of Toronto Hydro, would treat part of the meeting as the company's yearly meeting, re-appoint its auditor, and receive the 2024 yearly report and climate action update.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Waterfront Toronto Board
brief: This is a procedural item: a city panel is asked to recommend three public members to council for the Waterfront Toronto Board, for terms ending June 2028. No new rules here.

title: Commencing Public Consultations for Communities Impacted by New Shelter Locations - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Parthi Kandavel

stake: About homelessness. Decided by a recorded vote, 21 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

topics: television industry, community use of schools
brief: Staff would explore securing a closed school as a dedicated film and TV production location, reporting back by fall 2025, if council agrees. The motion cites $2.6 billion in economic activity tied to the screen sector.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $2.6 billion. Decided by a recorded vote, 21 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

brief: Council decides how to keep two city-owned projects — 267-275 Merton Street and 610 Bay Street/130 Elizabeth Street, with over 1,350 rental homes including at least 369 affordable — on track. The city is also asking Ottawa and CMHC to speed up construction funding.

brief: The Toronto Parking Authority board asks city staff and the TTC to prepare a business case for fixing the parking garages at City Hall and 40 York Street. The report cites a $280 million repair backlog and figures of $20.17 million, $15.38 million, $12.6 million, $128 million and $152 million.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $280 million.

title: Toronto Parking Authority Enterprise Risk Management
body: Toronto Parking Authority - Audit and Risk Management Committee
brief: The Toronto Parking Authority board votes on approving its updated 2025 risk management report.

title: Assessment of City Impacts from Bill 17, Protect Ontario by Building Faster and Smarter Act, 2025 and Provincial Budget
brief: Council would ask Ontario to consult staff and the public before writing Bill 17 rules, to allow zoning with conditions, and to drop mandatory development charge increases in 2025 and 2026. The province moved the bill to third reading without committee review or public hearings, and it became law before the public comment period closed. The changes could cost the city about $1.9 billion over 10 years, and council also asks Ontario to make the city whole and reconfigure the Building Faster Fund.
stake: About buildings. Decided by a recorded vote, 19 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: FIFA World Cup 2026 Toronto: Community Benefits Plan Update, Social Procurement and Workforce Development Status, Community Activation Plan, Marketing and Communications Overview, Support for Concurrent Special Events, Principles of Bidding on International Events, and Purchase Order Amendment
brief: Council would add a $23 million World Cup 2026 upgrade project to the Exhibition Place budget, paid for by Maple Leaf Sports and Entertainment, and let staff negotiate the funding deal. The item also cites figures of $23.0 million, $15.0 million, $8.0 million, $23 million, $0.7 million, $664,234.55 and $675,925.08.

title: Delegation of Authority Update: April 2 - June 1, 2025
body: Toronto Parking Authority - Audit and Risk Management Committee
brief: This is a routine item: the Toronto Parking Authority board receives an update on decisions made under delegated authority from April 2 to June 1, 2025. The President can commit up to $500,000 and award non-competitive contracts up to $250,000. No policy change.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $250,000.

title: Toronto Parking Authority - 2025 May 31 Year-to-Date Financial Performance (First Five Months Results)
body: Toronto Parking Authority - Audit and Risk Management Committee
brief: This is a routine item: the Toronto Parking Authority board receives its financial results for the first five months of 2025, with net income of $18.1 million. The report cites revenue of $69.2 million, operating costs of $46.3 million, $5.6 million invested in capital projects, a $55.6 million full-year capital plan, $25.8 million in city funding for Bike Share and EVs, and figures of $2.4 million, $1.0 million, $4.3 million, $1.4 million, $1.1 million, $44 million, $47 million, $2 million and $5 million. No policy change.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $18.1 million.

title: 7-17 Nipigon Avenue - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about a proposed 50-storey building with 620 homes at 7-17 Nipigon Avenue. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: 77 Erskine Avenue - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
