brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about a proposed 26-storey tower with 352 homes at 99 Birmingham Street and 210 Islington Avenue. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: 4696 Yonge Street - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about a proposed 40-storey building with 536 homes at 4696 Yonge Street. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: 579 Glencairn Avenue - Appeal of Toronto Local Appeal Body Decision
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on whether to challenge a tribunal decision approving a property split and variances at 579 Glencairn Avenue. The legal strategy is confidential.
stake: About activities in planning and development. Council put off deciding this item.

title: 389-393 Broadway Avenue - Official Plan Amendment 770 - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about Official Plan Amendment 770, which made 391 Broadway Avenue parkland. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: 586 Eglinton Avenue East - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about a proposed 32-storey building with 249 homes at 586 Eglinton Avenue East. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: 2346 Yonge Street - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about a proposed 56-storey building with 407 homes at 2346 Yonge Street. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: 708-712 Kennedy Road - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about a redevelopment at 708-712 Kennedy Road replacing 98 rental homes. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: 36 Romeo Street - Request for the City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
brief: The city's lawyer would go to the local appeals board to defend the refusal of a lot split and two new homes at 36 Romeo Street, if council agrees. The committee refused the plan in April 2025.
stake: About appeals. Decided by a recorded vote, 17 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for the Pelham Park Hub - Giving Youth Leaders of Tomorrow a Brighter Today - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
brief: $10,000 of developer money to fix up a new youth hub at 61 Pelham Park Gardens is before council for approval. The hub would offer mentorship, leadership and recreation programs.

title: Ombudsman Toronto 2024 Annual Report
brief: Council receives for information the Ombudsman Toronto 2024 annual report on the office's investigations. No decision is proposed.

title: Construction Project 25ECS-RD-104LR: Removal of Sidewalk Installation in Brookhaven Neighbourhood - by Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Vincent Crisanti
brief: Planned new sidewalks on four Brookhaven streets from a fall 2025 repaving contract would be dropped, if council agrees. At a June 10 meeting, 71 of 72 residents voted against the sidewalks.

title: Review of Seasonal Grass Cutting and Inter-Divisional Coordination - by Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
brief: Staff would report on starting grass cutting earlier in April and better coordinating mowing across city divisions, if council agrees. The report would come through the 2026 budget process.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Heritage Toronto for Heritage Plaque at 101 Dewson Street - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: conservation, heritage preservation, historic sites, plaques
brief: $10,000 of developer money on a heritage plaque at 101 Dewson Street is before council for approval. The plaque honours the home's history of Black, gay and lesbian activism in the 1980s.

title: New Etobicoke Centre Shelter Public Consultation - by Councillor Stephen Holyday, seconded by Councillor Vincent Crisanti
brief: The property deal for a new shelter in Ward 2 would be paused until residents are consulted, if council agrees. The shelter's location and details would be made public.
stake: About homelessness. Decided by a recorded vote, 6 in favour and 12 against — every member's position is public.

title: Green P Parking Lot Usage Data - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
brief: A call on the Toronto Parking Authority to publish its parking-lot usage data online, updated every three months goes to council. The data would help planning decisions.

title: East Mall Bus 111 Route Public Consultation - by Councillor Stephen Holyday, seconded by Councillor Vincent Crisanti
brief: A call on the TTC to pause rerouting the 111 East Mall bus and building four new bus pads on Beaver Bend Crescent goes to council. Residents and the local school would be consulted first.

title: Waiving of Toronto Parking Authority Fees on Bond Street - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
brief: A call on the Toronto Parking Authority to drop $115,230 in fees tied to removing three parking spaces and two machines for the St. Michael's Hospital rebuild on Bond Street goes to council. The hospital's street upgrades are valued at close to $1.5 million.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $1.5 million. Decided by a recorded vote, 16 in favour and 2 against — every member's position is public.

title: Authorization to Release Sections 37 and 45 Funds to Support Toronto Community Housing Capital Projects at 90 Mornelle Court - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Nick Mantas
brief: $623,310.07 ($402,500.00 plus $220,810.07) of developer money to Toronto Community Housing for a new playground, basketball court fixes and a gathering place at 90 Mornelle Court would be granted, if council agrees. Building would start in 2026.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $623,310.07.

title: Supporting the North York Harvest Food Bank in meeting rising food scarcity needs in Toronto - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng
brief: Staff would report by fall 2025 on ways to help the North York Harvest Food Bank move to a bigger warehouse at 4050 Chesswood Drive, if council agrees. Options include a grant or a low-interest loan.

title: Introduction of General Bills and Confirming Bills
brief: This is a procedural step: City Council will introduce general bills and confirming bills, which turn approved decisions into official bylaws. No new policy is decided.

title: Amending Item 2022.NY29.1 - 824 Sheppard Avenue West, 177, 179 and 181 Cocksfield Avenue- Official Plan Amendment, Zoning Amendment and Rental Housing Demolition and Conversion Application - Final Report - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Anthony Perruzza
brief: The builder could tear down 15 empty rental units at 824 Sheppard Avenue West sooner, without waiting for digging permits, if council agrees. The tenants have moved out with help and compensation.

title: Recognition of 50th Anniversary of the Cabbagetown Group Softball League - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
brief: This is a recognition item: council is asked to congratulate the Cabbagetown Group Softball League on its 50th anniversary. No new rules or spending.
stake: About recreation & tourism (sc). Its recorded vote was unanimous — 19 in favour, none against.

title: Accepting a Donation from East York Foundation at Leaside Gardens Memorial Arena - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
brief: A $319,000 donation from the East York Foundation for new scoreboards at Leaside Gardens Memorial Arena would be accepted, if council agrees. No city money would be used.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $319,000.

title: Implementation of Permit Parking on Dundas Street West (Permit Area 1F), Bloor Street West and Quebec Avenue (Permit Area 1B) - by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
brief: Whether new buildings on Dundas Street West, Bloor Street West and Quebec Avenue should be kept out of on-street permit parking would be studied, if council agrees. Staff would report back.

title: Speeding Up Streetcars: Traffic Amendments on Adelaide Street, King Street and York Street - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
brief: Approval of temporary parking and traffic changes on Adelaide, King and York streets starting July 2, 2025, until streetcars return to King and Church is before council. The changes would keep the 504 King moving during construction. The streetcar track contract would also grow by $350,000, to about $3.43 million, to pay for extra paid-duty officers near the King and Church work site.
stake: About streetcars. Decided by a recorded vote, 22 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: Re-Opening King Street for Business: Keeping Toronto’s Downtown Core and Canada’s Financial District Moving - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor Stephen Holyday
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, congestion, public transit, transportation
brief: A councillor asks council to reopen King Street between Spadina Avenue and Church Street to cars, even though the King and Church intersection stays closed for watermain and track work. The closure began June 2 and runs at least to mid-August.
stake: About Toronto Transit Commission. Decided by a recorded vote, 19 in favour and 4 against — every member's position is public.

title: Fixing Roads Faster - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
brief: Permanent repaving of the roads with the most potholes, aiming to finish by the end of 2025 would speed up, if council agrees. An extra $350 million from the province would pay for the work.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $350 million.

title: Award of Doc5010288941 to Riel Sale & Service Tire Accessories & Equipment Limited for the Non-Exclusive Supply and Delivery of Garage Equipment for Toronto Paramedic Services
brief: A two-year, $1,063,261 contract ($1,201,485 including HST; $1,081,975 net of HST recoveries) with Riel Sale & Service for garage gear for Toronto Paramedic Services, is up for approval by the contract panel. The bids were $935,245.32, $886,051.00, $813,261.92 and $42,404.00.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $935,245.32.

title: Waterfront School Playground Expansion - Amendment to existing nominal lease and ancillary real estate agreements with Toronto District School Board - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
brief: The city's lease with the Toronto District School Board would grow by about 260 square metres at 627-635 Queens Quay West, if council agrees. This would let the Waterfront School playground expand.

title: Award of Doc4749624256 to Arup Canada Inc. for the Geospatial Document Access System Project Assessment for Toronto Water
brief: A $768,985 contract ($868,953 including HST; $782,519 net of HST recoveries) with Arup Canada for a study of a map-based document system for Toronto Water is up for approval by the contract panel.

title: Award of Doc4844777854 to Stantec Consulting Ltd. for Professional Engineering Services for the Proposed New Sections of Commissioners Street  Sanitary Trunk Sewer for Engineering and Construction Services
brief: A $6,163,256 contract ($6,964,479 including HST; $6,271,729 net of HST recoveries) with Stantec Consulting for design work on new sections of the Commissioners Street main sewer line is up for approval by the contract panel.

title: Award of Doc4864874854 to Develotech Inc. for the Non-Exclusive Supply and Delivery of Bike Lane Bollards and Related Items for Purchasing and Materials Management (Stores)
brief: A one-year, $ 235,692 contract ($ 266,332 including HST; $ 239,840 net of HST recoveries) with Develotech for bike lane posts for city supply stores, with four optional renewal years, is up for approval by the contract panel. The bids were $196,410.00, $235,692.00, $280,597.50, $282,425.55, $301,785.00 and $553,839.15; the option years are $242,763 / $274,322 / $247,035, $250,046 / $282,552 / $254,446, $257,547 / $291,028 / $262,080 and $265,273 / $299,759 / $269,942, for a five-year total of $1,251,321 / $1,413,993 / $1,273,344.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $196,410.00.

title: Award of Doc4953550456 to Infosys Public Services Canada Inc., for the Phase 2 Implementation of the IBM Maximo Work and Asset Management (EWMS) for Solid Waste Management Services Division
brief: A three-year, $2,199,951 contract ($2,485,944 including HST; $2,238,670 net of HST recoveries) with Infosys for Phase 2 of the IBM Maximo work-tracking system for Solid Waste Management, is up for approval by the contract panel. The bids were $2,199,950.57 and $2,666,230.67.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $2,199,950.57.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 and Section 42 Funds to Amend the 2025 Capital Budget and 2026-2034 Plan for Parks and Recreation for Canoe Landing Off Leash Area Improvements in Ward 10 - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
brief: $1.69 million of developer money to design and build permanent upgrades to the off-leash dog area at Canoe Landing Park is before council for approval. The total breaks down as $0.1 million in 2025 and $1.59 million in 2026, with $795,000 from Section 37 and $795,000 from Section 42 funds.

title: Award of Doc5078321208 to 2489960 Ontario Inc. o/a Kore Infrastructure Group for Watermain Replacement and Road Resurfacing for Engineering and Construction Services
brief: A $10,987,900 contract ($12,416,327 including HST; $11,181,287 net of HST recoveries) with Kore Infrastructure for water pipe and sewer work plus road repaving in several districts, is up for approval by the contract panel. The five bids were $ 9,989,000.00, $10,337,576.25, $10,723,990.00, $14,482,725.00 and $14,717,916.00.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $10,337,576.25.

title: Award of Doc5117247719 to Chemtrade Chemicals Canada Ltd. for the Non-Exclusive Supply and Delivery of Aluminum Sulphate for Toronto Water
brief: A $2,231,620 contract ($2,521,731 including HST; $2,270,897 net of HST recoveries) with Chemtrade Chemicals for aluminum sulphate to treat drinking water, is up for approval by the contract panel. Chemtrade was the only bidder.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $2,231,620.

title: Award of Doc5074031114 to ZPro Solutions Canada Inc., for the Phase 1 Implementation of the IBM Maximo Work and Asset Management (EWMS) for Toronto Water Division
brief: A three-year, $3,825,242 contract ($4,322,524 including HST; $3,892,567 net of HST recoveries) with ZPro Solutions Canada for Phase 1 of the IBM Maximo work-tracking system for Toronto Water is up for approval by the contract panel.

title: Award of Sourcewell Solicitation Number 082923-DAC to Green Tractors Inc. for the Supply and Delivery of Fifty Two (52) Various Agriculture Tractors with Related Accessories, Attachments and Supplies for Fleet Services
brief: A $10,894,006 deal ($12,310,227 including HST; $11,085,741 net of HST recoveries) with Green Tractors for 52 diesel farm tractors, with an option to buy seven more in 2026, is up for approval by the contract panel. The 2026 option is $1,875,706 / $2,119,548 / $1,908,718; with it, the total is $12,769,712 / $14,429,775 / $12,994,459.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Uptown Yonge Business Improvement Area for Seating and Streetscape Improvements - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
topics: benches (street furniture), business improvement areas, urban form
brief: $63,000 of developer money would go to the UPtown Yonge business group for 22 new benches on the west side of Yonge Street, if council agrees. The city would match the amount.

title: Addressing Gaps in the City’s Heat Relief Strategy - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: climate, environment (sc), extreme heat alerts, health (sc), public health, temperature
brief: The city's heat relief plan would be reviewed, with quick steps taken before the next heat wave, like longer pool hours and extra shelter spaces, if council agrees. This summer's humidex hit 46. Up to $50,000 from the extreme weather reserve would go to Project FoodChain to hand out at least 500,000 bottles of water.
stake: About climate. Decided by a recorded vote, 21 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: Results of Interest Arbitration Between the City of Toronto and Toronto Civic Employees Union Local 416 - Paramedics - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
brief: The arbitrator's June 23, 2025 deal for Toronto paramedics (union Local 416) would be put into effect, if council agrees. That means budget changes to match the new pay and benefits.

title: Targeted Lane Re-Openings to Reduce Congestion During Construction Downtime - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
brief: Staff would look at making construction crews reopen traffic lanes nearby during big events and quiet times, if council agrees. This would cut congestion from overlapping projects.

title: Open or Closed? Improving Public Information on Pool Closures and Alerts - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
brief: A request to make the city's online pool-closure info accurate and easy to find goes to council. Residents showed up at closed pools during the recent heat wave.

title: Preserving Community Access at Loretto College School - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
brief: An effort to keep the field and green space at Loretto College School in Davenport open to the public would go to council. Parks staff would ask the Catholic school board for a formal deal to share the space.

title: Re-Opening and Amending Item 2025.CC30.8 - 943 - 963 Eglinton Avenue East and 23 Brentcliffe Road - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
brief: This is a procedural item: council is asked to fix a wrong address in an earlier decision, changing 161 Vanderhoof Avenue to 131 Vanderhoof Avenue for a parkland handover. No new rules here.

title: Request to Accept In-Kind Community Benefits for 49 Ontario Street Rental Housing Development - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
brief: Land from the developer instead of cash as the community benefit for the rental housing project at 49 Ontario Street would be accepted, if council agrees. The project has 1,226 rental units, including about 246 affordable ones.

title: Action to Address Speed Racing on Expressways - by Councillor Jon Burnside, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
brief: A call on Toronto police to consider joint action on late-night speed racing on highways like the Don Valley Parkway goes to council. The parkway would also be added to noise enforcement work.

brief: The Board will hear how two City investment funds did in early 2025 and whether they followed the investment rules.

brief: Two money managers, Connor, Clark and Lunn and Leith Wheeler, will present their bond investment plans to the Board.
stake: About investment. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

brief: The Board will get an update on investment manager staffing changes, fund rebalancing since February 2025, and fund balances as of April 30, 2025.

brief: The Board will keep four private ESG reporting documents secret. They cover how outside money managers are checked on environmental, social, and governance issues.

title: Presentation - Lobbyist Registrar for the City of Toronto
brief: The City's Lobbyist Registrar will explain to the Toronto Investment Board what counts as lobbying and how to handle sales pitches from outside vendors.
stake: About investment. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Mayor’s Economic Action Plan in Response to United States Tariffs
brief: Council approved the Mayor's plan to protect Toronto's economy from US tariffs. The Board just needs to note the decision.
stake: About economic development. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Establishing The City of Toronto Mayor's Awards for Artificial Intelligence Innovation within City Divisions, Agencies, and Boards
brief: Council told staff to start a yearly Mayor's contest honouring projects that use data and AI to improve City services and civic life. The Board just needs to note it.
stake: About awards. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Authority to Issue a Debenture
brief: Approval of the city borrowing $350 million through a 30-year bond for capital projects is before the Debenture Committee. The borrowing was arranged June 11, 2025 and delivered to investors June 27, 2025.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $350 million.

title: Introduction of By-laws
brief: A general bill and a confirming bill to turn its decisions into official bylaws would be introduced, if the Debenture Committee agrees. No new policy is proposed.

brief: A Rick Hansen Foundation representative gives a verbal presentation on its Accessibility Certification program for public buildings and spaces.
stake: About accessibility. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

brief: This is a routine item: the committee hears a progress report on the city's Service Promise Refresh, new guidelines for professional and consistent public service. Nothing is decided.

brief: Staff present the Toronto Strategic Parking Framework and ask the committee for accessibility feedback. The framework will guide current and future parking projects.

title: Platform Edge Doors Study - Outcome of Feasibility and Business Case Studies
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, infrastructure, safety, subway stations
brief: A study on subway platform screen doors is before the TTC Board for review, which would add door rules for new stations and seek money for a test at TMU (Dundas) Station.

brief: This is routine business. The TTC Board is asked to approve KPMG's report on the audit of the TTC's 2024 financial statements and send it to the City Audit Committee.

title: Draft Consolidated Financial Statements of Toronto Transit Commission for the Year Ended December 31, 2024
brief: Approving the TTC's 2024 financial statements and send them to the City Audit Committee. It goes to the TTC Board for approval. They show a $503.2 million accounting surplus, up $49.3 million from 2023. That is an accounting number, not extra money to spend.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $503.2 million.

brief: This is a routine item: the head of Transportation Services presents on joining up its software systems and improving customer service. Nothing is decided.
