brief: A routine fire-safety item: North York Community Council is asked to mark lanes at 12 Concorde Place as fire routes, so fire trucks can reach the property and cars blocking them can be ticketed.

title: 805, 807, 811, and 813 Glencairn Avenue - Residential Demolition Application
brief: The owner of 805-813 Glencairn Avenue wants to tear down six single-family houses there. North York Community Council has the final say; the decision turns on whether a replacement building is planned.

title: 499 Briar Hill Avenue - Request for a Fence Exemption to the Toronto Municipal Code, Chapter 447
brief: The owner at 499 Briar Hill Avenue wants to keep a fence that breaks the city's fence rules. Staff recommend North York Community Council refuse the exemption; if refused, the owner gets another notice to fix the fence.
stake: About fences. Council put off deciding this item.

title: 369 Soudan Avenue - Application for Fence Exemption
brief: The owner at 369 Soudan Avenue wants an exemption from the city's fence-height rules. North York Community Council, which has the final say, is asked to decide.
stake: About applications. Council put off deciding this item.

title: 78 Burncrest Drive - Request for a Fence Exemption to the Toronto Municipal Code, Chapter 447
brief: The owner at 78 Burncrest Drive wants to build a fence that breaks the city's fence rules. Staff recommend North York Community Council refuse the exemption.

title: 101 Westmore Drive - Designation of Fire Routes and amendment to Chapter 880 - Fire Routes
brief: This is procedural: the Etobicoke York Community Council will vote on designating a fire route at 101 Westmore Drive so firefighters keep clear access.

title: Assumption of Services, Registered Plan 66M-2503, 3035 Weston Road, Damaris Development Incorporated
brief: Council would formally take over the roads and city services in the Damaris Development subdivision at 3035 Weston Road, release the developer's performance guarantee, and pass an assumption by-law for the public road.
stake: About assumption of services. Council put off deciding this item.

title: 3807-3815 and 3819-3829 Lake Shore Boulevard West - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City Council will vote on a 39-storey, 490-home tower on Lake Shore Boulevard West, with 14 rental replacement units and a small public plaza.
stake: About official plan amendments. Council put off deciding this item.

title: 14 Atherton Crescent - Application to Remove a City Tree
brief: The local council would deny a permit to cut down a ginkgo at 14 Atherton Crescent. The owner cites smelly fallen fruit and clogged pipes, but staff say the 47-centimetre tree is healthy and can stay. The owner is appealing.

title: 12 Monkton Avenue - Application to Remove a City Tree
brief: The local council would deny a permit to cut down a blue spruce at 12 Monkton Avenue. The owner wants it gone for a new driveway, but staff say the 43-centimetre tree can stay. The owner is appealing.

title: 3807-3815 and 3819-3829 Lake Shore Boulevard West - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City Council will vote on demolishing 14 rental units and two rooms on Lake Shore Boulevard West, with a tenant plan offering the right to return at similar rents and $20,000.00 in financial compensation.
stake: About demolitions. Council put off deciding this item.

title: Lawrence Park Transportation Plan
brief: This finalizes the Lawrence Park Transportation Plan, which guides road work in the area. It includes speed humps on Buckingham Avenue, and North York Community Council is asked to approve the installations.

title: Carmichael Avenue - Traffic Calming (Speed Humps)
brief: Speed humps are proposed for Carmichael Avenue, between Kelso Avenue and Avenue Road. North York Community Council is asked to approve them; staff say the street meets the city's traffic-calming rules.

title: Corbett Avenue - Traffic Calming (Speed Humps)
brief: The Etobicoke York Community Council will decide on staff's advice not to install speed humps on Corbett Avenue between Jane Street and Rockcliffe Boulevard, since the street does not meet the city's criteria.

title: Poynter Drive and Stapleton Drive - U-Turn Prohibitions and Parking Amendments
topics: change, parking prohibitions, transportation (sc), turn prohibitions (traffic)
brief: The Etobicoke York Community Council will decide whether to ban U-turns on Poynter Drive and Stapleton Drive near Westway Junior Public School, and to allow short-term parking on part of Poynter Drive for school drop-offs.

title: Elms-Old Rexdale Neighbourhood Streets Plan
topics: crossing guards, neighbourhoods (planning), road safety, sidewalks, traffic calming measures
brief: The local community council would approve the Elms-Old Rexdale Neighbourhood Streets Plan so it can be put into action, including new all-way stops, speed humps, and no-standing zones to improve road safety in the neighbourhood.

title: Removal of a Director from the Wilson Village Business Improvement Area Board of Management
brief: Removing a director from the Wilson Village Business Improvement Area board goes to North York Community Council. The council has the authority to appoint and remove BIA directors in its area.

title: 6 Locust Street - Residential Demolition Application
brief: Council would approve tearing down one half of the semi-detached home at 6 Locust Street, with no replacement permit issued, on condition the owner beautifies the site with clean fill, landscaping, and a construction fence.

title: Sunnylea and The Kingsway Neighbourhoods - Traffic Calming (Speed Humps) and All-Way Stop Control
brief: The Etobicoke York Community Council will decide whether to install 56 speed humps on nine streets in Sunnylea and The Kingsway, plus an all-way stop, since staff found the streets meet the city's safety criteria. The humps would cost about $4,000 each, or about $224,000 in total.

title: Lemonade for Love
brief: The Etobicoke York Community Council will hear a presentation from Lemonade for Love, the kid-run Etobicoke fundraiser that has raised over $200,000 for children with special needs at Silver Creek Preschool. No funding decision is requested; the presentation is for information.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $200,000. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Re-opening of Item NY22.17 - Maxome Avenue - Traffic Calming (Speed Humps)
brief: A procedural step: council is asked to re-open its earlier decision on speed humps for Maxome Avenue. This follows a resident petition and survey on traffic safety; re-opening lets council revisit the item.

title: Introduction of By-laws
brief: This is procedural: the Etobicoke York Community Council will introduce by-law bills.

title: Introduction of By-laws
brief: A routine step: North York Community Council formally introduces the by-laws that make this meeting's decisions official. No new policy is decided.

title: Award of Doc4611820536 to GFL Environmental Services Inc. for Preventive Maintenance of Catch Basins, Grease Traps and Oil Interceptors for Various Divisions
brief: A three-year, $6,023,348 contract ($6,806,383 including HST; $6,129,358 net of HST recoveries) with GFL for upkeep of catch basins, grease traps and oil separators, with two optional renewal years, is up for approval by the contract panel. The bids were $439,490, $23,140, $1,740,830, $142,323, $2,116,470, $5,837,931, $1,904,537, $6,623,645 and $774,735; the option years are $2,068,016 / $2,336,858 / $2,104,413 and $2,130,056 / $2,406,964 / $2,167,545, for a five-year total of $10,221,420 / $11,550,205 / $10,401,317.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $439,490.

title: Award of Doc4985288483 to Forest Ridge Landscaping Inc. O/A Urban Life Solutions for Tree Pit and Planter Maintenance for Environment, Climate and Forestry
brief: A one-year, $132,840 contract ($150,109 including HST; $135,178 net of HST recoveries) with Forest Ridge Landscaping for tree pit and planter care, with three optional renewal years, is up for approval by the contract panel. The bids were $132,840.00, $184,500.00, $196,800.00, $287,820.00, $306,270.00, $307,500.00 and $322,875.00; the option years are $136,825 / $154,612 / $139,233, $140,930 / $159,251 / $143,410 and $145,158 / $164,028 / $147,713, for a four-year total of $555,753 / $628,001 / $565,534.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $132,840.00.

title: 250 Wincott Drive and 4620 Eglinton Avenue West
brief: The Etobicoke York Community Council has a status update on the 250 Wincott Drive and 4620 Eglinton Avenue West redevelopment, where the developer wants taller, denser buildings than the three 11-storey towers Council approved in 2021.

title: 2025 Toronto Urban Health Fund Allocations and Review Process
brief: Approval of $645.4 thousand for seven one-year projects and $1,679.2 thousand for fifteen three-year projects, totalling $2,324.6 thousand for HIV prevention and substance use programs is before the Board.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $645.4 thousand.

title: Update from the Deputy Ombudsman (Housing)
brief: The committee gets an update from Ombudsman Kwame Addo and Deputy Ombudsman (Housing) Reema Patel on the Housing Unit's work over the past six months.

title: Promising Practices in Supportive Housing
brief: The committee hears a talk on Dunn House as an example of supportive housing, from Dr. Andrew Boozary and City staff.

title: Supporting Unhoused Rights Holders Working Group Chair Update
brief: The committee gets an update from the chair of the Supporting Unhoused Rights Holders Working Group, including its work on the City's Shelter Safety Action Plan.
stake: About housing. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Toronto Public Health response to the Ontario Measles Outbreak
brief: For information only. The Board hears a talk from the Associate Medical Officers of Health on Toronto Public Health's response to the Ontario measles outbreak.

title: Public Appointment to the Housing Rights Advisory Committee
brief: The committee notes that City Council appointed Diana Chan McNally to the Housing Rights Advisory Committee for a term from April 25, 2025 to November 14, 2026.
stake: About appointments. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Chair Update
brief: The committee gets an update from Housing Rights Advisory Committee chair Elizabeth McIsaac, including on the working groups.
stake: About advisory committees. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Presentation by Right to Housing Network Toronto
brief: The committee hears a talk from the Right to Housing Toronto network on its draft framework for tracking the City's progress on a rights-based approach to housing.

title: Maintaining Housing Working Group Chair Update
brief: The committee gets an update from the chair of the Maintaining Housing Working Group, including its work on the City's Multi-Tenant Homes Framework.
stake: About government services. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Update on the City’s Multi-Tenant Homes Framework and Supports for Tenants
brief: City staff give a talk on the City's Multi-Tenant Homes Framework and an overview of supports for tenants. No new rules are proposed.

title: Improving Access to Housing Working Group Chair Update
brief: The committee gets an update from the chair of the Improving Access to Housing Working Group, including its work on the waitlist for rent-geared-to-income and affordable rental homes.

title: Establishing The City of Toronto Mayor's Awards for Artificial Intelligence Innovation within City Divisions, Agencies, and Boards
brief: This item notes that Council has already directed staff to set up the annual Mayor's Data and AI Innovation Challenge. City divisions, agencies, and boards are asked to take part.

title: Creating an Independent Website for Toronto Public Health
brief: The Medical Officer of Health would study whether Toronto Public Health should have its own website, separate from the City's website, and report back, if the Board agrees.

title: Additional Applications for the Toronto Hydro Board
brief: This is a procedural item: a city panel is asked to consider extra applicants for the Toronto Hydro Board and select four candidates to interview. No new rules here.

title: Selection of Candidates for Interview for the Waterfront Toronto Board
brief: This is a procedural item: a city panel is asked to select nine candidates to interview for the Waterfront Toronto Board. No new rules here.

title: Award of Doc4890584788 to Kudlak-Baird (1982) Limited for Dufferin Transfer Station Exterior Lighting Improvements for Solid Waste Management Services
brief: A $1,525,571 contract ($1,723,895 including HST; $1,552,421 net of HST recoveries) with Kudlak-Baird for lighting upgrades at the Dufferin Transfer Station, is up for approval by the contract panel. The bids were $1,271,309.00 and $1,357,380.00.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $1,271,309.00.

title: Award of Doc5048607075 to Robert B. Somerville Co. Limited for the Watermain CIPP Lining at Various Locations for Toronto Water
brief: A $10,849,713 contract ($12,260,176 including HST; $11,040,668 net of HST recoveries) with Robert B. Somerville Co. for dig-free watermain relining in Wards 16, 21 and 24, is up for approval by the contract panel. The bids were $ 9,863,375 and $ 9,958,866.

title: 15 Glen Morris Street - Alterations to and Demolition of Heritage Attributes of a Designated Property under Sections 33 and 34 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
brief: Recommending that council approve changes to the protected heritage property at 15 Glen Morris Street, where an 8-storey residential building is proposed behind the old facades. It goes to the board for a decision.

title: 604 Bay Street (including entrance address 610 Bay Street) - Alterations to and Demolition of Heritage Attributes of a Designated Property under Sections 33 and 34 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
brief: Recommending that council approve changes and partial demolition at the protected heritage property at 604 Bay Street, plus a heritage protection agreement. It goes to the board for a decision.

title: 2255 Sheppard Avenue East - Inclusion on the Heritage Register
brief: Adding 2255 Sheppard Avenue East to the city's Heritage Register. It goes to the board for a decision. Listing marks it as historic and requires notice before demolition.

title: 132, 136, 138, 142, 144, and 148 Dundas Street West and 24 Jefferson Avenue - Inclusion on the Heritage Register
brief: Adding seven properties on Dundas Street West and Jefferson Avenue to the city's Heritage Register. It goes to the board for a decision. Listing requires notice before any demolition.

title: Property Included on the City's Heritage Register - Consideration of Objection for 1751 Bayview Avenue
brief: The owner of 1751 Bayview Avenue objects to the property being on the Heritage Register. The board is asked to review the objection and recommend whether the listing should stay.

title: 2025 Toronto Heritage Grant Awards
topics: conservation, heritage properties, restoration, subsidies and grants
brief: Approving 22 heritage grants totalling $317,000.00, matching private money for repairs to protected heritage buildings. It goes to the board for approval. The item also references $660,225.61, $10,000.00 and $20,000.00.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $317,000.00.

title: Selection of Candidates for Interview for the Committee of Adjustment
brief: This is a procedural item: a city panel is asked to select six candidates to interview for appointment to the Committee of Adjustment. No new rules here.

title: 900 Middlefield Road - Official Plan Amendment, Zoning Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City staff suggest changing planning rules to allow a five-storey apartment building with 48 homes and a small shop at 900 Middlefield Road.

title: Official Plan Amendments to Align with Provincial Legislative and Policy Changes Related to Employment Areas - Decision Report
brief: Adopting Official Plan Amendment 804 to match new provincial rules on employment areas, including redesignating 255 hectares across four office business parks. It goes to Council for approval. Council decides.

title: Thistle Down Boulevard - Parking Amendments
brief: Council would ban parking at all times on the inner loop of Thistle Down Boulevard and update parking rules on the outer circle, so parked cars do not block buses using the new speed cushions.

title: Assumption of Services, Reference Plan 66R-21894, Bastion Street, part of Grand Magazine Street and Sloping Sky Mews
brief: Council will vote on taking over roads and services on Bastion Street and nearby streets in Fort York. Construction is complete and guarantees expired.

title: 23-29 Greenbriar Road - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Approval of tearing down 22 rental homes at 23-29 Greenbriar Road and replacing them in the new building, with tenant help to return at similar rents is before council. The item lists $20,000.00.

title: 21-25 Windsor Street, 18 Buckingham Street, 60 Newcastle Street and 95 Portland Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: buildings, emergency housing, official plan amendments, rezoning
brief: Council would approve planning changes for three blocks near Windsor, Buckingham, Newcastle, and Portland Streets, including a 36- and 42-storey mixed-use building with 933 homes and a 14-storey building with 184 affordable co-op homes.

title: 1798, 1800, 1802, 1804, 1806, 1808, and 1812 Weston Road - Rental Housing Demolition Application- Decision Report - Approval
brief: Council would approve tearing down six rental units at 1806 and 1812 Weston Road for a new 40-storey development, on condition that six replacement rentals are provided on the site for at least 20 years. The report cites a $20,000.00 figure.

title: 2595 St. Clair Avenue West - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: mixed use areas, official plan amendments, rezoning
brief: Council would approve planning changes at 2595 St. Clair Avenue West for an 11-storey mixed-use building plus a 20-storey tower with 505 homes, ground-floor shops, and a public plaza, with the site classed as a provincial noise area.

title: 2024 Distillery Winter Village: Post-Event Review
brief: Community council will receive a review of the 2024 Distillery Winter Village. It covers traffic, noise and 311 calls.

title: 799 Brimley Road - Zoning Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: zoning bylaw amendments, residential real estate
brief: City staff suggest changing zoning rules to allow a 24-storey building with 385 homes at 799 Brimley Road.

title: 586 Eglinton Avenue East - Official Plan Amendment Application - Appeal
brief: A revised 35-storey building is proposed at 586 Eglinton Avenue East, with a request to skip the rule that demolished office space must be replaced. The applicant appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal, and North York Community Council is asked to have the City Solicitor oppose the appeal.

title: Permanent Closure of a Portion of Montesson Street
brief: Council would permanently close part of Montesson Street, an unused section of road, so the land can be transferred to Parks and Recreation for building new park space.

title: 3194-3206 Dundas Street West - Construction Staging Area
brief: Council will vote on closing part of Dundas Street West near St. Johns Place for 24 months for construction at 3194-3206 Dundas Street West. The item lists a $3.00 fee.

title: 1251 Bridletowne Circle - City-Initiated Zoning By-law Amendment - Re-allocating Section 37 Funds within Ward 22 - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Staff suggest a city-led rule change to move $250,000 in unspent community benefit money tied to the townhouse project at 1251 Bridletowne Circle, which is fully built, toward park improvements instead. No new building is proposed. Council is asked to approve.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $250,000.

title: Dundas Street West at Dundas Street West - Traffic Regulation Amendments
brief: Council would update lane markings and turn rules at the Dundas Street West intersection, including removing the no-right-turn-on-red rule for northbound traffic and marking the easterly northbound lane as right-turn-only, to match actual road conditions.

title: St. Clair Avenue West - Pay-and-Display Parking
brief: Council would approve new paid on-street parking in an existing layby on St. Clair Avenue West in Ward 5, replacing current no-parking rules, to encourage parking turnover and support nearby businesses and the community.

title: 23-29 Greenbriar Road - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Approval of a 25-storey building with 325 homes, including 22 rental replacement units, at 23-29 Greenbriar Road is before council. Future residents would be affected.

title: 895 Lawrence Avenue East - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Appeal
brief: Staff recommend refusing a plan for three residential towers (26, 32 and 34 storeys) at 895 Lawrence Avenue East. North York Community Council is asked to adopt the refusal, keeping the site's current rules.

title: 1736 and 1746 Weston Road - Non-Residential Demolition Application
brief: Council would approve tearing down the commercial buildings at 1736 and 1746 Weston Road, with no replacement building permit issued, on condition the owner beautifies the site with clean fill, landscaping, and a construction fence.

title: Growing Glencairn Phase 1 Report: Emerging Vision and Guiding Principles
topics: land development, multi residential apartment buildings
brief: This sets the draft vision and guiding ideas for the Growing Glencairn study, which plans future growth near Glencairn Subway Station. North York Community Council is asked to endorse them so the study can move to its next phase.

title: Changes to the Rogers Road Business Improvement Area Board of Management
brief: Appointing Sonia Martinho to the Rogers Road Business Improvement Area Board of Management, under the city's public appointments policy is on council's agenda.

title: 253, 255, 259, 263 Viewmount Avenue and 12, 14, 16, 18 Romar Crescent - Official Plan Amendment, Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Appeal
topics: zoning bylaw amendments, residential real estate
brief: Two towers (35 and 39 storeys, 1,055 homes) are proposed at 253-263 Viewmount Avenue and 12-18 Romar Crescent. The applicant appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal, and North York Community Council is asked to have the City Solicitor oppose the appeal.

title: 250, 252, 254, 258 Viewmount Avenue - Official Plan Amendment, Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Appeal
brief: A 40-storey, 477-home building is proposed at 250-258 Viewmount Avenue. The applicant appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal, and North York Community Council is asked to have the City Solicitor oppose the appeal at the hearing.

title: 243-255 Consumers Road, North York - Assumption of Services, Registered Plan 66M-2545
brief: This is a procedural item: council is asked to take over the roads and city services in the 243-255 Consumers Road subdivision. No new rules here.

title: Turn Prohibitions onto Eglinton Avenue East from Brentcliffe Road and Don Avon Drive
brief: A councillor asks council to block turns onto Eglinton Avenue East from Brentcliffe Road and Don Avon Drive to cut traffic chaos from Crosstown LRT work. Drivers there would be affected.

title: Assumption of Services Fernbrook Homes (Lawrence) Limited, 66M-2569, 14 110017 WET 12 SB, Wild Rose Gardens, Creekbank Road
brief: Council would formally take over the roads and city services in the Fernbrook Homes subdivision at Wild Rose Gardens and Creekbank Road, release the developer's performance guarantee, and pass an assumption by-law.

title: Dockside Drive - Parking and Traffic Amendments
brief: Council will vote on parking changes, a 30 km/h speed limit and a new stop sign on Dockside Drive. They support the George Brown waterfront campus.

title: 77, 81 and 83 Mutual Street - Extension of Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Council will vote on extending the land-splitting exemption at 77, 81 and 83 Mutual Street for two more years. One parcel transfer remains.

title: 229 Richmond Street West - Temporary Use Zoning By-law - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Council will vote on extending the temporary patio permission at 229 Richmond Street West to December 31, 2027.
stake: Ward 10 is named in the record.

title: 72 Perth Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Council will vote on an 18-storey building with 262 homes, including 13 affordable rentals, at 72 Perth Avenue.
stake: Ward 9 is named in the record.

title: Riverdale Avenue (Non-Delegated) - Accessible Parking Space
topics: accessibility, accessible permit parking, parking spaces
brief: Council will vote on one new on-street accessible parking space on Riverdale Avenue east of Carlaw. Full council approval is needed because the TTC runs transit there.

title: 1555 Midland Avenue - Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: A rule break for 1555 Midland Avenue so 30 unsold townhouses can be sold as separate lots would be renewed, if council agrees. The break lets each townhouse owner get their own property title. No design changes are proposed.

title: 1798-1812 Weston Road - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Council would change zoning at 1798-1812 Weston Road to allow a 40-storey mixed-use building with 490 homes and ground-floor shops, with a building hold until servicing and sewer requirements are met, and six rental units replaced.

title: 11 Pleasant Boulevard - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
brief: Council will vote on sending city lawyers to oppose a proposed 17-storey building with 87 homes at 11 Pleasant Boulevard. The developer appealed after council missed its deadline.

title: Quayside Infrastructure and Public Realm Project - Construction Staging Area
brief: Council will vote on closing part of Queens Quay East and all of Small Street from June 2025 to October 2026 for the Quayside project. The item lists a $5.50 fee.

title: 123 and 123A Parkway Forest Drive - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, planning approvals, rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws
brief: Approval of a 33-storey building with 384 rental homes, including six affordable ones, at 123 and 123A Parkway Forest Drive is before council. Future renters would be affected.

title: 3386-3398 Bayview Avenue and 32 Brenham Crescent - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Appeal
brief: A plan for fifty four-storey townhomes at 3386-3398 Bayview Avenue and 32 Brenham Crescent, since staff say it breaks the city's plan, would be refused, if council agrees. The builder could appeal.

title: Approval of Recommended Retention Schedule for Accountability Records for the Auditor General's Office
brief: Council would change the accountability officers rules to set a record-keeping schedule for the Auditor General's Office, since city records cannot be destroyed without an approved schedule.

title: Waiver of the Public Appointments Policy and Appointment of a Public Member to the Larry Grossman Forest Hill Memorial Arena Board
brief: The two-term limit would be waived and Melissa Grossman re-appointed to the Larry Grossman Forest Hill Memorial Arena Board for a term ending April 2029, if council agrees. No new rules here.

title: Toronto Water 2024 Year End Capital Budget and 2025-2034 Capital Plan Adjustments
brief: Council would approve moving $32.378 million and $6.871 million in cash flows within Toronto Water's budgets to match project timelines, with no change to the total budget. The report cites figures of $32 and $6.

title: Access to Outdoor Ovens in Toronto Parks
brief: The booking fee for community use of outdoor ovens in city parks would be removed, making the fee zero, and a revised policy to reduce barriers to their use goes to council for approval.

title: Appointment of Public Member to the Toronto Hydro Board
brief: This is a procedural item: a city panel is asked to select six candidates to interview for the Toronto Hydro Board. No new rules here.
stake: About public appointments. Council sent it back for more work.

title: Service Agreements Awarded and Executed by the Medical Officer of Health for 2025
brief: For information only. Council gets the list of Toronto Public Health's 2025 contracts with community groups for programs like food security, sexual health, and dental care. No policy change is proposed.

title: 2025 Student Nutrition Program Service Subsidies
brief: City Council will vote on 2025 school food funding of $31,020,579: $5,508,378 to the Angel Foundation for Learning and $25,512,201 to the Toronto Foundation for Student Success, with $1,448,575 kept in reserve for new programs.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $31,020,579.

title: Unwin Avenue Bailey Bridge Replacement Study
brief: Replacing the temporary one-lane bridge on Unwin Avenue in the Port Lands with a new two-lane bridge so detailed design can move ahead would get council's support.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Board of Directors of TO Live
brief: The committee recommends 3 candidates for council to appoint to the TO Live board, for terms ending May 24, 2029. Candidate details are kept private.

title: Proposed Amendments to Municipal Code Chapter 669, Climate Change Goals and Governance
topics: climate change, greenhouse effect, municipal codes
brief: Staff would get more time on the climate plan, with the deadline for the next short-term net-zero action plan moved to the end of 2025, pending a council vote.

title: Authorization to Amend and Extend the License Agreement with High Park Initiatives
brief: The High Park Nature Centre's lease would be extended by 10 years, from 2025 to 2035, with a possible extension to 2045, updating the area and fees, pending a council vote.

title: Toronto Local Appeal Body - Member Complement
brief: Shrinking the Toronto Local Appeal Body from fourteen members to ten, by not replacing members as their terms end, except for the Chair. It goes to Council for a decision. Council decides.

title: Toronto Zoo Community Conservation Centre - Lease With University of Toronto Scarborough
brief: City Council will vote on a lease letting University of Toronto Scarborough run post-secondary programs in lab and classroom space at the Toronto Zoo's conservation centre.

title: 450 Rustic Road - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: Starting the legal process to give heritage protection to a rare pre-Confederation property at 450 Rustic Road, north of Highway 401. It goes to Council for a decision. If no one objects, the formal by-law can follow. Council decides.

title: 3100 Weston Road - Proposed Designation By-Law under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Consideration of Objection
brief: Standing by its earlier decision to protect 3100 Weston Road as a heritage property despite the owner's objection, and to pass the formal protection by-law before the June 8, 2025 deadline. It goes to Council for a decision. Council decides.

title: Economic Development and Culture Grants - 2024 Funding Allocation and Creative Industries Grants
topics: arts and culture, funding, subsidies and grants
brief: A Creative Industries Grants Program with two funding streams, for skills development and sector development, would be set up, and staff could disburse one-time grants to eligible people and non-profits, if council agrees.

title: Remediating Flooding and Minimizing Flood Vulnerable Areas Associated with Taylor-Massey Creek near Eglinton Avenue East between Birchmount Road and Kennedy Road
brief: A councillor wants the City Manager to work with the TTC, conservation authority, and builders on a plan to fix flooding from Taylor-Massey Creek near Eglinton Avenue East.

title: Transitioning Towards Zero-Emission Outdoor Power Equipment
brief: A way to move gas-powered tools like leaf blowers toward zero-emission options would be picked by council. Council earlier supported exploring a ban as a precaution against cumulative health and climate impacts. Without a ban it would cost about $200,000 over five years; a ban would cost about $2.88 million to start up, then $675,000 a year.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $200,000. Decided by a recorded vote, 18 in favour and 5 against — every member's position is public.

title: Development Application Fee Review
brief: Updating the fee schedule for development applications, raising what developers pay the city for reviewing their projects, starting July 1, 2025. It goes to Council for a decision. The review service costs about $80.1 million a year to run, but fees only bring in about $62.8 million. Council decides.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $715,000. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 17 in favour, none against.

title: Confirmation of Minutes
brief: This is a routine item: council checks the written record of its April 23 and 24, 2025 meeting and confirms it is correct. No new decision is asked for.

title: Support for Grants and Incentives Program - Expanding the Urban Forest on Private Lands
topics: environmental incentive programs, subsidies and grants, tree canopy
brief: Staff could sign deals to plant more trees on private land, aiming for 40 percent tree cover by 2050, and apply for federal money for the program, if council agrees.

title: Expropriation of Portions of Properties at the Rear of Jolly Way and the Rear East Side of Jenkinson Way for the Scarborough Rapid Transit Bus Replacement - Stage 2
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, buses, construction, expropriations, land acquisition, real estate transactions
brief: City Council will vote on expropriating temporary easements behind Jolly Way and Jenkinson Way for the Scarborough RT bus replacement busway.

title: Federation of Municipalities (FCM) March 2025 report to Council
brief: Councillor Ainslie introduces the Federation of Canadian Municipalities board report from March 2025, covering advocacy ahead of the 2025 federal election. Council just receives it.

title: Recommended Strategies to Address Prematurely Failing Water Meter Transmission Units
brief: A plan for replacing the City's broken water meter readers, which come from a single supplier, would take effect if council adopts it. Details are private because talks are ongoing.

title: Delegation of Development Review Related Authorities for Consolidated Linear Infrastructure Environmental Compliance Approvals
brief: The development review boss could name staff who can sign environmental forms for the City under the province's new approval process for sewer and stormwater systems, if council agrees.

title: Call to Order
brief: This is a routine item: the meeting opens with the call to order, O Canada and a moment of silence. No decision is asked for.
stake: A citywide decision. Decided by a recorded vote, 17 in favour and 3 against — every member's position is public.

title: Introduction of Committee Reports and New Business from City Officials
brief: This is a routine item: committee leaders and city staff introduce reports and new business. Council only hears them now; no decision is asked for.

title: Declarations of Interest
brief: This is a routine item: councillors say if they have a personal interest in any item, as the conflict-of-interest law requires. No decision is asked for.
stake: A citywide decision. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Petitions
brief: This is a routine item: councillors may hand in petitions from residents to be recorded. No decision is asked for.
stake: A citywide decision. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Presentations, Introductions and Announcements
brief: This is a routine item: the meeting includes presentations, introductions and announcements. Council only listens; no decision is asked for.
stake: A citywide decision. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Review of the Order Paper
brief: This is a routine item: council looks over the order paper, the list of topics for this meeting. No decision is asked for.

title: Scarborough Bluffs West Project: Environmental Assessment Agreement - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
brief: The City Manager could sign an agreement with the province and the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority to apply the Environmental Assessment Act to the Scarborough Bluffs West Project, if council agrees. Council allocated $2.912 million to the project in 2021.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $2.912 million.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with G.C. Duke Equipment Limited for the Provision of Proprietary Original Equipment Manufacturer Parts and Service for Parks and Recreation
brief: City Council will vote on an $854,771 ($869,815 net of HST recoveries) one-year G.C. Duke mower parts and service contract; source documents also list $500,000.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $854,771.

title: Award of Doc4769714345 to Royal Bank of Canada for Banking Services for the City of Toronto
brief: The General Government Committee will vote on awarding RBC the city's banking contract at $10,882,907.87 ($11,074,447.04 net of HST recoveries) for five years, or $32,648,723.60 ($33,223,341.14 net of HST recoveries) with extensions ($32,648,723.61 also listed).
stake: The official summary names a figure of $10,882,907.87.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Zamboni Company Limited for Proprietary Original Equipment Manufacturer Parts and Services for Parks and Recreation
topics: arenas, facilities, ice rinks, maintenance, purchasing
brief: City Council will vote on a $1,423,534 ($1,448,588 net of HST recoveries) five-year Zamboni parts and service contract; source documents also list $500,000.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $1,423,534.

title: Amendment to Toronto Municipal Code Chapter 219, Records, Corporate (Local Boards) Respecting  Swansea Town Hall Community Centre
brief: Council would change the corporate records rules to add the record-keeping schedule for the Swansea Town Hall Community Centre, as approved by its board.

title: Application for Approval to Expropriate Temporary Easements for the Mid-Town Toronto Storm Sewer Relief Project - Stage 1
brief: City Council will vote on starting expropriation of temporary easements on Hillhurst Boulevard and St. Clements Avenue for the Mid-Town storm sewer relief project.

title: Leaside Memorial Community Gardens: City Loan Agreement; 2020, 2021 and 2022 Settlement
brief: Council would approve a combined settlement of Leaside Gardens' 2020-2022 results, and change the city loan deal so early loan payments from extra revenues do not cause an operating shortfall. The report cites a $7.3 million figure.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $7.3 million.

title: Award of Doc4755698985 to Carla Construction and Maintenance Ltd., for Operation and Maintenance of a Passenger Transportation Shuttle Service for High Park and other Potential Parks
brief: City Council will consider licensing Carla Construction to run a passenger shuttle service in High Park for five years starting April 2026. The company would pay the city 15 per cent of the shuttle's gross revenue and run it at no cost to the city.
stake: About parks. Decided by a recorded vote, 15 in favour and 4 against — every member's position is public.

title: Metrolinx Ontario Line - Lower Don Bridge and Minton Place Portal - Temporary Lane Closures on the Don Valley Parkway and F.G. Gardiner Expressway and Temporary Delegation of Authority
brief: Council would let the transportation general manager temporarily close lanes of the Don Valley Parkway and Gardiner Expressway overnight for Ontario Line bridge and slope work from 2025 to 2027.

title: Expropriation of Property Interests at 320-326 Bloor Street West for the Spadina Station Streetcar Platform Extension - Stage 2
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, expropriations, land acquisition, properties (real estate), streetcars, transportation
brief: City Council will vote on expropriating easements at 320-326 Bloor Street West to extend the Spadina Station streetcar platform.

title: City of Toronto’s 2025 Corporate Asset Management Plan
brief: Council would adopt the city's 2025 Corporate Asset Management Plan, covering 11 types of city infrastructure, and send it to the province by the July 1, 2025 deadline. The report cites asset values of $215 billion, figures of $26 billion and $18 billion, and gap figures of $26.0, $17.9 and $8.1.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $215 billion.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Circular Materials Ontario for Authority to Pay Producer Obligation Fees the 2024 Reporting Year
brief: City Council will vote on a non-competitive contract with Circular Materials Ontario for Blue Box producer obligation fees; source documents list $500,000 and $1,000,000.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $500,000.

title: Payments Modernization Framework
brief: City Council will vote on adopting a framework for modernizing how residents pay the city, covering digital, cash, cheque and bank options.

title: Adjustments to Capital Budget, Carry Forward Funding and Future Year Commitments
brief: Council would approve carrying forward an extra $250.3 million of unspent 2024 building project money into the 2025-2034 budget, bringing the total carry-forward to $1.69 billion, plus other budget adjustments. The total 2025 capital budget would be $6.098 billion.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $1.438 billion.

title: 2025 Update on SafeTO Implementation
brief: Council would have staff keep advancing SafeTO, Toronto's 10-year community safety plan, and report back with a progress update in 2027, also shared with the Police Service Board. Phase 1 of the plan (2022–2024) is reported at $60.6 million.
stake: About funding. Decided by a recorded vote, 21 in favour and 3 against — every member's position is public.

title: 720 Humberwood Boulevard - Reallocation of Section 37 Benefit Contribution
brief: Council would redirect a $53,250 developer contribution at 720 Humberwood Boulevard from building a parking lot at Indian Line Park, which was never built and is no longer needed, toward playground equipment and related work in the park.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $53,250.

title: Management Update: Auditor General Recommendations on 9-1-1 Operations and Responses to Calls for Service by the Toronto Police Service
brief: Staff report an update on the Auditor General's suggestions to improve 9-1-1 operations and police responses to calls. Council would send the update to the Police Service Board.

title: Improved Active Transportation and Water Access to Toronto Island Park
brief: Council would set up a task force on Toronto Island access and harbour transportation, to coordinate short- and medium-term improvements, and study long-term options including a fixed link.
stake: About tourism. Decided by a recorded vote, 21 in favour and 2 against — every member's position is public.

title: Amendment to Non-Competitive Purchase Order 6052384 with OnX Enterprise Solutions Ltd for Wiring, Cabling and Hardware for the Provision of Wireless Internet Services at Various Shelter Locations
brief: City Council will vote on adding $1,250,000 ($1,272,000 net of HST recoveries) to the OnX shelter wireless internet order, raising it from $248,400 ($252,772 net of HST recoveries) to $1,498,400 ($1,524,772 net of HST recoveries); source documents also list $500,000.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $1,250,000.

title: Non-Competitive Bridge Contract with Acklands-Grainger Inc., for Supply and Delivery of Various Industrial Supplies, Equipment and Services for Various City of Toronto Divisions
brief: City Council will vote on a $3,053,675 ($3,107,420 net of HST recoveries) one-year bridge contract with Acklands-Grainger for industrial supplies; source documents also list $12,248,846 and $500,000.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $3,053,675.

title: Amendment to Non-Competitive Contract 47023030 with A Supreme Nursing and Home Care Services Inc., for Nursing Services at Various Shelter Locations
topics: emergency housing, long term care homes, purchasing
brief: City Council will vote on adding $100,000 ($101,760 net of HST recoveries) to the shelter nursing services contract, raising it from $800,000 ($814,080 net of HST recoveries) to $900,000 ($915,840 net of HST recoveries); source documents also list $500,000.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $100,000.

title: Ontario-Toronto New Deal - Advancing the Delivery of Transit Oriented Communities along the Eglinton Crosstown West Extension
brief: Council would approve giving city-owned lands to Metrolinx or another provincial body to support transit-oriented communities along the Eglinton Crosstown West Extension, in line with the Ontario-Toronto New Deal. The deal included over $4 billion in financial supports to the city. The city lands are worth an estimated $137 million to $160 million.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $4 billion. Decided by a recorded vote, 18 in favour and 5 against — every member's position is public.

title: Designating a Community Safety Zone at the Vaughan Road and Bathurst Street Corridor
brief: Council will vote on a Community Safety Zone on Bathurst Street between Vaughan Road and Austin Terrace. It would allow a southbound speed camera near a school.

title: Overview of Security Practices for Employee Access Card Photos
brief: City Council will vote on keeping confidential the security details in the follow-up report on employee access card photo practices.

title: Toronto Builds - A Policy Framework to Build More Affordable Rental Homes on Public Land
brief: Approving the Toronto Builds policy, one set of rules for building affordable rental and mixed-income housing on city-owned land, applied to all sites in the portfolio. It goes to Council for approval. Council already approved about $32.2 million in fee waivers and tax breaks for 422 affordable rental homes at 970 Kipling Avenue and 158 Borough Drive. The source text also cites $150 million, $5 billion, $4.75 billion, $7.3 billion and $5 million. Council decides.
stake: About land. Decided by a recorded vote, 17 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: Air Conditioner Pilot Program for Low-Income Seniors
topics: heating, ventilation and air conditioning systems, low income groups, seniors
brief: Approval of a summer 2025 pilot giving up to 500 portable air conditioners to low-income seniors in apartments whose health suffers in extreme heat, picked by random draw is before council.
stake: About heating. Decided by a recorded vote, 16 in favour and 2 against — every member's position is public.

title: Watermain Replacement and Sidewalk Construction on York Downs Drive from Bathurst Street to Sandringham Drive - Amendment to the Plans for Construction Project 25ECS-LU-02SU
brief: The planned new sidewalk on York Downs Drive would be dropped from the 2025 contract, after 19 of 20 nearby residents said no, if council agrees. Watermain work would still go ahead.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Support Non-Profit Affordable Rental Housing Property Acquisition - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: rental units, reserves and reserve funds
brief: A councillor wants Council to add $1,200,000.00 to the housing budget, paid by developer community benefits, to help the Kensington Market Community Land Trust buy a 26-unit affordable rental building. The Trust already has $1,600,000 in approved City funding for eight units.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $1,200,000.00.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 and Section 42 Funds for Improvements to the Jose Rizal Memorial in Earl Bales Park - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: permanent memorials, reserves and reserve funds
brief: $60,000 ($15,000.00 in the budget detail) of developer money to upgrade the Jose Rizal Memorial in Earl Bales Park is before council for approval. The bust and plaques would be turned 180 degrees to open up gathering space.

title: Providing Housing Opening Today Toronto Inc, with Section 37 Funds for Purchase of Affordable Rental Housing Building
brief: Council votes on giving Housing Opening Today Toronto Inc. $1,500,000.00 from developer community-benefit funds so the non-profit can buy a 38-unit rental building in Ward 4 and keep it affordable. MURA funding covers up to $200,000.00 per unit; the $1,500,000.00 includes $205,966.27 from 403 Keele plus $478,208.82 and $815,824.91 from other Ward 4 sources. Council decides.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $200,000.00.

title: The Development of the Proposed Demonstrations By-law
brief: The item asks City staff for details on how the proposed rules about protests near vulnerable places are being written, before Council talks about them.
stake: About by-laws. The item was withdrawn before a final decision.

title: Nominal Sublicense Agreement with Malvern Family Resource Centre for Use of a Portion of the Finch Hydro Corridor as a Community Garden
topics: community centres, community gardens, leasing, utility corridors
brief: City Council will vote on a nominal five-year land agreement letting the Malvern Family Resource Centre continue its community garden in the Finch Hydro Corridor.

title: Requesting a Fair Consultation Process Regarding the North York Centre Secondary Plan
brief: The item asks for a fair consultation on the review of the North York Centre Secondary Plan, after residents raised concerns about the survey.
stake: About Secondary Plans. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: 68 Wellesley Street East - Alterations to a Heritage Property Designated Under Part IV of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
brief: Approval of heritage changes at 68 Wellesley Street East and a heritage easement agreement for a 28-storey building is before council. The proposal is tied to a tribunal appeal.

title: Report on Options Available When Incorrect Facts or Legal Advice is Presented to Council by an Accountability Officer
brief: Council receives for information a report on what options it has when an accountability officer presents incorrect facts or legal advice to council. No decision is proposed.
stake: About accountability. Council put off deciding this item.

title: Status update of funding from the Federal and Provincial Governments for FIFA World Cup 2026
brief: The committee would have the World Cup hosting director report to the May 2025 council meeting on whether Ottawa and Ontario will help pay for hosting the FIFA World Cup 2026. Spending is capped at $340 million until funding covers the full $380 million budget. The item cites figures of $380 million, $2 billion, $1.3 billion, $700 million, $460 million and $100 million.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $3.8 billion.

title: FIFA World Cup 2026 Toronto: Procurement Plan Update
brief: Council would move ahead with the buying plan for World Cup 2026 goods and services in Toronto, and let staff negotiate and sign the vendor contracts in the private attachment.

title: Legal Services Resourcing to Expedite Priority Affordable Housing Projects
brief: Council would add more city lawyers to speed up deals for priority affordable housing projects, set target timelines for housing legal work, and report on staffing needs in the 2026 budget.

title: Office of the Integrity Commissioner - 2024 Annual Report
brief: Council receives for information the Integrity Commissioner's 2024 annual report on ethics and conduct rules for council members. No decision is proposed.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Community Matters Toronto for Mural Art on Bell Utility Boxes in Davenport - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
brief: $18,080 of developer money on eight murals on Bell utility boxes in Davenport is before council for approval. The money would go to Box Murals Inc.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for the Heliconian Club - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: arts and culture organizations, heritage properties
brief: $20,000 of developer money to the Heliconian Club for accessible washrooms at Heliconian Hall, 35 Hazelton Avenue would be granted, if council agrees. The 1876 hall is a historic women's arts venue.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Development at 43, 49, and 51 Gerrard Street West and 695 Bay Street for Public Wi-Fi in Five Toronto Community Housing Buildings - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
brief: $243,335.49 of developer money to install free public Wi-Fi in shared areas of five Toronto Community Housing buildings in Ward 11 is before council for approval.

title: 50-64 Merton Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about a 45-storey building with 581 homes at 50-64 Merton Street, involving a heritage Girl Guides building. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: 943-963 Eglinton Avenue East and 23 Brentcliffe Road - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about four buildings with 1,279 homes at 943-963 Eglinton Avenue East and 23 Brentcliffe Road. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: 3140, 3170 and 3180 Dufferin Street and 60 and 68 Apex Road - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about coordinated developments at Dufferin Street and Apex Road. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: 7-11 Rochefort Drive - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about three towers with 1,322 homes at 7-11 Rochefort Drive. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: Declaring the Office of Councillor, Ward 25 - Scarborough-Rouge Park Vacant and Filling the Vacancy
brief: After Jennifer McKelvie's resignation, council declares the Ward 25 Scarborough-Rouge Park seat vacant and chooses between appointing someone or holding a byelection. A byelection would cost $550,000.
stake: About councillors. Decided by a recorded vote, 19 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Development at 30 Tippett Road (South Lands), in Order to Fabricate and Install Branded Street Name Signs for the Downsview Neighbourhood - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Anthony Perruzza
brief: $63,488.25 of developer money to make and install about 375 branded street signs for the Downsview neighbourhood is before council for approval. The signs honour the area's aviation history.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $63,488.25.

title: Status Update on City Activities Related to the Therme Spa Project
brief: Council receives for information a notice that a report on city activities related to the Therme spa project at Ontario Place will come to the May 21-23, 2025 meeting. No decision is proposed.
stake: About projects. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Ombudsman Toronto Report: An Investigation into the City’s Response to a Vital Services Outage in a Multi-Tenant Home
brief: Staff would carry out the Ombudsman's recommendations after his investigation into the city's response to a vital-services outage at a multi-tenant home, if council agrees. The recommendations cover urgent service requests and eviction prevention.
stake: About housing. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 22 in favour, none against.

title: Under Gardiner Public Realm Plan - Multi-Use Trail Study Delivery Agreement - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
brief: A councillor wants Council to sign a deal with the Bentway Conservancy, up to $201,000, to study and design a proposed 7-kilometre trail under the Gardiner Expressway from Dufferin Street to the Don Valley Parkway.

title: Save Toronto’s School Pools - Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
brief: A councillor wants Council to ask the Ontario government to keep paying for school pools in Toronto public schools, for student swim lessons and community use.

title: Re-Opening and Amending Item 2024.IE14.4 - Cycling Network Plan - 2024 Cycling Infrastructure and Missing Sidewalk Installation - Third Quarter Update - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
brief: A councillor asks council to drop two planned bike lane sections from its earlier Cycling Network Plan decision and pause the Beltline Gap Connection while a wider transport study for the Marlee Avenue area finishes.

title: Appointment of a Public Member as Chair of the Toronto Local Appeal Body
brief: Appointing Nazila Atarodi West as chair of the Toronto Local Appeal Body, for a term ending May 24, 2029 is on council's agenda. Details are confidential.

title: Commencing Public Consultations for Communities Impacted by New Shelter Locations - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Parthi Kandavel
brief: A separate public meeting for each of the six planned new shelter sites, instead of one general process, would be held, if council agrees. The local councillor would help set the date and format.
stake: About homelessness. Decided by a recorded vote, 10 in favour and 5 against — every member's position is public.

title: Accepting a Donation from Tennis Canada to Enhance the Tennis Courts at Malvern Park - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
brief: Up to $100,000.00 from Tennis Canada to improve the tennis courts at Malvern Park in 2025 would be accepted, if council agrees. No city money would be needed for the donated portion.

title: Requesting Funding Support from Federal and Provincial Governments for Enhanced Festival Safety and Security - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: federal governments, festivals and special events, funding, provincial governments, safety
brief: A call on Ottawa and Ontario to create new funding programs for festival safety and security goes to council. The City already put $3.85 million toward festival safety in 2025.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $3.85 million.

title: Support for the Canadian Tire Jumpstart Multi-Year Sport Court Refurbishment Initiative - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
brief: The Mayor asks council to accept a donation of up to $3.5 million over five years from Canadian Tire Jumpstart Charities to fix up outdoor basketball and multi-sport courts across Toronto.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $3.5 million.

title: Accepting a Donation from Spin Master for Sumach-Shuter Parkette Playground Enhancements - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
brief: Spin Master would give the City $50,000 ($50,000.00) to upgrade the playground at Sumach-Shuter Parkette, 485 Shuter Street. Council decides whether to accept the donation.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $50,000.

title: Ensuring Transparency and Accountability in the Mayor’s Office - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor Vincent Crisanti
brief: The motion asks the Mayor to start livestreaming press conferences online again, including questions from the media, and to let all councillors and staff attend. Council would make the request to the Mayor's office.
stake: About accountability. Decided by a recorded vote, 7 in favour and 17 against — every member's position is public.

title: Changes to the Marlee-Glencairn Study - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
brief: The Growing Glencairn Study would be renamed to the Growing Marlee-Glencairn Study, honouring the Marlee Ville name, if council agrees. Staff would also add growth data from nearby areas, like Eglinton Avenue West, to the study.
stake: Ward 8 is named in the record.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Ward 13 2024 Participatory Budgeting Projects for Cabbagetown, Winchester Park, and St. James Town - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
brief: Ward 13 residents voted on how to spend $750,000 of developer money, and council is asked to fund the six winners: park benches, mosaics, a gateway sculpture and art pieces. Project costs are listed as $80,000, $75,000, $160,000, $100,000.00, $200,000.00 and $300,000.00 — the $200,000 is for gateway sculptures at three Cabbagetown intersections.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $750,000.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Colborne Street Area Streetscape Improvements - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
brief: $1,250,000 of developer money on street upgrades in Old Town: $850,000 to Transportation Services and $400,000 to the local business group (budget lines show $719,420.43 and $130,579.57) is before council for approval. The work covers Colborne Street, Leader Lane and Colborne Lane.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $1,250,000.

title: Securing a Dedicated School Location to Support Toronto’s Film Industry - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: television industry, community use of schools
brief: Turning a closed school into a dedicated film and TV production site, working with the Toronto Lands Corporation, would be explored, if council agrees. The film industry spent a record $2.6 billion in Toronto in 2022 and employs over 30,000 people.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $2.6 billion. Decided by a recorded vote, 22 in favour and 2 against — every member's position is public.

title: Renaming Sumach-Shuter Parkette to Louis March Park - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
brief: Sumach-Shuter Parkette would be renamed to Louis March Park, with new signs put up, if council agrees. Louis March founded the Zero Gun Violence Movement and died July 20, 2024.
stake: Ward 13 is named in the record. Decided by a recorded vote, 22 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: Introduction of General Bills and Confirming Bills
brief: This is a procedural step: City Council will introduce general bills and confirming bills, which turn approved decisions into official bylaws. No new policy is decided.

title: Award of Doc4461777056 to Firetech Manufacturing Ltd., for the Non-Excusive Supply and Delivery of Ambulance Response Bags for Toronto Paramedic Services
topics: ambulances, contracts, emergency medical services, paramedics, purchasing
brief: A three-year, $2,202,570 contract ($2,488,904 including HST; $2,241,336 net of HST recoveries) with Firetech Manufacturing for ambulance response bags, with one optional two-year extension, is up for approval by the contract panel. The extension is $764,544 / $863,935 / $778,000; the five-year total is $2,967,114 / $3,352,839 / $3,019,336.

title: Award of Doc4815572097 to Toronto Metropolitan University and Inclusive Kind Inc., for the Equity Learning and Training Services for People and Equity
topics: contracts, equity, purchasing, workplace training and development

title: Award of Doc4892449484 to Acapulco Pools Limited for the Repair and Maintenance for City Water Slides for the Parks and Recreation
topics: contracts, recreational facilities, sports facilities, water parks
brief: A one-year, $108,618 contract ($122,738 including HST; $110,530 net of HST recoveries) with Acapulco Pools for water slide repairs, with four optional renewal years, is up for approval by the contract panel. The bids were $90,515.00 and $958,210.00; the option years are $111,877 / $126,420 / $113,846, $115,233 / $130,213 / $117,261, $118,690 / $134,119 / $120,779 and $122,251 / $138,143 / $124,402, for a five-year total of $576,668 / $651,635 / $586,817.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $90,515.00.

title: Award of Doc4930010603 to GIP Paving for Basement Flooding Protection Program, Phase 4 Various Assignments for Engineering and Construction Services
brief: A $17,797,115 contract ($20,110,740 including HST; $18,110,344 net of HST recoveries) with GIP Paving for basement flooding protection work, is up for approval by the contract panel. The five bids were $15,475,752.12, $17,429,375.02, $17,986,939.84, $18,459,646.19 and $19,919,924.50.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $15,475,752.12.

title: Award of Doc4953590192 to Lomco Limited for Tennis Courts State of Good Repair Rehabilitation for Seneca Hill Park for Parks and Recreation
topics: contracts, purchasing, recreational facilities, repairs, sports facilities, tennis courts
brief: A $1,408,097 contract ($1,591,150 including HST; $1,432,880 net of HST recoveries) with Lomco Limited for tennis court repairs at Seneca Hill Park, is up for approval by the contract panel. The five bids were $1,153,997.00, $1,252,521.00, $1,252,480.50, $1,298,525.00 and $1,289,766.58.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $1,153,997.00.

title: Award of Doc4956515637 to 614128 Ontario Ltd., operating as Trisan Construction for Basement Flooding Protection Program, Phase 4 Various Assignments for Engineering and Construction Services
brief: A $16,556,539 contract ($18,708,889 including HST; $16,847,934 net of HST recoveries) with Trisan Construction for basement flooding protection work, is up for approval by the contract panel. title: Proposed By-law Amendment to Provide Access to Social Infrastructure
brief: The streets and sidewalks bylaw to address harassment near places of worship, faith-based schools and cultural institutions, effective July 2, 2025 would be amended, if council agrees. Up to $200,000 is set aside for public education and outreach about the change.
stake: About by-laws. Decided by a recorded vote, 16 in favour and 9 against — every member's position is public.

title: Piloting a Red Tape Hotline for Businesses - by Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
brief: A nine-month Red Tape Hotline test where Toronto businesses can report bad city rules and permit delays would be run, if council agrees. Staff would study the reports and suggest fixes by early 2026.

title: Establishing an Annual Mayor’s Savings Challenge - by Councillor Shelley Carroll, Seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
brief: A yearly Mayor's Savings Challenge honouring city staff whose ideas save money or improve services would be created, if council agrees. Winners get non-cash recognition from the Mayor.

title: Tamil Genocide Monument in Scarborough - by Councillor Parthi Kandavel, seconded by Councillor Councillor Josh Matlow
brief: A Scarborough park site for a Tamil Genocide Monument, working with the National Council of Canadian Tamils, would be sought, if council agrees. Staff would report to Scarborough Community Council late in 2025.

stake: The official summary names a figure of $125,000.

stake: The official summary names a figure of $2.6 billion.

title: Assessing Sunshine List Reporting Requirements and Incentive Programs of City Agencies and Corporations - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
brief: Yearly salary reports for city agencies not covered by Ontario's public Sunshine List would be published, if council agrees. The reports would include agencies that claim they are exempt.

title: Administrative Penalty Administration During Possible Postal Strike - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Stephen Holyday
brief: Drivers would get 60 days instead of 30 to respond to red-light and speed-camera tickets if a postal strike disrupts mail, pending a council vote. The change only applies during a mail disruption.
