title: Finch Avenue East and Baylawn Drive - Temporary Traffic Control Signals
brief: Approval of temporary traffic lights at Finch Avenue East and Baylawn Drive from May 2025 to December 2031 is before council. They are needed while a rail bridge is built over the road.

title: 18A Downsview Park Boulevard - Introduction of Overnight On-Street Permit Parking - Permit Area
brief: Overnight permit parking on Downsview Park Boulevard between George Butchart Drive and Stanley Greene Boulevard, from 12:01 a.m. to 7:00 a.m. Drivers there would be affected would be allowed, if council agrees.

title: 230 and 240 The Donway West - Exclusion of the Development from the Permit Parking Program
brief: The development at 230 and 240 The Donway West would be blocked from using any future on-street permit parking on the street or in the area, if council agrees. Residents there would be affected.

title: 2491 Lake Shore Boulevard West - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: mixed use areas, rezoning, zoning bylaws
brief: Council would change zoning at 2491 Lake Shore Boulevard West to allow a nine-storey mixed-use building with 151 homes and ground-floor shops, including eight rental replacement units for existing renters and an on-site park.

title: Assumption of Services, Registered Plan 66M-2530, 11 286680 STE 17 SB, Somerset Wallace Developments Ltd., Sousa Mendes Street, Macaulay Avenue Extension, Wallace Avenue Subdivision
brief: Council will vote on taking over the roads and services in the Wallace Avenue subdivision, including Sousa Mendes Street. The developer built them under its agreement with the City.

title: Confirmation of Minutes
brief: This is a routine item: council checks the written record of its March 26 and 27, 2025 meeting and confirms it is correct. No new decision is asked for.

title: Introduction of Committee Reports and New Business from the Mayor and City Officials
brief: This is a routine item: committee leaders and city staff introduce reports and new business. Council only hears them now; no decision is asked for.

title: Declarations of Interest
brief: This is a routine item: councillors say if they have a personal interest in any item, as the conflict-of-interest law requires. No decision is asked for.
stake: A citywide decision. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Petitions
brief: This is a routine item: councillors may hand in petitions from residents to be recorded. No decision is asked for.
stake: A citywide decision. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Presentations, Introductions and Announcements
brief: This is a routine item: the meeting includes presentations, introductions and announcements. Council only listens; no decision is asked for.
stake: A citywide decision. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Review of the Order Paper
brief: This is a routine item: council looks over the order paper, the list of topics for this meeting. No decision is asked for.
stake: A citywide decision. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 24 in favour, none against.

title: Call to Order
brief: This is a routine item: the meeting opens with the call to order, O Canada and a moment of silence. No decision is asked for.

title: Changes to the Mount Pleasant Village Business Improvement Area Board of Management
topics: boards of management, business improvement areas
business improvement associations, boards of directors
brief: Gregory Heller from the Mount Pleasant Village Business Improvement Area Board of Management, under the city's BIA rules would be removed, if council agrees.

title: Amendments to Toronto Municipal Code Chapter 217, Records, Corporate (City)
brief: This is procedural: City Council will vote on adding a records retention schedule for documents on the Mayor's special powers and duties.

title: 2 Tippett Road - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Appeal Report
topics: official plan amendments, residential tenants, rezoning
brief: A request to have the city's lawyer oppose a 33-storey, 417-home tower proposed at 2 Tippett Road at the Ontario Land Tribunal goes to council. The builder appealed after council did not decide in time.

title: 3377 Bayview Avenue, Draft Plan of Subdivision Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Approval of a subdivision plan at 3377 Bayview Avenue with ten blocks, including homes, two parks, a large green space, and land kept by Tyndale University is before council. Future residents would be affected.

title: 2491 Lake Shore Boulevard West - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: demolitions, development, rental housing, rezoning, zoning bylaws
brief: Council would approve tearing down eight rental units at 2491 Lake Shore Boulevard West, on condition that eight replacement rentals are provided on the site for at least 20 years and existing tenants get help moving. The report cites a $20,000.00 figure.

title: 1 Broadlands Boulevard - Zoning By-law Amendment Application- Decision Report - Approval
brief: Approval of a three-storey building with 21 homes at 1 Broadlands Boulevard in North York is before council. Future residents would be affected.
stake: About construction. Decided by a recorded vote, 19 in favour and 2 against — every member's position is public.

title: 150 The Donway West and 4 Overland Drive - Zoning Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Approval of two new rental buildings with 230 homes, a 15-storey tower and a nine-storey tower, at 150 The Donway West and 4 Overland Drive is before council. Future renters would be affected.

title: 54-70 Brownlow Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Council will vote on a 59-storey residential building at 54-70 Brownlow Avenue. Nine homes would be demolished, including two rentals.

title: Manse Road - U-Turn Prohibition
brief: Staff suggest banning U-turns both ways on Manse Road between Hainford Street and Deanscroft Square to make it safer, especially near Joseph Brant Public School. Since buses run there, this needs a City Council vote.

title: Pritchard Avenue - Accessible Parking Space
brief: Council would approve an on-street accessible parking space on the north side of Pritchard Avenue, just east of Mariposa Avenue, for use at all times.

title: Duncan Mill Road - Pedestrian Crossing Protection
topics: pedestrian crossovers, pedestrian infrastructure, road safety
brief: Council is asked not to install a pedestrian crossing on Duncan Mill Road about 200 metres east of Lesmill Road. Walkers there would be affected.

title: 152-164 Bathurst Street and 623-627 Richmond Street West - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Council will vote on a 29-storey building with 362 homes, including nine affordable rentals, at 152-164 Bathurst Street. The site was approved for 18 storeys in 2023.

title: 1 Fallingbrook Road - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property Under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: Approval of changes to the heritage home at 1 Fallingbrook Road, including a modern addition is before council. Since the home is protected by heritage law, council must give permission.

title: 1925 Victoria Park Avenue - Public Art Plan
brief: Approval of the public art plan for the building at 1925 Victoria Park Avenue, which says how the builder will add artwork to the north-facing wall is before council. Approval is a required step for the project.

title: 5933 and 5951 Steeles Avenue East - Alterations to Heritage Properties and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
brief: Changes to two heritage homes at 5933 and 5951 Steeles Avenue East go to council for approval, along with a deal protecting them. The changes are part of a bigger building plan. Council permission is required by law.

title: 2655 Lawrence Avenue East - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City staff suggest changing zoning rules to allow two towers of 18 and 28 storeys plus eight townhouses at 2655 Lawrence Avenue East, with 412 homes and shops. The same plan was approved in 2018 but never took effect.

title: East Avenue - Road Safety Review
brief: This is a routine item: council hears a road safety review of East Avenue near William G. Davis Junior Public School. Staff did the review after community council asked. Nothing is decided.

title: 2221 and 2223 Kennedy Road and 3, 5 and 7 Collingwood Street - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City staff suggest changing planning rules to allow three four-storey townhouse buildings with 68 homes at 2221-2223 Kennedy Road and 3-7 Collingwood Street.

title: Scarborough Busway - On-Street Measures to Support Busway Operations
brief: Approval of road changes on Eglinton Avenue East and a new traffic light to support the Scarborough Busway, the dedicated bus route replacing the old SRT line is before council. The changes would give buses priority.
stake: About bus routes. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 20 in favour, none against.

title: 30, 40, 43, 44 and 45 Price Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Council will vote on a 3-storey expansion of the Toronto Lawn and Tennis Club at 30-45 Price Street. Parts of the existing buildings would be demolished.

title: 43, 44 and 45 Price Street - Demolition of Buildings Within the South Rosedale Heritage Conservation District and Approval of Replacement Buildings
brief: Council will vote on demolishing three unrated buildings at 43-45 Price Street in a heritage district. Heritage rules require council's permission.

title: Corridor Safety Review Update - Mortimer Avenue, between Pape Avenue and Broadview Avenue
brief: Council will receive an update on the safety review for Mortimer Avenue between Pape and Broadview. No policy change is proposed.

title: 78 and 80 Nassau Street - Inclusion on the Heritage Register
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties
brief: Council will vote on adding the 1885-era houses at 78 and 80 Nassau Street to the Heritage Register. Listing notes their heritage value but does not block changes.

title: 120 Peter Street, 122-124 Peter Street, 126-128 Peter Street and 357-359 Richmond Street West - Alterations to, Demolition and Construction of, Buildings under Sections 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Amend a Heritage Easement Agreement
brief: Council will vote on changes to heritage properties on Peter Street and Richmond Street West for a new 40-storey building. One heritage house would be altered and others demolished.

title: 50-64 Merton Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Appeal Report
brief: Council will vote on sending city lawyers to oppose an appeal over the 45-storey building at 50-64 Merton Street. Talks with the developer continue.

title: 111 Peter Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Council will vote on a 52-storey tower with 852 homes at 111 Peter Street. The project includes 24 affordable rental homes.
stake: About rental housing. Decided by a recorded vote, 23 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: 158 Sterling Road (Blocks 5B, 5C and 5D) and 190 Sterling Road (Block 3B) - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: by-laws, official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning
brief: Council will vote on two towers of 28 and 31 storeys with 745 homes at 158 and 190 Sterling Road. A 62-space childcare centre would go to the City.
stake: About by-laws. Decided by a recorded vote, 20 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: Accessible Parking Space - April 2025 (Non-Delegated)
brief: Council will vote on the monthly list of on-street accessible parking spaces for people with disabilities. Full council approval is needed because the TTC runs transit there.

title: 215 Lake Shore Boulevard East Phase 1 - Official Plan and  Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Council will vote on adding five storeys to three approved towers at 215 Lake Shore Boulevard East. The project adds 114 homes, including about 16 affordable rentals. The item lists $85,000 in secured benefits.

title: 707 Dundas Street West and 327 Bathurst Street - City-initiated Official Plan Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Council will vote on redesignating the Scadding Court Community Centre and Sanderson Library lands for mixed use. The change would allow redevelopment with affordable housing.

title: Review of Bid Award Panel
brief: City Council will vote on eliminating the Bid Award Panel and giving the Chief Procurement Officer authority to award competitive contracts up to $30 million; source documents list $500,000, $20 million, $133,800, and $30 million.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $500,000. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 17 in favour, none against.

title: Safety Barriers Along the Leaside Bridge - Feasibility Study Update
brief: The committee will get a study on adding permanent safety barriers to the Leaside Bridge, a high-risk spot. No new rules are proposed. Design work and public input would cost about $500,000, to be requested in a future capital budget.
stake: About bridges. Decided by a recorded vote, 22 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: Implementation Guidelines for Rental Replacement
brief: Adopting the Rental Replacement Handbook as the new guide for how rent gap help is calculated and how tenant protections apply when rental housing is torn down. It goes to Council for approval. Council decides.
stake: About rental housing. Decided by a recorded vote, 19 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: 309-311 and 349 George Street - Alterations to Designated Heritage Properties under Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: Council will vote on the heritage plan for City-owned properties at 309-311 and 349 George Street. The plan supports a new 10-storey institutional building.

title: 309-349 George Street - City-Initiated Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws
brief: Council will vote on a City-led 10-storey building at 309-349 George Street. It would have shelter beds, long-term care beds and 70 affordable rentals.

title: Amending existing Zoning By-law Section 37 Schedules to Facilitate Purchase of Community Space in the Church-Wellesley Village
brief: Council will vote on letting developer funds be used to buy community space for 2SLGBTQ+ non-profits in Church-Wellesley. Staff are evaluating a property.

title: 315-325 Front Street West - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Council will vote on a four-building development with 1,793 homes at 315-325 Front Street West. The item lists secured benefits of $150,000.00, $1,250,000, $250,000 and $1,000,000.00.

title: 847-855 Kingston Road - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
brief: Council will vote on sending city lawyers to oppose a proposed 11-storey building with 99 homes at 847-855 Kingston Road. The developer appealed after council missed its deadline.

title: Litigation Arising from the Rehabilitation of Section 1 of the F.G. Gardiner Expressway (Jarvis Street to Cherry Street)
topics: bridge maintenance, bridge rehabilitation, bridges, damages, maintenance
brief: City Council will consider the city's legal action against WSP Canada over alleged design errors in the Gardiner Expressway Section 1 rehabilitation.

title: Award of Doc4556210399 to Multiple Suppliers for Fire and Life Safety, Inspection, Test and Maintenance for Fire Alarm, Sprinkler, Standpipe, Special Suppression, Fire Extinguisher, and Fire Hydrants for Various City Divisions
topics: fire extinguishers, fire hoses, fire hydrants, fire sprinklers, inspection
stake: The official summary names a figure of $110,558,332.

title: Non-Competitive Procurement Contracts with Mister Safety Shoes Inc operating as Mister Safety Shoes and Kodiak Group Holdings operating as Work Authority for the Non-Exclusive Supply and Fitting of Various New Safety Footwear and Related Items for Various City of Toronto Divisions
brief: City Council will vote on $12,505,494 ($12,725,591 net of HST recoveries) in non-competitive safety footwear contracts with Mister Safety Shoes and Work Authority, split $8,182,012 ($8,326,016 net of HST recoveries) and $4,323,482 ($4,399,575 net of HST recoveries); source documents also list $500,000.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $12,505,494.

title: Addressing Dangerous Dogs - Response to 2024.EC16.3
topics: dogs, improvement, investigation, policies and procedures
brief: The animals bylaw would be amended so dangerous dog warning signs can be required on an owner's property and on apartment or condo unit doors, and staff would publish clearer guidance on dangerous dog decisions, if council agrees.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Salesforce.com Canada Corporation for Proprietary Tableau Software Licenses, Training, Maintenance and Support Services
brief: City Council will vote on a non-competitive Salesforce Canada contract for Tableau licences, training and support, the city's main data visualization tool; source documents list $500,000.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $500,000.

title: Non-competitive Contracts with SAP Canada Incorporated for Proprietary System Software Licenses, Cloud Subscriptions, and Related Services
brief: City Council will vote on non-competitive SAP Canada contracts for software licences, cloud subscriptions and services that run the city's core finance and HR systems; source documents list $500,000.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $500,000.

title: Changing the Night of Garbage Collection for the West-End (Ossington/Queen West/College Promenade Areas)
topics: garbage, garbage collection, waste, waste collection
brief: Moving garbage pickup in Ossington, Queen West, and College Promenade from Thursday nights to a quieter night like Monday, after asking residents and shops, would be considered by council.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Rowland Emergency Vehicle Products Inc for the provision of Stryker Powered Stretchers with all Components, Accessories, and Repairs
brief: City Council will vote on a $27,195,964 ($27,674,613 net of HST recoveries), precisely $27,195,964.37 ($27,674,613.34 net of HST recoveries), three-year Stryker stretcher contract with Rowland Emergency for paramedics; source documents also list $500,000.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $27,195,964.

title: Authority to Enter into Municipal Housing Project Facility Agreements with Community Housing Providers
brief: Setting up a new chapter in the city's rulebook for housing programs and sign facility deals with community housing providers to support the upkeep of existing community housing. It goes to Council for a decision. Council decides.

title: Toronto's Academic Housing Strategy - Improving Housing Outcomes for Post-Secondary Students
brief: Adopting the Academic Housing Strategy, a plan built with colleges and universities to increase student housing in Toronto, with a five-year rollout and yearly updates. It goes to Council for approval. Council decides.
stake: About housing. Decided by a recorded vote, 20 in favour and 2 against — every member's position is public.

title: Enhancing Capital Construction Delivery
brief: Staff would run big construction projects better, with faster on-site decisions and better updates to neighbours, if council agrees. The City plans over $2 billion in capital spending in 2025, and now delivers over $1 billion a year. The plan would cost $1.314 million for seven temporary staff positions.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $2 billion. Decided by a recorded vote, 21 in favour and 3 against — every member's position is public.

title: 750, 752, and 756-758 Yonge Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: Starting the legal process to give heritage protection to four adjacent properties at 750, 752, 756 and 758 Yonge Street. It goes to Council for a decision. If no one objects, formal by-laws can follow. Council decides.

title: Basement Flooding Protection Program Status Update
brief: The Basement Flooding Protection Program, which builds pipes and tanks to cut urban flooding, would speed up, with staff reporting on the money needed through the 2026 budget, if council agrees. The plan's projects are valued at about $18 billion. Spending $50 million more a year could speed up the work by half, helping about 1,000 more homes a year.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $18 billion.

title: Dufferin Organics Processing Facility Update and Contingency Processing Capacity
brief: Staff could spend up to $12,500,000 on backup deals with outside processors for green bin organics, since the City's two plants cannot handle it all, if council agrees. No single vendor could get more than $2,500,000 of the $12,500,000.

title: Request for Temporary Delegation to the General Manager, Transportation Services, to Approve Temporary Road Closures Up To and Including 365 Consecutive Days for Toronto Transit Commission Traction Power Upgrade Projects
brief: The General Manager of Transportation Services could approve road closures of up to a year for Easier Access construction projects through 2026 and for TTC traction power upgrades through 2032, if council agrees. The manager would not have to notify the local ward councillor about the closures first.

title: Transition of the Blue Box Program to Extended Producer Responsibility: Post-Transition Update
topics: blue bins, service delivery, solid waste management
recycling boxes, solid waste management planning
brief: Staff could sign long-term garbage deals for City transfer stations, with an update coming on the Blue Box program shifting to producer responsibility from 2026, if council agrees.

title: 1 Dundas Street East: Amendments to the Sign By-law
brief: Updating the sign rules for 1 Dundas Street East (Sankofa Square) to use the current name in the regulations and simplify the sign permit process. It goes to Council for a decision. Council decides.
stake: About change. Decided by a recorded vote, 21 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: 7-9 Wardlaw Crescent - City-Initiated Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Allowing a four-storey building with 51 affordable rental homes and on-site support services at 7-9 Wardlaw Crescent in Rexdale. It goes to Council for a decision. Council decides.

title: Annual Strategic Capital Coordination Report
topics: capital budgets, traffic management, transportation infrastructure
brief: The committee will get the first yearly report from the office that coordinates construction across City teams, utilities, and partners.

title: Business Improvement Areas (BIAs) - 2025 Operating Budgets - Report 2
topics: business improvement associations, budgets and accounts
brief: The 2025 operating budgets and levy requirements for a second list of Business Improvement Areas would be adopted and certified, letting the city collect a special levy from businesses in those areas, if council agrees.

title: Swansea Mews Initial Development Proposal
brief: Approving the first rebuild plan for Swansea Mews, the 154-unit Toronto Community Housing site at the Queensway and Windermere Avenue that was emptied after a structural failure, so the unliveable units can be torn down and the site renewed. It goes to Council for approval. Council decides.

title: Council Member Appointments to the Canadian National Exhibition Association, Municipal Section and Board of Directors
brief: This is a routine item: the Striking Committee suggests five councillors for the Canadian National Exhibition Association board, for a one-year term starting spring 2025. Council makes the final choices.

title: Council Member Appointments to the Federation of Canadian Municipalities Board of Directors
brief: This is a routine item: the Striking Committee suggests two councillors for the Federation of Canadian Municipalities board, for a term from June 2025 to 2026. Council makes the final choices.

title: Council Member Appointment to Fill a Vacancy on the Association of Municipalities of Ontario Board of Directors
brief: This is a routine item: the Striking Committee suggests a councillor to fill an empty seat on the Association of Municipalities of Ontario board until November 2026. Council makes the final choice.

title: Continuation of Appointed Public Member as Chair of the Benefit Fund Committee of the Toronto Fire Department Superannuation and Benefit Fund
brief: William Chinery's term as chair of the Toronto Fire Department pension and benefit fund committee to November 14, 2026 would be extended, pending a council vote. Details are confidential.

title: 2025 Education Property Tax Levy and Clawback Rate By-Law
brief: Council would adopt the 2025 education property tax rates, totalling $2,189,040,814 for schools, which the city collects for the province. The report also cites a $500 figure and a $4,221,673 figure. This lets the city send out final property tax bills.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $500. Decided by a recorded vote, 18 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: Toronto's Dog Off-Leash Strategy: A Citywide Approach to Dogs Off-Leash Areas
topics: city initiatives, dog off-leash areas, public safety & protection (sc)
brief: Approval of a new citywide plan for dog off-leash areas, covering how they are planned, built, and kept up, plus rules for commercial dog walkers is before council. It would replace the 2010 policy.

title: Congestion Management Plan - 2025 Update
brief: Staff would report on whether traffic measures for Gardiner and King/Church construction are working, and the green business program could widen its idea of a local green company, if council agrees. A one-year $400,000 deal with pointA to run the Smart Commute program would also be approved.
stake: About city initiatives. Decided by a recorded vote, 17 in favour and 7 against — every member's position is public.

title: Advancing the George Street Revitalization Project
brief: Council would move ahead with building Phase 1 of the George Street Revitalization project using a city-run approach, within budget. It combines shelter services, a care home, supportive housing, and a community hub.
stake: About budgets. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 25 in favour, none against.

title: Amendments to Municipal Code Chapter 190, Polling and Notification including Lowering the Polling Age
brief: Council would change the polling rules to lower the minimum voting age in neighbourhood polls from 18 to 16, except for business area polls, and make other changes to make voting easier.
stake: About municipal codes. Decided by a recorded vote, 18 in favour and 3 against — every member's position is public.

title: Appointment of a Public Member to the Dangerous Dog Review Tribunal
brief: Appointing Sophia Davis to the Dangerous Dog Review Tribunal for a term from March 28, 2025 to November 14, 2026 is on council's agenda.

title: Report from the Mayor’s Designate to the Sao Paulo Urban Summit and Urban 20 Rio Summit
brief: Councillor Bravo reports on attending the Sao Paulo Urban Summit and the Urban 20 Rio Summit in Brazil in 2024 as the Mayor's stand-in, representing Toronto at international city meetings. Council just receives it.

title: Towards a Beautiful City - A Path Forward
brief: Council would have city planning, transportation, and parks staff report back late in 2025 on five priority actions to make Toronto's public spaces, parks, and buildings more beautiful and well-designed.

title: Appointment of a Public Member to the Housing Rights Advisory Committee
brief: The Civic Appointments Committee picks 5 people to interview for the Housing Rights Advisory Committee, then recommends one to council. Candidate names are kept private.

title: Naming Recommendation for a Parcel of Land within Lawrence Park Ravine to "Jaye Robinson Park"
topics: facility naming, naming, parkettes, parks, public realm
brief: A piece of land in Lawrence Park Ravine would be named "Jaye Robinson Park" after the late Councillor Jaye Robinson, if council agrees. Park users would see the new name.
stake: About facility naming. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 22 in favour, none against.

title: Requiring Metrolinx to Develop a Heavy Truck Safety Plan - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
brief: After two collisions involving heavy construction vehicles on Ontario Line work, council is asked to direct the City Manager to ask Metrolinx for a Heavy Truck Safety Plan by April 11, 2025, and make it a condition of city permits in Ward 14.

title: 1117 Queen Street West - Alterations to a Designated Property and Demolition of Heritage Attributes of a Building on a Designated Property under Sections 33 and 34(1)1 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about heritage changes at 1117 Queen Street West. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: Winter Maintenance on Heathfield Drive Path
brief: A councillor asks council to have staff clear snow on the Heathfield Drive Path between Hill Crescent and Sylvan Drive each winter. The path is a key walking route to transit. Council is asked to approve.

title: Design Revision to the Woodbine Cycle Track
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, public transit, transportation
brief: Council will vote on removing curbs along the Woodbine Avenue bike lane near Woodbine station. This would help TTC shuttle buses during subway outages.

title: Appointment of a Public Member to the Aboriginal Affairs Advisory Committee
brief: Appointing a public member from the Toronto Aboriginal Support Services Council to the Aboriginal Affairs Advisory Committee, for a term ending November 14, 2026 is on council's agenda.

title: Dovercourt Road - Parking Amendments
brief: Council will vote on parking changes on Dovercourt Road, including no-stopping zones near Hallam Street and Geary Avenue. Residents reported blocked access.

title: Establishing The City of Toronto Mayor's Awards for Artificial Intelligence Innovation within City Divisions, Agencies, and Boards
brief: City Council will consider creating Mayor's Awards for Artificial Intelligence Innovation to recognize AI work by city divisions, agencies and boards.

title: 1304-1318 King Street West and 143-145 Cowan Avenue - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about a proposed 21-storey building with 263 homes at 1304-1318 King Street West. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: Requesting a Transparent, Clear and Fair Consultation Process Regarding the “Proposed Demonstrations By-law to Protect Vulnerable Institutions”
brief: The item asks for a fair public consultation on the proposed rules about protests near vulnerable places, after a letter from the Canadian Civil Liberties Association.
stake: About by-laws. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Mayor’s Economic Action Plan in Response to United States Tariffs - Update to Council
brief: Council would have the City Manager and Economic Development keep advancing the Mayor's economic plan in response to US tariffs, and report back to council in July 2025 on progress.
stake: About financial reports. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 22 in favour, none against.

title: 271 Front Street East, 25 Berkeley Street, and 44 Parliament Street - Expropriation of City-owned Lands by Metrolinx for Transit Purposes
brief: Metrolinx expropriated city-owned lands at 271 Front Street East, 25 Berkeley Street and part of 44 Parliament Street for the Ontario Line's Corktown station. The City Solicitor asks council to adopt confidential recommendations.

title: 1117 Queen Street West - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on the tribunal case about planning and zoning applications for 1117 Queen Street West. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: 4151 to 4155 Sheppard Avenue East and 5 Lamont Avenue - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about a proposed 46-storey building at 4151-4155 Sheppard Avenue East. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: Build More Homes: Identifying Opportunities for More Purpose-Built Rental Housing
brief: Council would have staff resume reviewing remaining applications under the rental housing incentives program, and report by July 2025 on projects that could get long-term development charge delays. The report cites a $7.3 billion figure.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $7.3 billion. Decided by a recorded vote, 19 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: Results of Collective Bargaining Negotiations between the City of Toronto and The Carpenters' District Council of Ontario/United Brotherhood of Carpenters and Joiners of America
brief: The new labour agreement with the Carpenters' District Council of Ontario would be ratified by council. The agreement details are confidential.
stake: About labour relations. Decided by a recorded vote, 21 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: Introduction of General Bills and Confirming Bills
brief: This is a procedural step: City Council will introduce general bills and confirming bills, which turn approved decisions into official bylaws. No new policy is decided.
stake: About by-laws. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 19 in favour, none against.

title: 1175-1181 Weston Road and 7-17 Locust Street - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about refused applications for 1175-1181 Weston Road and 7-17 Locust Street. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Public Realm and Streetscape Improvements Within the Highland Creek Community Area - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Nick Mantas
brief: A councillor wants Council to add $29,000.00 to the capital budget, paid by developer community benefits, for decorative paving and community signs in the Highland Creek neighbourhood. That includes $24,000 for paving and banners, plus $5,000 also listed in the motion.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $29,000.00.

title: Authority to Enter into a Licence Amending Agreement with Toronto Island Bicycle Rental Ltd. - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley

business improvement associations, boards of directors
brief: The local community council would appoint Guzman, Jovana to the Weston Village business association board, for a term ending with this council term.

title: 21 Elderfield Crescent - Application to Remove a Private Tree
brief: The local council would deny a permit to cut down a honey locust at 21 Elderfield Crescent. The owner cites property damage and safety concerns, but staff say the healthy tree can stay. The owner is appealing.
stake: About applications. Council put off deciding this item.

title: Nordin Avenue (1156 The Queensway) - Construction Staging Area
topics: construction, mid rise buildings, road restrictions, sidewalks
brief: The local community council would approve closing the east sidewalk and part of the northbound lane on Nordin Avenue from April 2025 to June 2027 for an 11-storey building, with a temporary protected walkway for pedestrians.

title: 37 Advance Road and 212-216 Norseman Street - Encroachment Agreement
brief: The local community council would let the city sign a deal with the owner of 37 Advance Road and 212-216 Norseman Street, letting three existing maintenance holes (two storm, one sanitary) stay on city property.

title: Subway Crescent - Speed Limit Reduction
brief: The local council would lower the speed limit on Subway Crescent near the Kipling Transit Hub from 40 to 30 km/h, after residents raised concerns about speeding buses and pedestrian safety on the wide, curving street.

title: Changes to the Bayview Leaside Business Improvement Area Board of Management
brief: This is a procedural item: council is asked to make changes to the Bayview Leaside Business Improvement Area Board of Management. No new rules here.

title: Thistle Down Boulevard - Parking Amendments
brief: Council would ban parking at all times on the inner loop of Thistle Down Boulevard and update parking rules on the outer circle, so parked cars do not block buses using the new speed cushions.
stake: About parking prohibitions. Council put off deciding this item.

title: Scott Road - Accessible Parking Space
brief: The local community council would designate an on-street accessible parking space on the east side of Scott Road, just south of Dunraven Drive, for use at all times.

title: 1886 - 1920 Eglinton Avenue West - Shortt Street, Fairbank Village Lane - Construction Staging Area
topics: landscaping permits (right-if way), one way operations
brief: Parts of Shortt Street and Fairbank Village Lane would close for 14 months, from May 2025 to July 2026, for the eight-storey condo at 1886-1920 Eglinton Avenue West, if council agrees. Drivers and walkers there would be affected.

title: Vision Zero Road Safety Plan Speed Limit Reductions to 30 Kilometres Per Hour on Local Roads, Public Lanes
brief: Speed limits to 30 kilometres per hour on local roads and public lanes in North York areas under the Vision Zero plan would be cut, if council agrees. Drivers there would be affected.

title: 55 and 57 Montgomery Avenue - Residential Demolition Application
brief: Tearing down two semi-detached houses at 55 and 57 Montgomery Avenue is before council for a decision. Staff say council can refuse them, since there is no permit for new buildings, or approve them.

title: 17 - 31 Henning Avenue - Residential Demolition Application
brief: Tearing down eight semi-detached houses at 17 to 31 Henning Avenue is before council for a decision. Staff say council can refuse them, since there is no permit for new buildings, or approve them.

title: Re-Opening Item EY17.17 Windsor Street and Buckingham Street - Pay-and-Display Parking
brief: The local council would reopen its earlier decision on pay-and-display parking on Windsor and Buckingham Streets to add a no-standing zone on the east side of Windsor Street, restoring loading access local businesses lost.

title: 21 Tepee Court - Application to Remove a Private Tree
brief: A permit to remove a healthy littleleaf linden tree at 21 Tepee Court would be denied, if council agrees. The tree would stay.

title: 390 Glencairn Avenue - Application to Remove a Private Tree
brief: A permit to remove a healthy Colorado blue spruce tree at 390 Glencairn Avenue would be denied, if council agrees. The tree would stay.
stake: About applications. Council put off deciding this item.

title: Aberfoyle Crescent - Temporary Taxi Stand Relocation
brief: The local community council would temporarily move a two-taxi stand on Aberfoyle Crescent from the south side to the north side, from April 2025 to June 2027, while Islington subway station is redeveloped for accessibility.

title: 8-16 Locust Street - Construction Staging Area
brief: The local community council would approve closing the north sidewalk and part of the westbound lane on Locust Street from April 2025 to April 2028 for a 37-storey condo build, sending pedestrians to the south sidewalk.
stake: About condominium housing. Council put off deciding this item.

title: Steeles Avenue East and Bayview Avenue - Improving Pedestrian Safety and Signal Timing Operations
topics: pedestrians, road operations, traffic signal timing
brief: Safety and traffic light timing for walkers at Steeles Avenue East and Bayview Avenue after new crossovers were approved in December 2024 would be reviewed, if council agrees. Drivers and walkers there would be affected.

title: Wild Rose Gardens, Creekbank Road and Blackstone Street - Parking and Traffic Amendments
brief: The local community council would set 30 km/h speed limits on Wild Rose Gardens and Creekbank Road, ban heavy vehicles, and add a stop sign for southbound traffic on Wild Rose Gardens at Creekbank Road.

title: First Nations, Inuit and Métis Procurement Policy
brief: City staff will show how they are building a policy to give more city contracts to First Nations, Inuit and Métis businesses, and ask the committee for feedback. No decision is requested.
stake: About First Nations. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Indigenous Representation and Public Boards
brief: City staff will explain how appointments to public boards and committees, including the Toronto Police Service Board, work, to guide talk about Indigenous representation on them. No decision is proposed.

stake: About planning. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

brief: A $3,207,523 contract with Dependable Emergency Vehicles for two heavy rescue trucks for Toronto Fire Services, with delivery expected between May and November 2025 ($3,624,501 including HST; $3,263,975 net of HST recoveries), is up for approval by the city's contract panel. brief: A $1,298,575 contract with M.E. Andrews and Associates for engineering work to repair drains on the Mid Toronto Interceptor main sewer line, through December 2029 ($1,467,390, including HST; $1,321,430 net of HST recoveries) is up for approval by the city's contract panel.

brief: A $3,584,280 contract with GHD Limited for electrical design and inspection on 2025 to 2026 road and streetcar projects, through December 2028 ($4,050,236 including HST; $3,647,363 net of HST recoveries) is up for approval by the city's contract panel.

brief: A $2,920,305 contract with OJCR Construction for repairing and replacing water service connections and valve boxes across Toronto using vacuum-digging equipment, July 2025 to June 2026 with two optional renewal years ($3,299,945 including HST; $2,971,702 net of HST recoveries), is up for approval by the city's contract panel. Option years: $3,007,914 ($3,398,943; $3,060,853), $3,098,152 ($3,500,911; $3,152,679); three-year total: $9,026,371 ($10,199,799; $9,185,235). Bids: $2,830,305.00, $2,908,123.00, $2,978,948.00.

brief: The owner of 1 Fallingbrook Road wants to add a modern addition to the protected heritage house. The board is asked to recommend that council approve the alterations.

brief: Recommending that council approve tearing down three unrated buildings in the South Rosedale heritage district and approve replacement designs at 43, 44 and 45 Price Street. It goes to the board for a decision.

brief: Recommending that council approve the heritage conservation plan for 309-311 and 349 George Street, tied to proposed development on the site. It goes to the board for a decision.

brief: Recommending that council approve alterations to two protected heritage houses at 5933 and 5951 Steeles Avenue East, plus a heritage protection agreement. It goes to the board for a decision.

topics: boards of health, health, hiring process, public health

brief: The Board of Health will get an update on the Indigenous Wellness Committee co-led with Indigenous organizations.

title: Environmental and Occupational-Related Cancer Prevention in Toronto: Public Health Actions
brief: The Board of Health will decide whether to direct the Medical Officer of Health to keep working with partners on environmental and workplace cancer prevention in Toronto.

topics: health, noise, noise complaints, noise control, public health
traffic noise, health coverage, noise barriers
brief: The Board of Health will receive an update on the health impacts of noise and the Noise Action Plan.

topics: budgets, health, operating budgets, public health
brief: The Board of Health will receive the approved 2025 public health operating budget of $288,575.6 thousand gross and $85,705.5 thousand net, $2,677.5 thousand gross and $2,836.8 thousand net above the board's recommendation, and a $3,145.4 thousand gross and $6,000.0 thousand net increase over 2024.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $288,575.6 thousand.

topics: budgets, capital budgets, health, public health
brief: The Board of Health will receive the approved 2025 public health capital budget of $4,130 thousand plus $10,023 thousand in future commitments, totalling $14,153 thousand, and a 2026-2034 plan of $7,999 thousand.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $4,130 thousand.

topics: budgets, capital budgets, health, public health
brief: For information only. The Board of Health gets Toronto Public Health's 2024 capital budget update. No policy change is proposed.

topics: health (sc), health issues, homelessness, public health, substance abuse
brief: For information only. The Board gets an update on the City's downtown HART Hub. Five supervised consumption sites were ordered closed by March 31, 2025, and the province announced $378 million for HART Hubs across Ontario.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $378 million.

title: 1117 Queen Street West - Alterations to a Designated Property and Demolition of Heritage Attributes of a Building on a Designated Property under Sections 33 and 34(1)1 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Request for Directions
brief: A procedural item: the board is asked to adopt private legal advice about 1117 Queen Street West, where the owner appealed council's refusals to the Ontario Land Tribunal. The details are not public.

brief: The Board of Health will receive an update on the legal challenge of the Community Care and Recovery Act.

title: 2759 and 2761 to 2763 Kingston Road and 52 St Quentin Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City staff suggest changing planning rules to allow a 10-storey building with 95 homes and shops at 2759-2763 Kingston Road and 52 St Quentin Avenue.

title: 70-86 Lynn Williams Street - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Council will vote on a 44-storey building with 520 rental homes, including 13 affordable rentals, at 70-86 Lynn Williams Street. It includes a public daycare and park.

title: Traffic Control Signals and Traffic Regulations - Yonge Street and Delisle Avenue/Private Driveway
brief: Council will vote on new traffic lights at Yonge Street and Delisle Avenue, required by a nearby development. A westbound left-turn ban would be removed.

brief: Staff suggest a city-led rule change for 253 Markham Road and 12, 20 and 30 Dunelm Street, updating rules from a 2022 approval for 783 homes, including a building with 245 affordable and rent-controlled units. Council is asked to approve.

topics: administration, assessment, assets, audits, maintenance, management (activity)

brief: Council would formally take over the roads and city services in the Lowe's subdivision at 50 Resources Road, release the developer's performance guarantee, and pass an assumption by-law for the public road and services.

brief: This is a routine item: council is asked to accept the checked 2023 financial statements for two arenas: the North Toronto Memorial Arena and the William H. Bolton Arena. No policy change is proposed.
