brief: Council would decide whether to allow a clothing donation drop box at 455 Sentinel Road: staff refused the permit, so council must choose to uphold the refusal or approve the permit.

title: 104 - 114 Finch Avenue East - Official Plan Amendment, Zoning By-law Amendment, Applications - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Approval of an 11-storey building with 201 homes and ground-floor shops at 104 to 114 Finch Avenue East is before council. Future residents and shoppers would be affected.
stake: About applications. Decided by a recorded vote, 15 in favour and 7 against — every member's position is public.

title: 56, 58 and 60 Fieldway Road - Community Benefits Charge In-Kind Report
brief: Council would let the developer at 56, 58, and 60 Fieldway Road provide on-site public art instead of cash, up to 33% of its Community Benefits Charge, with the balance due when building permits are issued.

title: 250 Dundas Street West - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning bylaws
brief: Council will vote on raising a tower at 250 Dundas Street West from 49 to 57 storeys. The plan includes 962 square metres of affordable housing.

title: 110-112 Adelaide Street East and 85 Lombard Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
brief: Council will vote on sending city lawyers to oppose a proposed 65-storey building at 110-112 Adelaide Street East at the tribunal. The developer appealed after council missed its deadline.

title: Road Alteration - King Street East at George Street
brief: Council will vote on closing one eastbound lane on King Street East at George Street to widen the sidewalk and add a streetcar stop.
stake: About pavement markings. Decided by a recorded vote, 16 in favour and 3 against — every member's position is public.

title: Accessible Parking Spaces - February 2025 (Non-Delegated)
topics: accessibility, accessible permit parking, parking spaces
brief: Council will vote on the monthly list of on-street accessible parking spaces for people with disabilities. Full council approval is needed because the TTC runs transit there.

title: 1245 Dupont Street - Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Approval
brief: Council will vote on extending the land-splitting exemption at 1245 Dupont Street for three more years. This lets a community centre be finished and a park transferred.

title: Toronto Community Housing Tenant Engagement System and Implementation Plan
brief: Toronto Community Housing's board approved a new Engage Together tenant engagement model and phased workplan, forwarded to council for information. No decision is proposed.

title: Huntingwood Drive at Ridgecrest Drive - Pedestrian Crossing Protection
brief: Staff studied whether a marked crossing is needed on Huntingwood Drive at Ridgecrest Drive and suggest adding one, to help people crossing to the park, church, and nearby schools. Since buses run there, this needs a City Council vote.

title: Improving Bike Lane Inspections in Toronto and East York Community Council district
topics: on street bike lanes, site inspection
brief: Community council will receive a report on how the City inspects and sweeps bike lanes. A city-wide review follows later in 2025.

title: 40-60 St. Lawrence Avenue - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on the tribunal hearing for the residential proposal at 40-60 St. Lawrence Avenue. The legal advice stays confidential.

title: Permanent Closure of the Public Laneway between 10A Eastern Avenue and 16 Eastern Avenue
brief: Council will vote on permanently closing a public laneway between 10A and 16 Eastern Avenue. The land would be sold to a neighbouring owner.

title: Permanent Closure of portions of Railway Street and Centre Street
brief: Staff suggest permanently closing small unused parts of Railway Street and Centre Street so the land can become new park space for Grant Faulkner Park. Since these are public roads, this needs a City Council vote.

title: Amendment to Item 2024.TE13.5 - 639-653 Yonge Street  - Official Plan and  Zoning By-law Amendment Application
brief: Council will vote on dropping a condition from its approval of a 76-storey building at Yonge and Isabella. Staff say the required deal with 663 Yonge Street is not feasible.

title: Use of Nathan Phillips Square for Various Events - May 1 - September 30, 2025
brief: Council will vote on allowing listed festivals and events at Nathan Phillips Square from May to September 2025. These are routine event permissions.
stake: About culture (sc). Its recorded vote was unanimous — 22 in favour, none against.

title: 1400, 1408 and 1410 Victoria Park Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Council will vote on four towers with 951 homes, including 10 affordable rentals, plus a new public park at 1400-1410 Victoria Park Avenue.

title: 55 Eastern Avenue - Construction Staging Area
brief: Council will vote on closing parts of Cherry Street and Front Street East for 26 months for a care home at 55 Eastern Avenue. The item lists a $4.25 fee.

title: Potential Litigation Arising from the Construction of Certain Sanitary Sewer Upgrades in the Vicinity of 1215 York Mills Road
brief: City Council will vote on confidential legal recommendations about potential litigation over sanitary sewer upgrade costs near 1215 York Mills Road.

title: 75 Hyde Avenue - Expropriation of a Permanent Easement for the Construction of the Black Creek Sanitary Trunk Sewer Relief System - Stage 2
brief: City Council will vote on expropriating a permanent easement at 75 Hyde Avenue for the Black Creek sanitary trunk sewer relief project.

title: York-Eglinton Business Improvement Area - Name Change
brief: The York-Eglinton Business Improvement Area would be renamed to the Little Jamaica Business Improvement Area, as voted by its board and endorsed by its members, if council agrees.

title: Proposed Upper Avenue Business Improvement Area Poll Results
brief: The area along Avenue Road from Lawrence Avenue West to Joicey Boulevard as the Upper Avenue Business Improvement Area, after a poll showed the required business support would be designated, if council agrees.

title: Parkland obligations at 25 Fisherville Road - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
brief: The parkland for the 25 Fisherville Road redevelopment — 397 square metres required plus 133 extra — could be transferred to the city within 36 months of the first above-grade building permit, rather than earlier, if council agrees. Council also allowed the future park and street lands to be used for construction staging in the meantime.

title: Award of Doc4747531748 to Walker Environmental Group Inc., for Processing Services for Yard Waste Material and Digester Solids Material for Solid Waste Management Services
topics: contracts, solid waste, solid waste management, waste, waste collection, yard waste, yard waste collection
brief: City Council will vote on awarding Walker Environmental Group a $24,311,595 contract ($24,739,479 net of HST recoveries) to process yard waste and digester solids for three years.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $24,311,595.

title: 32 to 50 Larwood Boulevard - Expropriation of Portions of Properties - Stage 2
brief: City Council will vote on expropriating parts of nine Larwood Boulevard properties for a multi-use trail along Brimley Road South, part of the Scarborough Waterfront Project.

title: 486 Front Street West - Below Market Sublease Agreement with Macaulay Centres for Children For Child Care Services
topics: child care facilities, leasing, operating budgets
brief: City Council will vote on a ten-year below-market sublease letting Macaulay Centres for Children run a new child care centre at 486 Front Street West.

title: Proposed Pilot for Non-Motorized Mobile Food Vendors in University-Rosedale
brief: The street vending bylaw for a pilot allowing non-motorized food vendors, like food carts, in mobile vending zones in University-Rosedale (Ward 11) would be amended, if council agrees.

title: Re-allocating Unused Section 37 Funds Secured in By-law 1022-2014 in Ward 22
brief: A councillor suggests moving $250,000 in unspent community benefit money from the 1251 Bridletowne Crescent project to other community facilities in Ward 22. The original walkway plan was dropped. Council is asked to send staff back with the rule change.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $250,000.

title: Anti-idling By-law
brief: The report covers Toronto's anti-idling rule, which limits cars to one minute of idling per hour. It looks at enforcement, education, and the City's own fleet.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Comprint Systems Incorporated for Election Services Applications and Maintenance
topics: application software, contracts, software, system software
brief: City Council will vote on a non-competitive six-year election-systems contract with Comprint Systems for the voters list, voting locations, the MyVote portal and mail-in voting; source documents list $9,485,507 ($9,652,452 net of HST recoveries) and $500,000.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $500,000.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Teleflex Medical Canada Inc., for the Supply and Delivery of Medical Supplies and Equipment for Toronto Paramedic Services
brief: City Council will vote on a $340,713 ($346,710 net of HST recoveries) non-competitive contract with Teleflex Medical Canada for paramedic special-teams medical supplies; source documents also list $500,000.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $340,713.

title: Award of Provincial Vendor of Record and Non-competitive Procurement for the Supply of Paging and Mobile Devices, Accessories and Services
brief: The General Government Committee will consider adopting the provincial mobile-devices Vendor of Record valued at $69,476,714 ($70,669,504 net of HST recoveries), building on over $10 million saved since 2020 and $16.5 million more expected, plus a $1,500,000 ($1,526,400) paging contract; source documents also list $500,000, $57,484,224, $64,957,173, $58,495,946, $4,801,719, $5,425,942, $4,886,229, $1,800,361, $2,034,408, $1,832,048, $5,390,410, $6,091,163, $5,485,281 and $1,695,000.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $69,476,714.

title: Authority to Enter into a Multi-Year Agreement with Toronto Arts Council (2025-2029)
brief: A new five-year agreement with the Toronto Arts Council for 2025-2029 to distribute cultural grants on the city's behalf would be authorized by council. The current agreement expires March 31, 2025.

title: Suspension of Duron Ontario Ltd.
brief: City Council will vote on suspending Duron Ontario Ltd. from city contracts for five years over Supplier Code of Conduct contraventions including over-billing and false claims.

title: Developing an Urgent Downtown Coyote Action Plan
brief: Staff would share coyote safety education with downtown residents and urgently develop a Downtown Coyote Action Plan, ahead of the updated coyote strategy planned for late 2025, if council agrees.

title: Options to Fund and Expand the HTO To Go Water Trailer Program
brief: The HTO To Go water trailer program would become a regular part of the City's heat relief, with trailers spread more evenly and a contractor hired to run them, if council agrees. Council would also approve up to $220,000 to buy two stainless steel water trailers with ten taps each.

title: Wastewater Energy Program Implementation
brief: City officials could sign deals with companies for the program that captures heat from sewers as clean energy, with Toronto Water able to reject bad projects, if council agrees.

title: Street 'A' Environmental Assessment Study (Park Lawn Lake Shore Transportation Master Plan)
topics: Master Plans, environmental assessments, transportation infrastructure
brief: The design for a new Street A near Park Lawn and Lake Shore, tied to the old Christie's site and a future GO station. It goes to council for approval, along with moving its environmental review forward.

title: Cycling Network Plan - 2025 Cycling Infrastructure Installation - First Quarter Update
topics: bikeway networks, cycling maps, transportation planning
brief: Approval of 12.5 kilometres of new bike lanes and trails at six spots, including Bathurst Street and Ellesmere Road is before council. No car lanes would be removed. A temporary two-year position would also be added at $98,000, paid from the capital budget at no net cost.

title: William R. Allen Road (Wilson Station Bus Underpass and Mezzanine Bridge Rehabilitation) - Construction Staging Area
brief: A request to let the TTC close lanes on William R. Allen Road near Wilson Station until the end of 2025 to fix the station's bus underpass and bridge goes to council.

title: Proposed Amendments to Municipal Code Chapter 367, Building Emissions Performance
topics: greenhouse effect, municipal codes, property owners
brief: The energy reporting deadline for mid-size buildings would be pushed back to 2026, with July 2, 2025 set as the deadline for 2025 extensions, if council agrees.

title: Proposed naming of the Public Lane North of Gerrard Street East and East of Greenwood Avenue
brief: Council will vote on naming a laneway north of Gerrard Street East 'Luella Price Lane', honouring the founder of a 1910 club of Black women.
stake: About laneways. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 22 in favour, none against.

title: East Bayfront Community Recreation Centre Naming
brief: Council will vote on having staff work with Indigenous partners to name the new East Bayfront Community Recreation Centre. The centre opens in spring 2025.

title: Increasing Number of Meetings Per Year for the Confronting Anti-Black Racism Advisory Committee
brief: The committee would recommend changing the anti-Black racism committee's rules so it meets up to six times a year instead of up to four.

title: Replacement Units for Demovicted Dwelling Room Tenants
brief: Having staff report on whether developers who tear down six or more rental rooms should have to provide a replacement home for every displaced tenant. It goes to Council for a decision. Council decides.
stake: About dwellings. Decided by a recorded vote, 22 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: 2930 Lake Shore Boulevard West - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: Starting the legal process to give heritage protection to the former New Toronto Post Office at 2930 Lake Shore Boulevard West. It goes to Council for a decision. If no one objects, the formal by-law can follow. Council decides.

title: Review of Toronto’s Winter Maintenance Program
brief: Council would order a full review of winter operations after the February 2025 snowstorms, looking into why reported sidewalk clearing did not match reality, and whether private snow contractors kept their promises.
stake: About maintenance. Decided by a recorded vote, 22 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: Public Reporting of Performance and Service Standards
brief: Council would make all city departments share performance data with the Customer Experience Division, so it can publicly report on service standards, keep friendly public dashboards, and report on trends twice a year.

title: Rexdale - Casino Woodbine Community Benefits Agreement: 2024 Progress Update
brief: Council would have staff negotiate new Woodbine Local Area and Equity Deserving Communities definitions with One Toronto Gaming, and let the City Manager sign the updated community benefits deal. The report cites figures of $100.5 million and $1.8 million.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $100.5 million.

title: Supporting Ownership Housing Developments
brief: Council would have staff review stalled condo applications that include 5 to 10 percent affordable housing, and back up to 3,000 ownership units, favouring projects with more affordable housing. The city would delay collecting up to $182.1 million in development charges, plus lose $28.3 million in investment returns.
stake: About development. Decided by a recorded vote, 22 in favour and 2 against — every member's position is public.

title: Extending Vehicle Age Limits for Vehicles-for-Hire
brief: Council would let wheelchair-accessible taxis and private vehicles be up to ten model years old, and let taxis and limos due for replacement by March 2025 keep running until August 2025.
stake: About accessible taxicabs. Decided by a recorded vote, 20 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: 667 King Street West - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: Starting the legal process to give heritage protection to the property at 667 King Street West, at the corner of King and Bathurst. It goes to Council for a decision. If no one objects, the formal by-law can follow. Council decides.

title: 877 and 885 Lawrence Avenue East - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: Starting the legal process to protect two former bank branches at 877 and 885 Lawrence Avenue East as heritage properties. It goes to Council for a decision. If no one objects, formal by-laws can follow. Council decides.

title: 1660 Kingston Road - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: Starting the legal process to give heritage protection to the property at 1660 Kingston Road in Birch Cliff, Scarborough. It goes to Council for a decision. If no one objects, the formal by-law can follow. Council decides.

title: Toronto Ferry Service Operational Review
brief: Council would have the Deputy City Manager report back by late 2025 on progress carrying out the Toronto Ferry Service operations review.
stake: About ferries. Decided by a recorded vote, 22 in favour and 2 against — every member's position is public.

title: Advancing the Tamil Community Centre
brief: Council would drop city planning fees for the zoning changes needed for the non-profit Tamil Community Centre at 311 Staines Road in northeast Scarborough. The report cites a $26.3 million figure and a $1 figure.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $1. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 22 in favour, none against.

title: Building a Universal Student Food Program in Toronto
brief: Council would ask Ottawa to move unspent national student food program money to places with deals in place, like Toronto, and ask Ontario to raise its per-student funding for school nutrition programs. Council already added $5 million to the 2025 budget to grow the school food program.
stake: About food. Decided by a recorded vote, 22 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: Municipal Diversity Plan for Appointments to the Toronto Police Service Board and Police Board Composition
brief: Council would adopt a diversity plan for appointments to the Toronto Police Service Board, as required by the 2019 Community Safety and Policing Act.

title: Transit Priority on Queens Quay East - Interim Priority Bus Lanes
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, light rail transit, transportation
brief: Council would approve temporary priority bus lanes on Queens Quay East, Parliament, and Front Street West, to make transit faster for about 4,000 daily riders before the new light rail arrives. The bus lanes would cost about $800,000, paid from the TTC's capital budget.
stake: About Toronto Transit Commission. Decided by a recorded vote, 19 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: Appointment of a Public Member to the Toronto Transit Commission board
brief: The committee recommends one public member for council to appoint to the TTC board, for a term ending March 29, 2029. Candidate details are kept private.

title: Appointment of a Public Member to the Dangerous Dog Review Tribunal
brief: Appointing Sophia Davis to the Dangerous Dog Review Tribunal, for a term from March 28, 2025 to November 14, 2026 is on council's agenda. Further details are confidential.
stake: About advisory committees. Council put off deciding this item.

title: Amending Item 2021.TE26.4 - 33-49 Avenue Road and 136-148 Yorkville Avenue and Creation of New Park at 819 Yonge Street - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
brief: A councillor wants Council to give the owner of 148 Yorkville Avenue a development charge credit for building park upgrades at 819 Yonge Street, so that site can become a new park.

title: 266 and 268 Royal York Road - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about proposed 37-storey and 23-storey towers plus a self-storage warehouse at 266-268 Royal York Road. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: 114 and 114R Baldwin Street and 75 Cecil Street - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
brief: A councillor wants the City Solicitor to get party status at the Toronto Local Appeal Body to back the refusal of variances for a 10-unit townhouse complex at 114 and 114R Baldwin Street and 75 Cecil Street.

title: The Growing Crisis of Public Safety in the City of Toronto and the Urgent Need to Seek Clarity on the Date City Staff will Present Long Overdue “Bubble Zone” By-laws to Toronto City Council and Protect the Charter Rights of Those Trying to Access Faith-Based and Other Vulnerable Institutions
brief: The item asks City staff when new rules to protect places of worship, sometimes called 'bubble zone' rules, will come back to Council. Council had asked for the by-laws by the end of March 2025.
stake: About by-laws. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Micro-Shelters
brief: The item asks City staff for an update on the City's plan for homeless encampments, including small shelters called micro-shelters. Figures of $20 million and $5.5 million are also listed.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $20 million. Council sent it back for more work.

title: 6212-6600 Yonge Street - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about the Centerpoint Mall redevelopment at 6212-6600 Yonge Street, with buildings of 4 to 50 storeys. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: 137 Teddington Park Avenue - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
brief: A councillor wants the City Solicitor to argue at the Toronto Local Appeal Body against an appeal of the refusal of part of a variance application at 137 Teddington Park Avenue.

title: Results of Collective Bargaining Negotiations Between the City of Toronto and CUPE Local 79
brief: Council receives for information the results of bargaining with CUPE Local 79, the city's inside workers: four tentative agreements reached March 8, 2025. No decision is proposed.
stake: About agreements. Decided by a recorded vote, 23 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: 137-141 Isabella Street - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about a proposed 69-storey tower with 823 homes at 137-141 Isabella Street. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: Request to Accept an In-Kind Donation for the Playground Enhancement and Park Improvements at Pricefield Road Park - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
brief: A councillor wants Council to accept a donation of up to $620,000 from Scrivener Square Nominee Inc. for playground and park upgrades at Pricefield Road Park. Donations of $50,000 or more need Council approval.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $620,000.

title: Authority to Enter into a Nominal Agreement with the Indigenous People Garden Incorporated at Paul Martel Park - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
brief: A councillor wants Parks and Recreation to sign a low-cost licence with the Indigenous People Garden Incorporated for Indigenous-led training and gardening at Paul Martel Park, for one year, renewable up to three.

title: Mayor’s Economic Action Plan in Response to United States Tariffs
brief: Council would adopt the Mayor's economic plan in response to US tariffs, keep it updated, and report to the July Executive Committee on how it is being put into action. Staffing for the first steps would cost about $2.4 million, paid from existing budgets.
stake: About economic development. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 23 in favour, none against.

title: Better Management of Derelict Buildings - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
brief: A councillor wants staff to report by late 2025 on tools to deal with vacant and run-down buildings, including better information sharing between City teams about known empty properties.

title: 2636-2654 Eglinton Avenue West and 1856 and 1856A Keele Street - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about a proposed 33-storey building at Eglinton Avenue West and Keele Street. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: 604 Bay Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: An intent to designate 604 Bay Street as a heritage property under the Ontario Heritage Act would be stated by council. If no objections are filed, a designation bylaw follows.

title: Authority to Accept a Donation and Enter an Agreement with Toronto and Region Conservation Authority for an Indigenous Outdoor Gathering Space at Morningside Park - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
brief: A councillor wants Council to accept a donation of up to $500,000 from the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority to build an Indigenous outdoor gathering space at Morningside Park, co-developed with Williams Treaty First Nations.

title: Amending Item 2022.MM45.51 to Support Non-Profit Affordable Rental Housing - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
brief: A councillor wants Council to shift funding for the Kensington Market Community Land Trust’s affordable rental project: $50,000 for renovations and operations, with $400,000 of an earlier $450,000 allocation supporting a property purchase worth up to $200,000 per home.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $50,000.

title: Amending the Housing Rights Advisory Committee Terms of Reference
brief: The Housing Rights Advisory Committee's rules would be changed so it can form small working groups of up to five members, with staff help from the Housing Secretariat.

title: Sankofa Square Signage
brief: The item asks City staff for the latest on the Sankofa Square signs: production costs, when they will go up, and what happened to the old signs.
stake: About attractions. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Participation in Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Cities Initiative Advocacy Days and Advocacy Against Tariffs
brief: Councillor Ainslie reports on representing Toronto at Great Lakes advocacy days in Washington, D.C. in March 2025, pushing for the watershed and against tariffs. The report cites figures of $123 billion, $202 billion, $252 billion and $6. Council just receives it.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $6.

title: FIFA World Cup 2026 Toronto: Economic Benefits of Hosting, Soccer for All Legacy Fund and Community Benefits Plan Updates
brief: Council would add $10.7 million from the special event reserve for World Cup hospitality, and let staff accept donations for the Soccer for All Legacy Fund and 12 mini fields. Council would also stick to the $380 million tournament budget.

title: February 2025 Snow Events
topics: non emergency municipal services, sidewalk snow ploughs, snow removal
brief: The item asks City staff for details about the huge snowstorms of February 2025, the biggest snowfall Toronto has seen since January 2022.
stake: About non emergency municipal services. The item was withdrawn before a final decision.

title: 1522 Queen Street West - Liquor Licence Application 2972534 - Thamel Toronto - by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
brief: A councillor wants Council to tell the provincial liquor registrar that a licence for Thamel Toronto at 1522 Queen Street West is not in the public interest unless conditions on noise, litter, and safety are added.

title: 3042 Dundas Street West - Liquor Licence Application 2963606 - Gigli Café Junction - by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
brief: A councillor wants Council to tell the provincial liquor registrar that a licence for Gigli Cafe Junction at 3042 Dundas Street West is not in the public interest unless conditions on noise, litter, and safety are added.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Clocktower Trail Streetscape Improvements - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
brief: A councillor wants Council to add $200,000.00 to the transportation budget, paid by developer community benefits, for street and pedestrian safety upgrades on Maitland, Alexander, and Grosvenor streets near Yonge Street.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to the Laneway Project for Verner Lane and Drovers Lane - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
brief: A councillor wants Council to send $330,000.00 in developer community benefits to the Laneway Project to fix up Verner Lane and Drovers Lane in Cabbagetown South.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for 1841 Shoreline Interpretation - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
brief: A councillor wants Council to add $113,419.07 to Heritage Toronto's budget, paid by developer community benefits, for two plaques and 10 markers along the historic 1841 Lake Ontario shoreline in St. Lawrence.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for North Star Way Lane Heritage Plaque - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
brief: A councillor wants Council to add $10,000 to Heritage Toronto's budget, paid by developer community benefits, for a plaque honouring the North Star's role in the Underground Railroad at North Star Lane in Corktown.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Cy McLean Heritage Plaque - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
brief: A councillor wants Council to add $10,000 to Heritage Toronto's budget, paid by developer community benefits, for a plaque honouring Cy McLean, one of Toronto's first Black bandleaders, at 201 Yonge Street.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Henry “Box” Brown Heritage Plaque - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
brief: A councillor wants Council to add $10,000 to Heritage Toronto's budget, paid by developer community benefits, for a plaque honouring Henry 'Box' Brown at Henry 'Box' Brown Lane in Corktown.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 and Section 45 Funds for Heritage Lighting at the Young People’s Theatre - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
brief: A councillor wants Council to release $1,133,859.76 in developer community benefits for heritage lighting at the Young People's Theatre at 165 Front Street East. The motion breaks the funding down as $500,000, $633,859.76, $224,704.20, $107,741.73, $32,617.65, $33,651.59, $7,696.72, $94,672.34, $1,782.27, and $496,808.48.

title: Improving Earl Bales Ski and Snowboard Centre Season and Experience by Investing in Modern Snowmaking Capabilities - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng
topics: recreation & tourism (sc), ski centres, skiing, snowboarding
brief: A councillor wants staff to study better snowmaking at the Earl Bales Ski and Snowboard Centre to lengthen its ski season, and to look for money from other governments and City sources.

title: 621-623 The Queensway - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
brief: A councillor wants the City Solicitor to appeal the approval of parking variances for extra homes at 621-623 The Queensway and argue against them at the Toronto Local Appeal Body.

title: Accepting an In-Kind Donation from Pleasantview Tennis Club to Refurbish the Tennis Courts at Clydesdale Park and Henry Farm Tennis Club to Retrofit the Outdoor Court Lighting at Havenbrook Park - by Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
brief: A councillor wants Council to accept donations from two tennis clubs — up to $150,000 from Pleasantview Tennis Club for courts at Clydesdale Park and up to $75,000 from Henry Farm Tennis Club for lighting at Havenbrook Park — paid from the clubs' own reserve funds.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $0.150 million.

title: Recruitment for the Deputy City Manager, Community and Social Services
brief: Council receives for information a notice that an update on hiring a Deputy City Manager, Community and Social Services will come before the March 26-28, 2025 meeting. No decision is proposed.
stake: About cluster divisions. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 24 in favour, none against.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Sam Ching Heritage Plaque - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
brief: A councillor wants Council to add $10,000 to Heritage Toronto's budget, paid by developer community benefits, for a plaque honouring Sam Ching, one of the first Chinese residents on record in Toronto, at 9 Adelaide Street East.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $500.

title: Authority to Negotiate Agreements Related to Queen’s Park North Through Philanthropic Partnerships in Alignment with City of Toronto Priorities
brief: The Parks and Recreation general manager could negotiate a $50 million donation agreement with the Weston Foundations for Queen's Park North improvements, if council agrees.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $50 million.

title: Improving Toronto’s Public Washrooms - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
brief: The Mayor wants the City Manager to study where new public washrooms are most needed, put in temporary ones starting spring 2025, plan for more long-term, and fix the worst existing ones.

title: Authority to Enter into a Licence Agreement with Canada Ireland Foundation for Ireland Park - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
brief: A councillor wants Council to sign a 20-year, low-cost deal with the Canada Ireland Foundation to keep up Ireland Park, the memorial park for Irish Famine migrants who arrived in Toronto in 1847.

title: Update on Electric Ferries Shoreside Infrastructure and Ferry Terminal Improvement Projects
topics: electricity, terminals, transportation infrastructure, transportation infrastructure management
brief: Council receives for information a notice that an update on electric ferries and the Jack Layton Ferry Terminal will come to the March 26-28, 2025 meeting. The shoreside project has a base budget of $42,535,680 (net of HST recoveries); full financial details will come in a supplementary report. No decision is proposed.
stake: About electricity. Decided by a recorded vote, 20 in favour and 4 against — every member's position is public.

title: Under Gardiner Public Realm Lighting Project Delivery Agreement with The Bentway Conservancy - Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
brief: A councillor wants Council to have The Bentway Conservancy lead a pilot project lighting the space under the Gardiner Expressway at Dan Leckie Way, paid through the City's streetscape cost-share program.

title: Authorization to Reallocate Section 37 Funds to STEPS for a Mural at Wellesley Station - Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
brief: A councillor wants Council to move developer community benefits funding for a planned Wellesley Station mural from the Church-Wellesley Village business group to the non-profit STEPS Public Art. The funding totals $80,000.00 in Section 37 community benefits.

title: Protecting Paul Martel Indigenous Botanical Garden - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
topics: First Nations, botanical gardens, native plants

title: Reimbursement for Environmental Work at 640 Lansdowne Avenue to Magellan Community Charities - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
brief: A councillor wants Council to pay back Magellan Community Charities up to $1,500,000 for cleaning up pollution at 640 Lansdowne Avenue, the City-owned site where it is building affordable homes and a long-term care home.
stake: Ward 9 is named in the record.

title: 877 Yonge Street - Saint Clare's Multifaith Housing Society Community Space Tenancy Lease and Lease Amending Agreement - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher

title: Feasibility of Establishing an Intercultural Hub or Association of Community Centres at 45-47 Sheppard Avenue East - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
brief: A councillor wants staff to study whether an intercultural hub or group of community centres could work at 45-47 Sheppard Avenue East in Willowdale, including finding funding.

title: Sign the Deal: Extending the Canada-Ontario Early Learning and Child Care Agreement to 2031 - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
brief: A councillor wants Council to urge Ontario's education minister and the federal minister to extend the Canada-Ontario child care deal to 2031. An agreement in principle covers $16.77 billion, but a final deal has not been signed.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $16.77 billion.

title: Co-operative Housing Approval to Lease and Operate Thirty-Two New Affordable Rental Homes - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
brief: A councillor wants Council to approve deals with the Naismith Non-Profit Housing Co-operative to run 32 new affordable rental homes at the Don Summerville site. Council approved $6 million in 2021 to help buy the units. Up to $150,000 would also go to the housing federation for legal and admin costs to close the deal.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $6 million.

title: Authority to Donate Surplus Vehicles to Kyiv - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
brief: The Mayor wants Council to donate up to five surplus City vehicles, three from Fleet Services and two from Paramedic Services, to Kyiv for humanitarian use in 2025.

brief: A councillor wants Council to ask Ontario's health minister to consider allowing earbuds as hearing aids and making over-the-counter hearing aids easier to get.

stake: A citywide decision. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Review of the Order Paper
brief: This is a routine item: City Council reviews the order paper, the list of items for the meeting. No decision is being asked for.

title: 2025 Operating and Capital Budget
brief: This is the Mayor's proposed 2025 budget for Toronto, for council's approval: $18.849 billion in operating spending and a $59.597 billion 10-year capital plan. It starts with a $1.2 billion shortfall, a $600 million improvement from 2024's $1.8 billion, balanced with $680 million in reductions and offsets.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $1.8 billion. Decided by a recorded vote, 24 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: Budget Implementation Including Property Tax Rates, User Fees and Related Matters
brief: Council sets 2025 property tax rates and user fees, with an average tax-rate increase of 4.37%. The rates would raise a $6.063 billion property tax levy, including an extra $250.8 million from the budget increase and $69.7 million for transit and housing projects. The average home would pay $4,160 in municipal property tax.
stake: A citywide decision. Decided by a recorded vote, 24 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: Introduction of General Bills and Confirming Bills
brief: This is a procedural step: City Council will introduce general bills and confirming bills, which turn approved decisions into official bylaws. No new policy is decided.

title: Response to Ontario Regulation 286/09 Budget Matters - Expenses
brief: A provincial rule lets the city leave $1.84 billion in non-cash costs like amortization out of its budget. Council is asked to authorize publishing that information on the city website.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $1.84 billion.

topics: board members, boards of health, health, public health

title: Endorsing Toronto Public Health's Homelessness and Addiction Recovery Hub

title: Application for Two Variances, each Subject to Three Conditions, Respecting the Modification of One Third Party Electronic Roof Sign - 304 Yonge Street
brief: A company wants a rule exception to change its rooftop electronic billboard at 304 Yonge Street from two ad screens to three. City staff say the Sign Variance Committee should say no.

title: Ontario Line - Fourth Quarter Construction Update
brief: Community council will receive an update on Ontario Line subway construction, including work at Pape and Exhibition stations. The line is expected to be complete by 2031.

title: 182-184 Spadina Avenue - Construction Staging Area
brief: Council will vote on closing parts of Spadina Avenue and Cameron Street for four years for hotel construction at 182-184 Spadina Avenue. The item lists a $4.00 fee.

title: 210 Markland Drive - Zoning Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: zoning bylaw amendments, residential real estate
brief: Council would change zoning at 210 Markland Drive to allow three new apartment buildings of 9, 10, and 12 storeys with 484 homes, while keeping the existing 13-storey rental building with 152 units, plus on-site parkland.

title: 515 Markham Road - City-Initiated Zoning By-law Amendment - Re-allocating Section 37 funds within Ward 24 - Decision Report - Approval
brief: This item asks council to free up $213,747.92 in unspent community benefit money tied to 515 Markham Road so it can be spent elsewhere, such as park improvements or a splashpad. No new building is proposed.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $213,747.92.

title: 94 Cortleigh Boulevard - Alterations to and Demolition of Heritage Attributes of a Designated Heritage Property Under Sections 33 and 34 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: Approval of changes and partial demolition of heritage parts of the William Weeks House at 94 Cortleigh Boulevard, a protected 1914 home, for a new one-storey addition at the back is before council.
stake: Ward 8 is named in the record.

title: Designation of the Kensington Market Heritage Conservation District under Part V of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: Council will vote on naming Kensington Market a Heritage Conservation District, with a plan to guide future changes. New work there would have to follow heritage rules.

brief: A councillor wants Council to rule out a shelter at 1220 Wilson Avenue, explore supportive housing with Humber River Hospital instead, and have staff study making the site a park.
stake: About homelessness. Decided by a recorded vote, 10 in favour and 16 against — every member's position is public.

title: 508 and 510 Church Street - Alterations to Heritage Properties and Authority to Amend a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties
brief: Council will vote on letting the developer at 506-516 Church Street partly demolish the protected heritage buildings at 508-510 Church Street. The buildings have been home to Crews and Tangos since 1994.

title: 1778, 1908, 1914, 1920 and 1926 Bloor Street West - Inclusion on the Heritage Register
brief: Council will vote on adding five 1920s-era apartment buildings on Bloor Street West to the city's Heritage Register. Listing notes their heritage value but does not block changes.

brief: Council would have the City Solicitor and staff oppose a 26-storey, 352-home tower at 99 Birmingham Street and 210 Islington Avenue at the Ontario Land Tribunal, appealed after council missed its deadline, while talks continue.

topics: mixed use areas, official plan amendments, rezoning

topics: demolitions, rental housing, zoning bylaws, zoning designations
brief: Council will vote on demolishing 11 vacant rental units at 1-19 Thelma Avenue for a new apartment building. The rentals would be replaced at 2470 Bayview Avenue.

title: Thirtieth Street at Elder Avenue - Lane Designation
brief: Council would mark the easterly southbound lane on Thirtieth Street at Elder Avenue as left-turn-only, to make lane use clearer and reduce conflicts between vehicles.

title: 1552, 1554, 1562, 1570 and 1572 Kingston Road - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report

title: 980 Dufferin Street and 1141 Bloor Street West - TTC Tunnel Construction (Stage 1) - Construction Staging Area Time Extension
brief: Council will vote on extending the construction staging closure on Bloor Street West near Dufferin for the tunnel project. The developer cites delays in approvals and permits.

title: 90 Eastdale Avenue and 2 Secord Avenue - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Council votes on demolishing 31 rental townhouses at 90 Eastdale Avenue and 2 Secord Avenue for a 40-storey building with 35 replacement rentals. Tenants could return at similar rents; if the owner doesn't finish the replacement building on time, the City can charge $20,000.00 per demolished unit.

title: 55 Belmont Street - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Council will vote on an 11-storey addition to the care home at 55 Belmont Street, adding 168 long-term care beds and 30 assisted living units.

title: Ormont Drive - Parking Amendments
brief: Council would extend the no-parking zone on the south side of Ormont Drive 30 metres further east, to keep the area clear and improve heavy-truck access to the driveway at 1290 Ormont Drive.

title: 1-19 Thelma Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Council will vote on a 7-storey apartment building at 1-19 Thelma Avenue. Approval changes the area's low-rise planning rules.

title: 89 Avenue Road - Construction Staging Area Time Extension
brief: Council will vote on extending the sidewalk and lane closure on Avenue Road to December 31, 2025, for condo construction at 89 Avenue Road. The developer cites labour and delivery delays.

title: 450 Dufferin Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendments - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Council will vote on an 18-storey building with 175 rental homes, including 6 affordable rentals, at 450 Dufferin Street.

title: 506-516 Church Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Refusal
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning bylaws
brief: City council will vote on refusing a 48-storey tower with 574 homes at 506-516 Church Street. Staff say it is too big for the area's rules and the site has a protected heritage building.

title: 90 Eastdale Avenue and 2 Secord Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Council will vote on a 40-storey building with 535 homes at 90 Eastdale Avenue and 2 Secord Avenue. Existing tenants could return at similar rents.

title: 2025 Road Openings and Closures in the Port Lands, and Renaming of Streets
brief: Council will vote on road changes for the Port Lands flood protection project: making parts of Cherry and Commissioners public roads, extending a Villiers Street closure, and renaming New Cherry Street.

title: 263 Adelaide Street West - Construction Staging Area
brief: Council will vote on closing part of Adelaide Street West near John Street for four years for condo construction at 263 Adelaide Street West. A covered walkway would keep pedestrians moving.

title: Accessible Parking Space - January 2025 (Non-Delegated)
topics: accessible permit parking, persons with a disability
brief: Council will vote on adding one on-street accessible parking space for people with disabilities. Full council approval is needed because the TTC runs transit on the street.

title: Recommended Parking Requirements for New Development - Accessible, Bicycle, Visitor
topics: accessible permit parking, bicycle parking, standards
brief: Updating zoning rules for accessible, visitor and bicycle parking at new developments, finishing a parking review that started in 2021. It goes to Council for a decision. The source text also cites $538 and $1076. Council decides.

title: Amend Existing Community Safety Zone on Orton Park Road
brief: A councillor suggests fixing the edges of a Community Safety Zone on Orton Park Road near George B. Little Public School so speed cameras can be used up to Ladysbridge Drive. Council is asked to approve.

title: Green Gates Court (9 Fairmeadow Avenue) Subdivision, North York - Assumption of Services, Registered Plans 66M-2531
brief: This is a procedural item: council is asked to take over the roads and city services in the Green Gates Court subdivision. No new rules here.

title: 267-275 Merton Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Staff recommend allowing a 40-storey rental building with 494 homes at 267-275 Merton Street, 30 percent of them affordable. City Council is asked to approve the zoning change.

title: City-Initiated Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendments to Support the ReNew Golden Mile Municipal Class Environmental Assessment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: environmental assessments, official plan amendments, zoning bylaws
brief: Approving planning changes for the ReNew Golden Mile street redesign, updating the Official Plan and zoning along O'Connor Drive, Victoria Park Avenue and Eglinton Square to allow the new and reconfigured major streets. It goes to Council for approval. Council decides.

title: Housing Action Plan: Avenues Policy Review - Decision Report
brief: Approving a new vision and policies for Toronto's Avenues, so the main streets meant for growth can host more housing alongside shops and services. It goes to Council for approval. Council decides.
stake: A citywide decision. Its recorded vote was close — 11 in favour, 13 against.

title: Expanding Housing Options in Neighbourhoods - Ward 23 Multiplex Study - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendments - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Allowing multiplexes with up to six homes on residential properties in Ward 23 (Scarborough North), with building depth up to 19 metres. It goes to Council for a decision. Council decides.
stake: About official plan amendments. Decided by a recorded vote, 18 in favour and 5 against — every member's position is public.

title: Recipient of the 2025 Agnes Macphail Award
brief: Jason Ash would be confirmed as the 2025 Agnes Macphail Award winner, an award for a top volunteer in the former borough of East York, by council.

title: 29, 31, and 33 Sussex Avenue - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: Starting the legal process to give heritage protection to three houses at 29, 31 and 33 Sussex Avenue, in the Huron-Sussex neighbourhood. It goes to Council for a decision. If no one objects, formal by-laws can follow. Council decides.

title: Amendment to the Sign By-law to Regulate Bike Share Signs outside of the Public Right-of-Way
brief: Updating the Sign By-law with new rules for signs on Bike Share docking stations on private property, helping the bike-share network grow. It goes to Council for a decision. Council decides.

title: Multi-Unit Residential Acquisition (MURA) Program Update
brief: Asking the federal government to launch the Canada Rental Protection Fund with a special stream for Toronto, so the city can keep buying at-risk rental buildings and keep rents affordable. It goes to Council for a decision. The source text also cites $64.1 million, $102 million, $101 million, $20 million and $18 million. Council decides.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $64.1 million.

title: Woodbine Transit Oriented Community Secondary Plan - Authorization to Enter into Agreements for Resourcing
brief: Letting staff negotiate a deal where Woodbine Entertainment Group pays for the city staff time needed to finish planning a mixed-use community around the future Woodbine GO station. It goes to Council for a decision. Council decides.

title: 3100 Weston Road - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: Starting the legal process to give heritage protection to the property at 3100 Weston Road, at Weston Road and Sheppard Avenue West. It goes to Council for a decision. If no one objects, the formal by-law can follow. Council decides.

title: Community Benefits Charge: In-Kind Guidelines
brief: Adopting rules for when developers can give community benefits like parks or child care spaces instead of paying the Community Benefits Charge in cash. It goes to Council for approval. Council decides.

title: Thermal Comfort Guidelines: For Large Area Studies, Public Realm Capital Projects, and Large Site Developments - Final Report
topics: heating, ventilation and air conditioning systems
brief: Adopting heat comfort guidelines so big developments, public spaces and large neighbourhood studies are designed with shade and wind protection. It goes to Council for approval. The rules would apply to sites over 5 hectares with buildings over 6 storeys. Council decides.

title: Regent Park Phases 4 and 5 - Building 4A Update
brief: Asking CMHC and the federal and provincial governments to fast-track funding for Building 4A in phases 4 and 5 of the Regent Park rebuild. It goes to Council for a decision. Council decides.

title: Progress on Building More Supportive Homes
brief: Letting city staff apply for federal money from CMHC and other governments to build more supportive homes and rent-geared-to-income housing for people facing homelessness. It goes to Council for a decision. The source text also cites $963 million, $4 billion, $610.8 million, $10,562,651, $10,748,554, $51,857,637, $52,770,331, $62,420,288, $63,518,885, $500,000, $1.5 billion and $60 million. Council decides.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $963 million. Decided by a recorded vote, 17 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: Transit-Oriented Communities Update on Downtown Proposals and Affordable Housing
topics: affordable housing, community & life (sc), urban transit systems
brief: Letting the City Manager finalize a deal for the Queen-Spadina Ontario Line development site, and asking the Province to fix community benefits at 8 percent of each project's value. It goes to Council for a decision. Council decides.

title: Recipient of the 2025 Agnes Macphail Award
brief: Council will vote on confirming Jason Ash as the 2025 Agnes Macphail Award recipient. The award honours an outstanding volunteer in the former East York.

title: Toward Municipal Autonomy and Effective Local Governance
brief: Council would have the City Manager set up an advisory group on municipal autonomy and local government, in response to the province stepping into city decisions.
stake: About advisory committees. Decided by a recorded vote, 18 in favour and 2 against — every member's position is public.

title: Transmittal of a Report from the Board of Toronto Seniors Housing Corporation: Request regarding the composition of the Board
brief: Council, as owner of Toronto Seniors Housing Corporation, would add the City Manager, or a designate, to the board in a non-voting role until the end of 2026.

title: Dovercourt Road - Removal of Accessible Loading Zone
brief: Council will vote on removing a long-gone accessible loading zone on Dovercourt Road from the by-law. Nothing on the street changes.

title: Federation of Canadian Municipalities Report to Council
brief: Councillor Ainslie reports on a December 2024 Ottawa meeting of the Federation of Canadian Municipalities board, covering advocacy ahead of the federal election. Council just receives it.

title: Reducing Stormwater Runoff and Mitigating Basement Flooding
brief: Council would have staff report back on new and bigger basement-flooding subsidies, including home stormwater checks and higher subsidies for backwater valves and sump pumps.

title: Advancing the Waterfront East Light Rail Transit
brief: Council would have staff build a phasing and cost plan for the Waterfront East light rail, and approve advancing design of the Queens Quay East extension between Parliament and Cherry Streets.

title: Renewing the City's Partnership with Toronto Global
brief: Council would keep funding Toronto Global, the regional investment-attraction group, with $7.2 million over three years from April 2025 to March 2028, and at least three city members on its board. The report notes about $3.8 billion in attracted investment and cites annual figures of $2.3 million, $2.4 million and $2.5 million.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $3.8 billion.

title: Advancing Eglinton East Light Rail Transit
brief: Council would approve the early design for the Eglinton East light rail in Scarborough and the Kennedy Station option, and keep studying three maintenance yard sites and report back in early 2026.

title: Good Roads November Advocacy and Board Meeting
brief: Councillor Ainslie reports on representing Toronto at Good Roads advocacy days and board meetings in November 2024, including a proposed five-year, $168 million program for rural road funding. Council just receives it.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $168 million.

title: Moss Park Arena - Governance and Operational Transition Plan
brief: Moss Park Arena's management would move from a community board to city-run by the end of 2025, with ideas to improve fair community access. Council would keep the private attachment private. Running the arena would cost about $1 million a year ($0.3 million after $0.7 million in revenue from rentals and fees).
stake: About arenas. Decided by a recorded vote, 13 in favour and 5 against — every member's position is public.

title: 705 Progress Avenue - City-initiated Development Master Plan and Planning Approval Process
brief: Council would approve a city-led development master plan for the 10.9-acre site at 705 Progress Avenue, owned with the school board, delivered with CreateTO and the Toronto Lands Corporation.

title: ReNew Golden Mile Environmental Assessment:   Final Report
brief: Council would approve the preferred layouts for five new and changed streets in the Golden Mile area, and let staff finish the study report and issue the completion notice.
stake: About assessment. Decided by a recorded vote, 17 in favour and 3 against — every member's position is public.

title: Advancing Truth, Reconciliation and Justice: Supporting 2-Spirited People of the 1st Nations' Development of a 2SLGBTQIA+ Indigenous Emergency Shelter at 996 Woodbine Avenue
brief: Council would sell part of city land at 996 Woodbine Avenue for $2.00 to 2-Spirited People of the 1st Nations, so it can build an 11-bed emergency shelter for 2SLGBTQIA+ Indigenous people.

title: Old City Hall - Future Uses Analysis
brief: Council would have staff and CreateTO rethink future uses for Old City Hall, the historic Bay and Queen landmark, and report back by spring 2026. The report cites a $225 million figure.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $225 million.

brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about a proposed 59-storey, 480-unit tower at 86 Lombard Street, including changes to a heritage building. The legal strategy is confidential.

brief: A councillor wants Council to approve changes to parking meter rules for new paid parking hours on Avenue Road, reverting weekday hours to end at 9:00 p.m., and let the City Solicitor bring in the needed by-laws.

brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on the tribunal case about the Ookwemin Minising (Villiers Island) revitalization in the Port Lands. The legal strategy is confidential.

brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal case about a proposed 17-storey building with 144 homes at 1930-1938 Bloor Street West. The legal strategy is confidential.

brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a development-charges complaint for 5207 Dundas Street West. Details are legally confidential.

brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on an appeal hearing about a proposed vehicle dealership at 1040 Martin Grove Road. The legal strategy is confidential.

brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal hearing about 40-60 St. Lawrence Avenue in Etobicoke. The legal strategy is confidential.

brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on a tribunal hearing about Mississauga's Official Plan Amendment 182 on employment areas. The legal strategy is confidential.

brief: The City Solicitor asks council for private directions on the tribunal case about zoning changes for 86, 100-108 Lombard Street and 103 Richmond Street East. The legal strategy is confidential.

title: Authorization to Enter into Agreements to Deliver a Successful FIFA World Cup 2026
brief: Council would let the City Manager and the World Cup director sign deals with FIFA's official vendors, as long as they meet host city rules and stay within the approved buying plan.

title: Toronto Public Library Transfer to City of Toronto of 0.40 Metre Widening - 575 Van Horne Avenue (Pleasant View Branch) - by Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
brief: A councillor wants Council to approve moving a tiny 0.4-metre strip of land at the Pleasant View library branch, 575 Van Horne Avenue, from the Library Board to the City for site plan rules.

title: Accepting a Donation from Public Services and Procurement Canada to the City of Toronto - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
brief: A councillor wants Council to accept a donation of mobile hospital units worth $6,101,373 from the federal government to help Toronto Fire Services respond to emergencies. The donation tops the $50,000 threshold needing Council approval; the donor set a March 31, 2025 deadline.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $6,101,373.

title: Business Improvement Areas (BIAs) - 2025 Operating Budgets - Report 1

title: Approval of Property Tax Exemptions for new Affordable Rental Homes at 253 Markham Road - Building A - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
brief: A councillor wants Council to approve property tax breaks for the affordable rental and rent-controlled homes at 253 Markham Road Building A, built by the Cedars Non-Profit Housing Co-operative. The project would create 49 affordable and 196 rent-controlled homes. The tax break is worth about $10.25 million over 50 years: $7.95 million in city taxes, $2.19 million in education taxes, and $110,000 in the building levy.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $7,946,724.

brief: Adding 84 Maitland Street to the city's Heritage Register. It goes to the board for a decision. Listing marks it as historic and requires notice before demolition.

title: 94 Cortleigh Boulevard - Alterations to and Demolition of Heritage Attributes of a Designated Heritage Property Under Sections 33 and 34 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: The owner of 94 Cortleigh Boulevard wants to alter a protected heritage house and add a one-storey rear addition. The board is asked to recommend that council approve the work.

title: 29, 31, and 33 Sussex Avenue - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: The board votes on whether to recommend starting heritage protection for 29, 31 and 33 Sussex Avenue. Starting designation would limit future demolition and changes to the properties.

title: 1778, 1908, 1914, 1920, and 1926 Bloor Street West - Inclusion on the Heritage Register
brief: Adding 1778, 1908, 1914, 1920 and 1926 Bloor Street West to the city's Heritage Register. It goes to the board for a decision. Listing requires notice before any demolition.

title: Designation of the Kensington Market Heritage Conservation District under Part V of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage conservation districts, heritage preservation, heritage properties
brief: Recommending making Kensington Market a Heritage Conservation District. It goes to the board for a decision. That would set rules for how buildings in the area can be altered or torn down.

title: 522 University Avenue - Alterations to and Demolition of Heritage Attributes at a Designated Property under Sections 33 and 34 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
brief: The owner of 522 University Avenue wants to alter and partly demolish a protected heritage property as part of redeveloping the site. The board is asked to recommend that council approve the work and a heritage protection agreement.

title: 508 and 510 Church Street - Alterations to Heritage Properties and Authority to Amend a Heritage Easement Agreement
brief: The owners of 508 and 510 Church Street (the Crews and Tangos building) want to alter the protected heritage buildings as part of developing the site. The board is asked to recommend that council approve the alterations.

title: 3100 Weston Road - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties
brief: Recommending that council start the legal process to make 3100 Weston Road a protected heritage property. It goes to the board for a decision. This would limit future demolition and changes.

title: Award of Doc4527040342 to Midome Construction Services Ltd. for Watermain Replacement, Sewer Replacement, Laneway Reconstruction and Neighbourhood Improvements on Various Roads for Engineering and Construction Services
topics: road construction, sewer and water infrastructure
brief: A $18,088,400 contract with Midome Construction Services for replacing water pipes and sewers and rebuilding laneways in North York and Toronto-East York, January 2025 to August 2027 ($20,439,892 including HST; $18,406,756 net of HST recoveries), is up for approval by the city's contract panel. Bids: $16,444,000.00, $16,490,860.00, $16,660,000.00, $16,865,100.00 and $20,382,130.00.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $16,444,000.00.

title: Award of the nRFP0009 to Skidata, Inc. for the Provision of Turnstiles for the World Cup Hosting 2026 Secretariat
brief: A $ 571,467 contract with Skidata, Inc. for temporary turnstiles and handheld ticket scanners for the Toronto stadium during FIFA World Cup 2026, through September 2026 ($ 645,758 including HST; $ 581,524 net of HST recoveries) is up for approval by the city's contract panel.
